dossier.claim: Several passages change how Shirou understands and inherits the hero ideal: explicit obligation becomes aspiration, striving becomes capability, and criticism of rescue or personal motives takes a different logical form. A separate subject error removes his reflection on following Kiritsugu as an adopted son.
dossier.sourcePattern: The two Fate day-one passages make the ideal binding through 'must not break' and 'must become.' The day-seven recollection distinguishes trying to realize an impossible ideal from achieving it, while Archer's warning limits rescue to survivors. In the Rin route, the hero's disappointing conduct adds to Shirou's grievances, and Archer calls the ideal untenable. The Sakura-route passages locate distortion in Shirou's own motives, recall his earlier declaration, and identify him as the unrelated child who followed Kiritsugu. The fire recollection also makes saving Shirou a source of relief for Kiritsugu himself.
dossier.englishEffect: The English weakens the two explicit obligations into a continuing goal and a desire, and replaces attempted realization with miracle-working capacity. It reverses survivors from rescue recipients into rescuers, changes an added grievance into a concession, and makes an open condemnation explicitly moral. Elsewhere, personal unease becomes a question about right conduct generally, an earlier declaration becomes present resolve, Kiritsugu's relief becomes gladness, and Shirou's adopted-son reflection is assigned to Illya. These are distinct local changes to motive, agency, and argument; they do not all move his characterization in one direction.
dossier.limits: The English still preserves substantial parts of Shirou's ideal and conduct: Taiga describes his unsolicited help, he objects to human-shaped death despite Rin's reassurance, Archer's drowning imperative remains memorable, and Kirei connects Grail destruction to Shirou's ideals. Nearby passages also preserve an oath, suicidal resolve, and deliberate human sacrifice. The dossier therefore concerns specific altered formulations, not a general loss of altruism, duty, or childhood characterization. It does not establish later plot consequences or treat other characters' accusations and forecasts as objective accounts of Shirou.
dossier.diagnostic: 1,019 findings in this category; 10 cited passages.

findings.description: Shirou’s duty to honor his spoken commitment becomes pride in being a mage.
findings.sourceReading: He has said as a man that he will fight; from here he must proceed without disgracing those words.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s duty to honor his spoken commitment becomes pride in being a mage.

contexts.japanese: その言葉に恥じないよう、胸を張って進む
contexts.english: I'll face this on my pride as a mage.

findings.description: Rin sees Shirou as dangerously straightforward/single-minded; the English calls him narrow-minded.
findings.sourceReading: 一本気 describes his honest, unswervingly direct temperament, which makes strategic dealings with him futile.
findings.explanation: Rin sees Shirou as dangerously straightforward/single-minded; the English calls him narrow-minded.

contexts.japanese: 危なっかしいぐらい一本気
contexts.english: dangerously narrow-minded.

findings.description: Shirou’s deliberately lowered weapon is no longer specified.
findings.sourceReading: 木刀を下げたまま locates the sword lowered as he emerges before fighting to question whether Kuzuki is manipulated.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s deliberately lowered weapon is no longer specified.

contexts.japanese: 木刀を下げたまま
contexts.english: wooden sword in hand.

findings.description: Shirou’s already-determined response becomes something blurted out.
findings.sourceReading: 当然、俺の台詞なんて決まっていた says his reply was of course already settled, presenting taking over the ideal as an inevitable response.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s already-determined response becomes something blurted out.

contexts.japanese: 当然、俺の台詞なんて決まっていた
contexts.english: So I just kind of blurted something out, as if it were a natural thing to say.

findings.description: Kiritsugu smiles before the vow is completed, rather than after hearing the promise.
findings.sourceReading: そう言い切る前に fixes the smile before Shirou finishes; the next sentence says Kiritsugu needs no continuation.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu smiles before the vow is completed, rather than after hearing the promise.

contexts.japanese: そう言い切る前に、父は微笑った
contexts.english: The bold promise made my father smile.

findings.description: Kiritsugu not needing the rest of Shirou’s words becomes his face telling Shirou everything.
findings.sourceReading: 続きなんて聞くまでもない describes the father’s expression as saying he need not hear the continuation.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu not needing the rest of Shirou’s words becomes his face telling Shirou everything.

contexts.japanese: 続きなんて聞くまでもないっていう顔だった
contexts.english: His face said everything I needed to know.

findings.description: Kiritsugu's gratitude remains, but his own relief through saving Shirou becomes simple gladness at the rescue. The change weakens the passage's pairing of rescued child and relieved rescuer.
findings.sourceReading: Being able to save even one person brought Kiritsugu relief described as being saved himself.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu's gratitude remains, but his own relief through saving Shirou becomes simple gladness at the rescue. The change weakens the passage's pairing of rescued child and relieved rescuer.

contexts.japanese: 一人だけでも助けられて救われた
contexts.english: he was glad to have been able to rescue at least one person.

findings.description: Shirou’s admission of eavesdropping becomes merely hearing the news.
findings.sourceReading: 盗み聞き identifies how he obtained information not disclosed to students.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s admission of eavesdropping becomes merely hearing the news.

contexts.japanese: 生徒会室で盗み聞きした
contexts.english: I heard about it in the student council room.

findings.description: Having no room for this distraction becomes saying it is no big deal.
findings.sourceReading: 今の自分にそんな余裕はない judges his current capacity to indulge attraction before putting trust first.
findings.explanation: Having no room for this distraction becomes saying it is no big deal.

contexts.japanese: 今の自分にそんな余裕はない
contexts.english: It's just her clothes. This isn't a big deal.

findings.description: A lack of motivation until now becomes a recent comparative dip.
findings.sourceReading: 今までは本人にやる気がなかっただけ says he had not been motivated before this new training development.
findings.explanation: A lack of motivation until now becomes a recent comparative dip.

contexts.japanese: 今まではね、本人にやる気がなかっただけ
contexts.english: He just hasn't been quite as motivated lately.

findings.description: His worryingly extraordinary archery becomes being merely okay, with a new talent maxim.
findings.sourceReading: The contrast denies sword talent while archery made Taiga wonder whether the child was all right; the source describes unsettling prowess, not newly reaching ordinary competence.
findings.explanation: His worryingly extraordinary archery becomes being merely okay, with a new talent maxim.

contexts.japanese: 弓道はちょっと、この子大丈夫なのかなーって思うぐらいだった
contexts.english: talent isn't everything. Just when I thought he was okay in archery

findings.description: A question already asked becomes a hypothetical question she might ask.
findings.sourceReading: 問われた時 and なかった look back at the second why question and his inability to answer it.
findings.explanation: A question already asked becomes a hypothetical question she might ask.

contexts.japanese: 問われた時、俺には返す答えがなかった
contexts.english: If she asked me why I admired them, I would have nothing to say in response.

findings.description: Unconscious self-imposition of an absolute speech taboo becomes an unspecified obstacle.
findings.sourceReading: He identifies a self that unconsciously binds him under the rule that this answer must never be spoken.
findings.explanation: Unconscious self-imposition of an absolute speech taboo becomes an unspecified obstacle.

contexts.japanese: それは決して口にしてはいけない事なのだと、無意識で縛っている自分がいる
contexts.english: something is keeping me from saying it aloud.

findings.description: Nobody being able to accomplish the ideal becomes nobody going to do it.
findings.sourceReading: 誰も成し得ない states inability to achieve it, preceding his taking up the inherited aspiration.
findings.explanation: Nobody being able to accomplish the ideal becomes nobody going to do it.

contexts.japanese: 誰も成し得ないのなら
contexts.english: if no one's going to

findings.description: Shirou’s reluctance to recognize an enemy becomes preventing Saber’s recognition.
findings.sourceReading: The narrator explains his deliberate withholding: he wants to avoid treating Shinji as an enemy before knowing his intentions.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s reluctance to recognize an enemy becomes preventing Saber’s recognition.

contexts.japanese: 敵と認識する事は避けたかった
contexts.english: I don't want her to consider him an enemy

contexts.japanese: 敵と認識する事は避けたかった
contexts.english: I don't want her to consider him an enemy

contexts.japanese: 敵と認識する事は避けたかった
contexts.english: I don't want her to consider him an enemy

findings.description: Shirou still acknowledges his complaining, but his specific judgment that it was childish becomes a remark about how much he complained.
findings.sourceReading: Prompted by Saber, Shirou reproaches himself for the childishness of his grumbling.
findings.explanation: Shirou still acknowledges his complaining, but his specific judgment that it was childish becomes a remark about how much he complained.

contexts.japanese: 子供っぽかったな、と反省する
contexts.english: I have been complaining a lot.

findings.description: Not liking defeat becomes being a sore loser in Saber’s praise of Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: 負けず嫌い characterizes a desire not to lose; Saber links it positively to unyielding spirit in battle.
findings.explanation: Not liking defeat becomes being a sore loser in Saber’s praise of Shirou.

contexts.japanese: シロウは負けず嫌い
contexts.english: Shirou is a sore loser.

findings.description: The offered seal-bearing flesh becomes the cost of a whole arm.
findings.sourceReading: この程度 refers to Caster’s demand to remove the seal with skin/flesh; the preceding narration expects taking the seal with flesh by one utterance.
findings.explanation: The offered seal-bearing flesh becomes the cost of a whole arm.

contexts.japanese: この程度で藤ねえが助かるなら
contexts.english: at the cost of just one arm

findings.description: Two grounds for choosing to fight become capability implying duty.
findings.sourceReading: He chose to fight because it was something he could do, and because he believed it something he had to do: two parallel grounds.
findings.explanation: Two grounds for choosing to fight become capability implying duty.

contexts.japanese: 自分に出来る事だから、やらなくてはいけない事だと信じたから
contexts.english: I believed that since it was something I could do, it was something I must do.

findings.description: Past protection replaces the strengthened reason to remain responsible.
findings.sourceReading: If this pain means Saber was saving him until now, he is all the more involved: 尚更 refers to his rebuttal that he does have a stake in her fate.
findings.explanation: Past protection replaces the strengthened reason to remain responsible.

contexts.japanese: 今までセイバーによって助けられていたっていうのなら尚更だ
contexts.english: This pain is proof that I've been saved by Saber until now.

findings.description: Belated rage loses its lateness.
findings.sourceReading: 今更 places intolerable anger after he has restrained himself and let her die.
findings.explanation: Belated rage loses its lateness.

contexts.japanese: 今更、耐え切れない怒り
contexts.english: uncontrollable anger

findings.description: Given that he became a Master becomes as long as he became one.
findings.sourceReading: なった以上 supplies the already-established ground for his initial motive.
findings.explanation: Given that he became a Master becomes as long as he became one.

contexts.japanese: マスターになった以上は
contexts.english: as long as I became a Master

findings.description: An immediate retort becomes a whim.
findings.sourceReading: 咄嗟に describes the spur-of-the-moment response under pressure.
findings.explanation: An immediate retort becomes a whim.

contexts.japanese: 咄嗟に言い返しちまった
contexts.english: I said that on a whim

findings.description: Shirou treats the hero's conduct as another reason for outrage. English turns that grievance into an unfinished 'even if' concession.
findings.sourceReading: The final も adds another object of Shirou's inability to forgive: a hero embodying his ideal turns out to be such a man.
findings.explanation: Shirou treats the hero's conduct as another reason for outrage. English turns that grievance into an unfinished 'even if' concession.

contexts.japanese: 理想とも言える英雄が、あんな男だという事も
contexts.english: Even if the hero that saved many people and embodies my ideals is a man like that

findings.description: No reason to fight Kuzuki becomes no reason for Kuzuki to fight.
findings.sourceReading: 葛木と戦う considers the observers’ justification for fighting him.
findings.explanation: No reason to fight Kuzuki becomes no reason for Kuzuki to fight.

contexts.japanese: 葛木と戦う理由など何処にもない
contexts.english: any more reasons for Kuzuki to keep fighting

findings.description: Lack of ethical standing becomes physical powerlessness.
findings.sourceReading: 資格などない concerns his right to object after accepting the lethal contest.
findings.explanation: Lack of ethical standing becomes physical powerlessness.

contexts.japanese: 異を唱える資格などない自分
contexts.english: being utterly powerless to oppose.

findings.description: The floor where Shirou and Saber crossed blades becomes quality time they exchanged.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou stares at the plank floor where, for only a few days, he had truly sparred with Saber.
findings.explanation: The floor where Shirou and Saber crossed blades becomes quality time they exchanged.

contexts.japanese: たった数日、けれど確かにセイバーと打ち合った、板張りの床を見つめていた
contexts.english: It was a short few days, but we've exchanged quality time here... I think this while staring at the wooden floor.

findings.description: A counterfactual lifelong loss of face becomes a belief that he had overslept plus an imagined violent scolding.
findings.sourceReading: Had he carelessly slept too long and been shaken awake by Rin, he would never have been able to hold his head up before her again.
findings.explanation: A counterfactual lifelong loss of face becomes a belief that he had overslept plus an imagined violent scolding.

contexts.japanese: うっかり寝過ごし、遠坂にたたき起こされでもしたら一生頭が上がらなくなってたところだ
contexts.english: I for sure thought I would've overslept. I feel embarassed just thinking how Tohsaka would violently wake me up and give me a scolding.

findings.description: Shirou gripping the chain so he will not let go becomes the chain refusing to release him.
findings.sourceReading: He deliberately reverses his prior resistance, winds the chain deeply, and grips it so the two cannot separate.
findings.explanation: Shirou gripping the chain so he will not let go becomes the chain refusing to release him.

contexts.japanese: 決して離れないよう鎖を掴み
contexts.english: I grab onto the chain so that it won't let me go.

findings.description: Stopping his resistance becomes casually loosening up.
findings.sourceReading: 力を抜く asks whether he should cease exerting force and let the chain pull him so Gilgamesh falls too.
findings.explanation: Stopping his resistance becomes casually loosening up.

contexts.japanese: 力を抜くべきか
contexts.english: should I loosen up?

findings.description: Projection as Shirou's only fighting power becomes merely his primary weapon.
findings.sourceReading: ただ一つ explicitly says Projection is his sole combat asset at this point.
findings.explanation: Projection as Shirou's only fighting power becomes merely his primary weapon.

contexts.japanese: 投影は、自分にとってただ一つの戦力になっている
contexts.english: Projection has become my primary weapon.

findings.description: Shirou’s unfinished request that Lancer go home makes Shirou himself the person going home.
findings.sourceReading: Too exhausted for a long explanation, Shirou begins telling Lancer to go home quietly before Saber interrupts him.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s unfinished request that Lancer go home makes Shirou himself the person going home.

contexts.japanese: 大人しく帰って
contexts.english: I should go home

findings.description: Existential affirmation of people like Shirou becomes Rin being saved by possessing one.
findings.sourceReading: Rin is saved by the thought that Shirou must be as he is and that someone like him is allowed to exist.
findings.explanation: Existential affirmation of people like Shirou becomes Rin being saved by possessing one.

contexts.japanese: ああいうヤツがいてもいいんだって救われてる
contexts.english: I'm saved by having a guy like him.

findings.description: Shirou’s tentative interpretation of his life becomes settled biography.
findings.sourceReading: He thinks that perhaps all his time since Kiritsugu’s words was spent trying to overturn them.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s tentative interpretation of his life becomes settled biography.

contexts.japanese: その言葉を覆す為だけのもの、だったのかもしれない。
contexts.english: my life has just been trying to overturn those words.

findings.description: Refusing to turn his back on Kiritsugu’s final trust becomes not looking away from the moment.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou cannot turn his back on Kiritsugu’s end and what the relieved final words entrusted to him.
findings.explanation: Refusing to turn his back on Kiritsugu’s final trust becomes not looking away from the moment.

contexts.japanese: その最期に、背を向ける事はできない。
contexts.english: I can't look away from his final moment.

findings.description: The unfinished vow loses its self-directed object.
findings.sourceReading: The fragment breaks after “never, to myself alone—,” leaving readers to infer that the self who chose belief must not deny it.
findings.explanation: The unfinished vow loses its self-directed object.

contexts.japanese: 決して、自分にだけは
contexts.english: then I...

findings.description: No mental room to worry about death becomes a judgment that such gloom has no point.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou feels no fear because his recognition of Archer's condition leaves him no余裕—no room or capacity—to concern himself with his own death.
findings.explanation: No mental room to worry about death becomes a judgment that such gloom has no point.

contexts.japanese: 自身の死をどうだのと憂いる余裕などない
contexts.english: There's no longer any point in feeling gloomy about my own death.

findings.description: Becoming a so-called hero of justice becomes always doing what was right.
findings.sourceReading: Archer grants that he became the ideal's 正義の味方, then says the end yielded only regret and death.
findings.explanation: Becoming a so-called hero of justice becomes always doing what was right.

contexts.japanese: 確かにオレは理想通りの正義の味方とやらになったさ。
contexts.english: I did act according to my ideals and always did what was right.

findings.description: People whose side the hero took become people he had already decided to save.
findings.sourceReading: A hero of justice can save only the people whose side he takes; the claim concerns partiality created by siding with one party.
findings.explanation: People whose side the hero took become people he had already decided to save.

contexts.japanese: 正義の味方が助けられるのは、味方をした人間だけ。
contexts.english: A hero of justice can only save the people he's decided to save.

findings.description: Sacrificing one to save more becomes making the minimum sacrifice.
findings.sourceReading: The doctrine declares it right to sacrifice one thing/person in order to rescue a greater number.
findings.explanation: Sacrificing one to save more becomes making the minimum sacrifice.

contexts.japanese: 一つを犠牲にして、より多くのモノを助け出す事こそが正しい
contexts.english: Saving as many people as you can with the minimum sacrifice is the right choice.

findings.description: Archer says Shirou should never have become a hero of justice; English says he should never have tried.
findings.sourceReading: Archer corrects 'I' to 'you' and condemns becoming that role, whose completed outcome he has just described.
findings.explanation: Archer says Shirou should never have become a hero of justice; English says he should never have tried.

contexts.japanese: おまえは、正義の味方になぞなるべきではなかった
contexts.english: you never should have tried to be a hero of justice.

findings.description: A life of repeated strained self-denial and severe distortion becomes mostly pride.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou concedes that his path has likely been a continuous performance of painful endurance and was badly warped.
findings.explanation: A life of repeated strained self-denial and severe distortion becomes mostly pride.

contexts.japanese: それはやせ我慢の連続でひどく歪だったろう。
contexts.english: It probably is mostly pride, like he said.

findings.description: Shirou refusing to retreat for the sake of what he lost becomes refusing despite what he lost.
findings.sourceReading: Precisely because he lost more than he gained, he cannot retreat, including for the sake of the things left behind along the way.
findings.explanation: Shirou refusing to retreat for the sake of what he lost becomes refusing despite what he lost.

contexts.japanese: その、落としてきた物の為にも、衛宮士郎は退けない。
contexts.english: Shirou Emiya won't back down, not even for what he's lost.

findings.description: Facing one another empty-handed becomes an announced bare-handed fight.
findings.sourceReading: They confront one another with no weapons presently in hand; the next line immediately says both are beings who create swords.
findings.explanation: Facing one another empty-handed becomes an announced bare-handed fight.

contexts.japanese: 俺とヤツは徒手空拳のまま対峙する。
contexts.english: We're going to go at it bare-handed.

findings.description: A heart close to breaking but insisting it has not broken becomes a broken heart pretending to be whole.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou's nearly broken heart bluffs that it is not broken yet, allowing the body to demand continued resistance.
findings.explanation: A heart close to breaking but insisting it has not broken becomes a broken heart pretending to be whole.

contexts.japanese: 折れかかった心が、まだ折れていないと強がっている。
contexts.english: I've just been playing tough, pretending that my broken heart is whole.

findings.description: Shirou's promise to inherit his old man's dream becomes a vague question about that dream.
findings.sourceReading: The remembered fragment begins 'Old man, your dream—I will...', the casual sentence that relieved Kiritsugu and converted admiration into obligation.
findings.explanation: Shirou's promise to inherit his old man's dream becomes a vague question about that dream.

contexts.japanese: じいさんの夢は、俺が
contexts.english: Your dream, huh?

findings.description: Kiritsugu dying relieved by Shirou's casual words becomes explicitly entrusting Shirou with his wish.
findings.sourceReading: Kiritsugu heard Shirou's offhand statement, left the word 'relieved,' and died; the burden is the consequence Shirou formed from that response.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu dying relieved by Shirou's casual words becomes explicitly entrusting Shirou with his wish.

contexts.japanese: 自分の何気ない言葉を聞いて、安心したと遺して、俺以上に空っぽだった人は逝った。
contexts.english: A man even emptier than me heard my innocent words, entrusted his wish to me in relief, and passed away.

findings.description: What Kiritsugu wanted to become becomes what he failed to become.
findings.sourceReading: Archer calls Shirou's ideal an imitation of the thing Kiritsugu wanted to be and believed right.
findings.explanation: What Kiritsugu wanted to become becomes what he failed to become.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮切嗣という男がなりたかったモノ
contexts.english: what Kiritsugu failed to become

findings.description: English makes Archer's condemnation explicitly moral, where the Japanese calls the ideal untenable and explains it as a fairy tale.
findings.sourceReading: Archer calls the ideal broken or untenable, then describes its aspirations as a fairy tale.
findings.explanation: English makes Archer's condemnation explicitly moral, where the Japanese calls the ideal untenable and explains it as a fairy tale.

contexts.japanese: その理想は破綻している。
contexts.english: Your ideals are morally bankrupt.

findings.description: Kiritsugu pursuing an impossible ideal becomes Shirou following him because it was impossible.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou recognizes that Kiritsugu continued pursuing the dream precisely despite knowing it could not be realized.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu pursuing an impossible ideal becomes Shirou following him because it was impossible.

contexts.japanese: 叶わない夢、有り得ない理想だからこそ、切嗣は追い続けた。
contexts.english: I followed in Kiritsugu's footsteps because it's a dream that won't come true and an impossible ideal.

findings.description: Memories of people vanishing without reason become memories arriving unbidden.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou recalls the people he could not save and the self that was not saved, seeing those memories disappear causelessly and meaninglessly, and vows against repetition.
findings.explanation: Memories of people vanishing without reason become memories arriving unbidden.

contexts.japanese: いわれもなく無意味に消えていく思い出を見て、二度と、こんな事は繰り返させないと誓った。
contexts.english: The memories come unbidden, and I swore that I'd never let this happen again.

findings.description: Kiritsugu saying the dream cannot come true becomes Shirou promising to make it come true.
findings.sourceReading: The fragment 'It won't come true' introduces Kiritsugu, who saved Shirou as a child and died leaving the dream behind sadly.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu saying the dream cannot come true becomes Shirou promising to make it come true.

contexts.japanese: 叶わないと。
contexts.english: I'll make the dream come true.

findings.description: Shirou being cursed by himself becomes the oath turning out to be a curse.
findings.sourceReading: Even if the world hates him and he curses his own self in this confrontation, he will not relinquish the wish.
findings.explanation: Shirou being cursed by himself becomes the oath turning out to be a curse.

contexts.japanese: 世界中の人間に疎まれても、こうして自分自身に呪われても、それだけは—
contexts.english: Even if the whole world shuns me and the oath turns out to be a curse, I won't give it up.

findings.description: Shirou condemning himself for missing Rin's pain becomes condemning Rin as a fool.
findings.sourceReading: Realizing that Rin also does not want Saber to disappear, Shirou calls himself an idiot for failing to see her distress.
findings.explanation: Shirou condemning himself for missing Rin's pain becomes condemning Rin as a fool.

contexts.japanese: くそ、なんて馬鹿だ。
contexts.english: Damn it. What a fool she is.

findings.description: Shirou cursing a thought he has never had before becomes cursing himself for never considering implications.
findings.sourceReading: He knew he was inexperienced, yet now for the first time he bitterly curses the fact framed by the following question: why he has only this many circuits.
findings.explanation: Shirou cursing a thought he has never had before becomes cursing himself for never considering implications.

contexts.japanese: それでも今まで一度も思わなかった事を、心の底から罵倒した。
contexts.english: But I seriously curse at myself for never really thinking of the implications or how that would affect me.

findings.description: The reaching gesture still recalls the earlier rescue, but the gray sky disappears. The loss is a specific visual connection, not the entire connection to the fire.
findings.sourceReading: The raised arm recreates the remembered scene beneath that day's gray sky.
findings.explanation: The reaching gesture still recalls the earlier rescue, but the gray sky disappears. The loss is a specific visual connection, not the entire connection to the fire.

contexts.japanese: 何かを掴むようにあげられた片腕は、あの日の、灰色の空と同じだった。
contexts.english: I raise my arm to grab on to something...like I did on that fateful day.

findings.description: Shirou’s accusation that dropping the plate proves his guard is down becomes a pun about dropping the ball and being a klutz.
findings.sourceReading: He refuses numbness as an excuse and treats failure from such a small sensory mismatch as evidence of lax attention.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s accusation that dropping the plate proves his guard is down becomes a pun about dropping the ball and being a klutz.

contexts.japanese: この程度の感覚のズレで皿を落とすなんて気が緩んでいる証拠だ。
contexts.english: I'm really dropping the proverbial ball if I'm being a klutz just from this.

findings.description: A moment of calm judgment that Shirou should stop becomes a matter of being honest with himself.
findings.sourceReading: For an instant he rationally concludes that he should stop until the arm heals, then immediately rejects the sensible thought.
findings.explanation: A moment of calm judgment that Shirou should stop becomes a matter of being honest with himself.

contexts.japanese: 一瞬、左腕が治るまでやめるべきだ、と冷静に考えて
contexts.english: If I'm being honest with myself, I should stop until my arm no longer feels this way

findings.description: Shirou’s external-versus-internal failure rule becomes a malformed refusal with the failure itself omitted.
findings.sourceReading: He can only accept failure caused by an outside factor, but refuses to acknowledge failure caused from within himself.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s external-versus-internal failure rule becomes a malformed refusal with the failure itself omitted.

contexts.japanese: 外的要因で失敗するんなら受け入れるしかないが、内的要因で失敗するなんて認められない。
contexts.english: If this were from something else I could maybe excuse it, but I refuse over something coming from me.

findings.description: Shirou’s irritation is rendered with the nonexistent idiom “gets my gall.”
findings.sourceReading: He knows he is half-trained, but hearing Rin say so still irritates him.
findings.explanation: Shirou says Rin’s remark irritates him. “Gets my gall” mixes English expressions for irritation without producing the intended idiom.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂にそう言われるとカチンとくる。
contexts.english: it gets my gall that Tohsaka says so.

findings.description: Shirou’s categorical view that nine is no hour for a girl to be out becomes a narrower rule about being out alone.
findings.sourceReading: He states his protective, old-fashioned judgment without an “alone” condition, then privately treats outdoors after nine as effectively late night for a girl.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s categorical view that nine is no hour for a girl to be out becomes a narrower rule about being out alone.

contexts.japanese: 女の子が夜出歩く時間じゃない
contexts.english: It's getting to the point where girls shouldn't be out and about alone.

findings.description: Taiga says Shirou finally worked up the resolve to invite Rin, but English says he went through trouble.
findings.sourceReading: Her tease frames the invitation as a rare act of determined courage or initiative.
findings.explanation: Taiga says Shirou finally worked up the resolve to invite Rin, but English says he went through trouble.

contexts.japanese: せっかく一念発起して誘ったのに
contexts.english: After going through all that trouble to invite her

findings.description: Shirou’s calm beside Rin becomes calm despite being beside “the girl I admire so much.”
findings.sourceReading: He simply observes that Rin is this close yet he is strangely calm; the passage does not label his feeling as admiration.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s calm beside Rin becomes calm despite being beside “the girl I admire so much.”

contexts.japanese: こんなに近くに遠坂がいるのに、不思議と気持ちは落ち着いている。
contexts.english: The girl I admire so much is so close, yet I'm strangely calm.

findings.description: Rin cooperating because Shirou is interesting becomes cooperating because he is funny.
findings.sourceReading: She finds him an interesting person or case, consistent with curiosity and engagement rather than saying he makes her laugh.
findings.explanation: Rin cooperating because Shirou is interesting becomes cooperating because he is funny.

contexts.japanese: 貴方が面白いからだし
contexts.english: I'm working with you because you're funny.

findings.description: Shirou recognizing his burden narrative as his own assumption becomes claiming general ignorance about such matters.
findings.sourceReading: After Rin explains her chosen path, he explicitly retracts his projection that the Tohsaka lineage must weigh on her as a dark shadow.
findings.explanation: Shirou recognizing his burden narrative as his own assumption becomes claiming general ignorance about such matters.

contexts.japanese: けれどそんなのはこっちの思いこみだ。
contexts.english: But I guess I don't really have a clue about that sort of thing.

findings.description: Rin cornering Shirou and demanding surrender becomes Shirou being about to surrender.
findings.sourceReading: During the school chase she drove him into a corner while telling him to give up, but Rider interrupted before any result.
findings.explanation: Rin cornering Shirou and demanding surrender becomes Shirou being about to surrender.

contexts.japanese: 降参しろと追い詰められた
contexts.english: I was cornered and about to surrender

findings.description: Shirou’s inexplicable guilt under Rin’s silent pressure becomes concluding that her anger “must be bad.”
findings.sourceReading: Although he recalls no act deserving anger, her glare makes him start to feel as though he has done something terribly wrong.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s inexplicable guilt under Rin’s silent pressure becomes concluding that her anger “must be bad.”

contexts.japanese: 怒られる覚えはないんだが、すごく悪いコトをした気になってきた。
contexts.english: I don't know why she's mad, but it must be bad.

findings.description: Kiritsugu being absent-minded and unimpressive becomes being a klutz.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou fondly recalls Kiritsugu as habitually vague and somehow lacking in sharpness or distinction.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu being absent-minded and unimpressive becomes being a klutz.

contexts.japanese: 普段はぼーっとしていて、どうも冴えなかった。
contexts.english: He was often spacey and a klutz.

findings.description: Kiritsugu’s maxim about fully enjoying occasions of enjoyment becomes a general injunction to enjoy life to the fullest.
findings.sourceReading: Kiritsugu would say that when it was time to have fun, one should enjoy it wholeheartedly, and then romp like a child.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu’s maxim about fully enjoying occasions of enjoyment becomes a general injunction to enjoy life to the fullest.

contexts.japanese: 楽しむ時は思いっきり楽しむんだ
contexts.english: you need to enjoy life to its fullest

findings.description: A possibly purely enjoyable five-year period becomes the most enjoyable time in Shirou’s entire life.
findings.sourceReading: Looking back, Shirou thinks those five years may have been a time he could enjoy without admixture or reservation.
findings.explanation: A possibly purely enjoyable five-year period becomes the most enjoyable time in Shirou’s entire life.

contexts.japanese: 自分にとって純粋に楽しい時間だったのかもしれない。
contexts.english: that might've genuinely been the most fun time in my life.

findings.description: Archer’s “the answer is obvious” becomes “it is nothing worth mentioning.”
findings.sourceReading: Asked what he fights for, Archer answers that it is self-evident: he fights solely for himself.
findings.explanation: Archer’s “the answer is obvious” becomes “it is nothing worth mentioning.”

contexts.japanese: 知れた事。私の戦う意義は、ただ己の為のみだ。
contexts.english: It is nothing worth mentioning. The reason I fight is simply for myself.

findings.description: Archer’s distinction between outside rescue and a person being realized through their own will and result is flattened into another statement about saving.
findings.sourceReading: Outside salvation is not true salvation; only the person’s own will and its result can bring that person to fulfillment or realization.
findings.explanation: Archer’s distinction between outside rescue and a person being realized through their own will and result is flattened into another statement about saving.

contexts.japanese: 人を叶えるのは本人の意思と結果だけだ。
contexts.english: The only things that save a person are their own will and results.

findings.description: Shirou’s denial that the rapid turn of events causes his agitation becomes saying disorientation is only one contributing cause.
findings.sourceReading: He explicitly says the pounding heart is not because events have suddenly accelerated; what startles him most is waking with Rin directly before him.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s denial that the rapid turn of events causes his agitation becomes saying disorientation is only one contributing cause.

contexts.japanese: 事態が急展開を迎えているから、って訳じゃない。
contexts.english: This isn't just because I'm disoriented from everything else.

findings.description: Shirou’s declared reason for entering the war is replaced by an assertion that he had no real choice.
findings.sourceReading: Above all, Shirou recalls that he said he would fight precisely because he cannot leave the conflict and its danger alone.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s declared reason for entering the war is replaced by an assertion that he had no real choice.

contexts.japanese: 俺はこの戦いが放っておけないからこそ戦うと口にした。
contexts.english: I said that I would fight. Not that I had any real choice.

findings.description: The other participants’ designs or motives become their expectations.
findings.sourceReading: Whatever intentions bring someone into the war, participation requires displacing rivals to survive.
findings.explanation: The other participants’ designs or motives become their expectations.

contexts.japanese: どのような思惑だろうと
contexts.english: No matter what your expectations are

findings.description: Stopping ruthless contestants even by force becomes doing everything possible to stop them, echoing their unrestricted methods.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou distinguishes his end from winning: he will stop, by force if necessary, anyone trying to win by using any means.
findings.explanation: Stopping ruthless contestants even by force becomes doing everything possible to stop them, echoing their unrestricted methods.

contexts.japanese: どんな手を使っても勝ち残ろうとするヤツを、力ずくでも止める事。
contexts.english: It's to do everything I can to stop those who will try to win by any means necessary.

findings.description: Saber’s presence like pure water becomes like still water.
findings.sourceReading: Her silent, upright presence evokes clean or sacredly pure water, preparing Shirou’s thought that she is holy.
findings.explanation: Saber’s presence like pure water becomes like still water.

contexts.japanese: 清らかな水を思わせる。
contexts.english: like nothing so much as still water.

findings.description: Shirou’s explanation that he alone is getting confused disappears into “something else” and “nothing.”
findings.sourceReading: Reassuring Saber that his body is fine, he tells her he is merely becoming flustered on his own and asks her not to mind it.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s explanation that he alone is getting confused disappears into “something else” and “nothing.”

contexts.japanese: かってに戸惑ってるだけだから、気にしないでくれ
contexts.english: It's something else, really, it's nothing...!

findings.description: The sentence replaces explicit awareness of Saber as a woman with thinking she is real. This repeats the same attraction-related change in another route.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou becomes conscious of Saber as a woman because her ordinary clothes make her presence feel immediate and familiar.
findings.explanation: The sentence replaces explicit awareness of Saber as a woman with thinking she is real. This repeats the same attraction-related change in another route.

contexts.japanese: 否応なしに異性を意識してしまうのだ。
contexts.english: I can't help but actually think she's real now.

findings.description: Saber’s presence like pure water becomes like still water.
findings.sourceReading: Her silent, upright presence evokes clean or sacredly pure water, preparing Shirou’s thought that she is holy.
findings.explanation: Saber’s presence like pure water becomes like still water.

contexts.japanese: 清らかな水を思わせる。
contexts.english: like nothing so much as still water.

findings.description: Shirou’s explanation that he alone is getting confused disappears into “something else” and “nothing.”
findings.sourceReading: Reassuring Saber that his body is fine, he tells her he is merely becoming flustered on his own and asks her not to mind it.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s explanation that he alone is getting confused disappears into “something else” and “nothing.”

contexts.japanese: かってに戸惑ってるだけだから、気にしないでくれ
contexts.english: It's something else, really, it's nothing...!

findings.description: Shirou’s involuntary awareness of Saber as a member of the opposite sex becomes thinking she is real.
findings.sourceReading: Her ordinary, present-day clothing has too much everyday reality, forcing him to register her as a woman and explaining his physical nervousness.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s involuntary awareness of Saber as a member of the opposite sex becomes thinking she is real.

contexts.japanese: 否応なしに異性を意識してしまうのだ。
contexts.english: I can't help but actually think she's real now.

findings.description: Shirou’s claim that helping Saber was the least reciprocity required becomes saying it was nearly all he was capable of doing.
findings.sourceReading: If Saber was putting her body on the line, he had to do at least that much or their relation could not be called cooperation.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s claim that helping Saber was the least reciprocity required becomes saying it was nearly all he was capable of doing.

contexts.japanese: せめてあれぐらいはしないと協力関係だなんて言えない
contexts.english: it's just about all I can do. This wouldn't be a partnership otherwise.

findings.description: The arrow-self already knowing it will hit is replaced by a self moving farther away “with a hit.”
findings.sourceReading: In release, the arrow that is the self departs already knowing it will naturally strike; act and result unify, reducing past and future to a point in residual awareness.
findings.explanation: The arrow-self already knowing it will hit is replaced by a self moving farther away “with a hit.”

contexts.japanese: 離れ行く自身、すでに“中る”事を知り
contexts.english: The self that becomes further away with a hit

findings.description: Shirou’s exasperation at Saber screening everyone becomes tiredness.
findings.sourceReading: He is slightly dumbfounded or exasperated that she evaluates every person as a possible Master.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s exasperation at Saber screening everyone becomes tiredness.

contexts.japanese: 少し呆れた。
contexts.english: I'm a bit tired.

findings.description: Kiritsugu having plain or modest hobbies becomes Kiritsugu himself being dull.
findings.sourceReading: Taiga calls taking a walk an eccentric choice, says Kiritsugu also had unflashy tastes, and asks whether Shirou shares that trait.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu having plain or modest hobbies becomes Kiritsugu himself being dull.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣さんも地味な趣味してたけど
contexts.english: Kiritsugu was also kinda dull

findings.description: The explicit difficulty of sustained practice becomes a measure of duration. This passage concerns Shirou's training and does not support the proposed Ayako dossier.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou describes the demanding task of sustaining accuracy and penetration over time.
findings.explanation: The explicit difficulty of sustained practice becomes a measure of duration. This passage concerns Shirou's training and does not support the proposed Ayako dossier.

contexts.japanese: 中貫の力を長く維持する厳しさ
contexts.english: how long one can maintain the accuracy and piercing strength.

findings.description: Killing an enemy by some means other than a sword becomes merely beating them another way.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou realizes that an opponent unbeatable by sword can have their life ended by another method.
findings.explanation: Killing an enemy by some means other than a sword becomes merely beating them another way.

contexts.japanese: 剣以外で敵の息の根を絶つ
contexts.english: beat them some other way.

findings.description: Shirou’s recognition that he cannot survive both uninjured and inactive loses the inevitability of being hurt.
findings.sourceReading: He knows participation has passed the point of retreat and that neither pristine safety nor total inaction is compatible with survival.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s recognition that he cannot survive both uninjured and inactive loses the inevitability of being hurt.

contexts.japanese: 無傷で、何もしないままじゃ生き残れない
contexts.english: I won't make it out alive if I just sit and do nothing.

findings.description: Shirou’s inability to fight for himself becomes inability to fight only for himself.
findings.sourceReading: He says he cannot perform the act of fighting on his own behalf, but fighting for Saber feels right.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s inability to fight for himself becomes inability to fight only for himself.

contexts.japanese: 俺は自分の為に戦う、なんてのは出来ない。
contexts.english: I can't just fight for myself.

findings.description: The third element of the archery maxim loses the rigor required to sustain the first two and becomes duration itself.
findings.sourceReading: 久 is described as the demanding discipline of maintaining accuracy and penetrating force over a long time.
findings.explanation: The third element of the archery maxim loses the rigor required to sustain the first two and becomes duration itself.

contexts.japanese: 中貫の力を長く維持する厳しさ
contexts.english: persistence is how long one can maintain the accuracy and piercing strength.

findings.description: Repeating the successful Strengthening loses Shirou’s goal of making the sensation securely his own.
findings.sourceReading: Before the sensation fades, he must repeat the exercise until he has reliably internalized it; failing to capitalize on the rare success would be wasteful.
findings.explanation: Repeating the successful Strengthening loses Shirou’s goal of making the sensation securely his own.

contexts.japanese: 繰り返して、確実にモノにしなければ勿体ない
contexts.english: I need to repeat it so that I don't forget the sensation, or else it would be a waste.

findings.description: Shirou protecting Sakura from everything she will be called to account for becomes protecting her from things people will “ask” her.
findings.sourceReading: He vows to shield her from every accusation, judgment, or consequence that will confront her.
findings.explanation: Shirou protecting Sakura from everything she will be called to account for becomes protecting her from things people will “ask” her.

contexts.japanese: これから桜に問われる全てのコトから桜を守る
contexts.english: I'll protect you from everything people will ask you.

findings.description: Shirou reproaches his failure to listen as a failure in what he is saying.
findings.sourceReading: The recalled invitation makes him ask what he had been listening to: he failed to register Sakura’s earlier request.
findings.explanation: Shirou reproaches his failure to listen as a failure in what he is saying.

contexts.japanese: なにを聞いてたんだ俺はっ
contexts.english: What the hell am I saying!?

findings.description: Reciprocal obligation becomes etiquette.
findings.sourceReading: 義理堅い describes Shirou’s determination to repay unsolicited but useful information.
findings.explanation: Reciprocal obligation becomes etiquette.

contexts.japanese: 相変わらず義理堅い
contexts.english: ever a stickler for etiquette

findings.description: The knightly resolve to protect Illya becomes generic service.
findings.sourceReading: As her knight he must do his utmost to protect her.
findings.explanation: The knightly resolve to protect Illya becomes generic service.

contexts.japanese: 精一杯彼女を守らないといけない
contexts.english: serve Illya the best I can, as her knight.

findings.description: Shirou's description of himself as the unrelated child who became Kiritsugu's son is reassigned to Illya. His reflection on following his adoptive father is lost.
findings.sourceReading: The child is Shirou: originally unrelated to Kiritsugu, he followed his example as his son.
findings.explanation: Shirou's description of himself as the unrelated child who became Kiritsugu's son is reassigned to Illya. His reflection on following his adoptive father is lost.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣の息子として、その背中を追い続けた無縁の子供
contexts.english: From the perspective of Kiritsugu's son, she's a child who's been chasing after a man who has nothing to do with her.

findings.description: The observed interval begins with jumping into the thing instead of pushing Rin away.
findings.sourceReading: Rin measures less than ten seconds from his rescue shove.
findings.explanation: The observed interval begins with jumping into the thing instead of pushing Rin away.

contexts.japanese: 貴方がわたしを突き飛ばしてから今まで
contexts.english: since you jumped into that thing.

findings.description: Shirou sacrificing Saber and refusing further sacrifice become losing her and refusing more loss.
findings.sourceReading: 犠牲にした assigns his decision responsibility; the repeated sacrifice language motivates fighting alone.
findings.explanation: Shirou sacrificing Saber and refusing further sacrifice become losing her and refusing more loss.

contexts.japanese: セイバーを犠牲にした
contexts.english: I lost Saber in my fight to put a stop to all that.

findings.description: The fantasy of events having been different without Zouken becomes a future remedy, followed by asking what Shirou can do.
findings.sourceReading: His earlier normal-life counterfactual ends if Zouken had not been there; he then challenges what would really have been different without him.
findings.explanation: The fantasy of events having been different without Zouken becomes a future remedy, followed by asking what Shirou can do.

contexts.japanese: あいつさえいなければ、こんな事には
contexts.english: If I can just get rid of him, then all this will...!

contexts.japanese: あいつさえいなければ、何が、どうなったって言うんだ
contexts.english: What can I even do about it?

findings.description: Sole responsibility for his own failure becomes being the sole person who failed to notice.
findings.sourceReading: 俺だけの落ち度 isolates his blame for not noticing, irrespective of Zouken’s crimes.
findings.explanation: Sole responsibility for his own failure becomes being the sole person who failed to notice.

contexts.japanese: 気付かなかったのは俺だけの落ち度だ
contexts.english: I was the only person who failed to notice any of it.

findings.description: Saving others remains his purpose, but the English shifts from what has allowed him to keep living to how he has chosen to live. This softens the personal dependence expressed at this decision.
findings.sourceReading: The commitment to save people from arbitrary calamity has enabled or justified his continuing to live.
findings.explanation: Saving others remains his purpose, but the English shifts from what has allowed him to keep living to how he has chosen to live. This softens the personal dependence expressed at this decision.

contexts.japanese: 人々を救うからと、こうして生きていられた
contexts.english: lived the way I do:

findings.description: Shirou driving Illya away for his own relief becomes Illya trying to make him feel better.
findings.sourceReading: 自分が楽になりたくて describes the selfish motive he condemns in himself.
findings.explanation: Shirou driving Illya away for his own relief becomes Illya trying to make him feel better.

contexts.japanese: 自分が楽になりたくてイリヤを追い払っている
contexts.english: Illya's just trying to make me feel better, but I'm pushing her away.

findings.description: Being emotionally shaken becomes having doubts.
findings.sourceReading: 動揺 is disturbance from the report; he explicitly has no indecision and has resolved to stand by Sakura.
findings.explanation: Being emotionally shaken becomes having doubts.

contexts.japanese: 動揺しなかったと言えば嘘になる
contexts.english: I'd be lying if I said I didn't have doubts.

findings.description: Responsibility for the justice-hero oath becomes merely having sworn to do right.
findings.sourceReading: 責任 names the responsibility now paid for through the sacrifice, not another bare assertion of the oath.
findings.explanation: Responsibility for the justice-hero oath becomes merely having sworn to do right.

contexts.japanese: 正義の味方になると誓った責任
contexts.english: I've sworn to do the right thing.

findings.description: Shirou excluding death-as-salvation from his agreement becomes denying that Rin says it.
findings.sourceReading: 死が救いになる、という事ではなく limits Shirou's own assessment: correct in saving lives, not in death being salvation.
findings.explanation: Shirou excluding death-as-salvation from his agreement becomes denying that Rin says it.

contexts.japanese: 死が救いになる、という事ではなく
contexts.english: She isn't saying that death would save Sakura

findings.description: Long denial with hidden acceptance becomes habitual acceptance with hidden denial.
findings.sourceReading: ずっと否定してきて followed by 心の奥で受け入れていた distinguishes outward rejection from inward acceptance.
findings.explanation: Long denial with hidden acceptance becomes habitual acceptance with hidden denial.

contexts.japanese: ずっと否定してきて、心の奥で、受け入れていた
contexts.english: I've always accepted, but always wanted to deny deep down.

findings.description: Deferring thought about consequences becomes promising to find a way.
findings.sourceReading: その結果がどうなるかは、これから考える leaves consequences unresolved after admitting he cannot save everyone.
findings.explanation: Deferring thought about consequences becomes promising to find a way.

contexts.japanese: その結果がどうなるかは、これから考える
contexts.english: I'll think of a way.

findings.description: Never having conceived of losing Sakura becomes unable to bear thinking of it.
findings.sourceReading: 失うことさえ、思いつかなかった says loss had not occurred to him, a retrospective blind spot.
findings.explanation: Never having conceived of losing Sakura becomes unable to bear thinking of it.

contexts.japanese: 失うことさえ、思いつかなかった
contexts.english: Who I can't bear the thought of losing.

findings.description: Disclosure being the right outcome becomes being fine with the preceding unrealized separation.
findings.sourceReading: これで良かった says the present revelation was good; それだと describes the counterfactual continued suffering had she stayed undiscovered.
findings.explanation: Disclosure being the right outcome becomes being fine with the preceding unrealized separation.

contexts.japanese: けど、俺はこれで良かったと信じている
contexts.english: I'm sure I would have been fine with that.

contexts.japanese: それだと、俺はずっと桜を泣かし続けたままだった
contexts.english: so I kept her crying all this time.

findings.description: Forgiving Sakura in her own stead loses the substitution for self-forgiveness.
findings.sourceReading: 桜の代わりに桜を許し続ける directly answers her inability to stop blaming herself.
findings.explanation: Forgiving Sakura in her own stead loses the substitution for self-forgiveness.

contexts.japanese: 桜の代わりに桜を許し続ける
contexts.english: I'll keep forgiving Sakura, even if no one else does.

findings.description: Entering the plan with resolve becomes reassuring warmth.
findings.sourceReading: 覚悟が入った marks resolve replacing impulsive rage under a demanding rescue condition.
findings.explanation: Entering the plan with resolve becomes reassuring warmth.

contexts.japanese: 心に覚悟が入った
contexts.english: The reassurance warms my enraged heart.

findings.description: Deliberately pulling Rider’s arm to reverse positions becomes pulling himself up on her arms.
findings.sourceReading: 彼女の腕を引いて、あからさまに立ち位置を逆にした explicitly locates his tactical action and Shinji’s failure to notice it.
findings.explanation: Shirou pulls Rider’s arm to reverse their positions. The English instead has him pull himself up using her arms; it keeps the reversed positions but changes the movement that produces them.

contexts.japanese: 彼女の腕を引いて、あからさまに立ち位置を逆にした
contexts.english: our positions are reversed since I pulled myself up using Rider's arms?

findings.description: Refusing to presume her pain becomes inability even to imagine it.
findings.sourceReading: おいそれと推測していいものじゃない is an ethical/epistemic limit on claiming easy understanding despite his lesser experience.
findings.explanation: Refusing to presume her pain becomes inability even to imagine it.

contexts.japanese: おいそれと推測していいものじゃない
contexts.english: could never even imagine the depths of her pain.

findings.description: Lacking the mental room to turn becomes not bothering to turn.
findings.sourceReading: 振り向く余裕などない marks his overwhelmed capacity after the accusations.
findings.explanation: Lacking the mental room to turn becomes not bothering to turn.

contexts.japanese: 振り向く余裕などない
contexts.english: I don't bother turning around.

findings.description: The imposed cross-burden becomes the cross God/Christ bore.
findings.sourceReading: 科せられた十字 is the imposed cross under the guilt Shirou has just internalized; no He-bearing clause is supplied.
findings.explanation: The imposed cross-burden becomes the cross God/Christ bore.

contexts.japanese: 科せられた十字
contexts.english: the cross He bore.

findings.description: Shirou appealing to what anyone would normally do becomes only his own prior plan.
findings.sourceReading: 思うだろ、ふつう recruits an ordinary-person norm to deny that his Sakura concern is romantic boasting.
findings.explanation: Shirou appealing to what anyone would normally do becomes only his own prior plan.

contexts.japanese: うちに泊めようって思うだろ、ふつう
contexts.english: I was still going to ask Sakura to stay over tomorrow if she's feeling down.

findings.description: Showing sincerity becomes proving that he keeps his word.
findings.sourceReading: 誠意を見せる motivates offering the whole tea can as good faith; no promise to give this payment has been made.
findings.explanation: Showing sincerity becomes proving that he keeps his word.

contexts.japanese: 誠意を見せる
contexts.english: to prove I'm a man of my word

findings.description: Her being a girl as his reason to give way becomes her being a kid.
findings.sourceReading: 俺は年上 and イリヤは女の子 are separate stated reasons; the second adds gender rather than repeating the age premise.
findings.explanation: Her being a girl as his reason to give way becomes her being a kid.

contexts.japanese: イリヤは女の子な訳だし
contexts.english: Illya's just a kid.

findings.description: An ethical prohibition on deceiving family becomes a preference not to tell untruths.
findings.sourceReading: 偽るような真似はしちゃいけない expresses must not, explaining why he cannot replace withheld truth with a lie.
findings.explanation: An ethical prohibition on deceiving family becomes a preference not to tell untruths.

contexts.japanese: 言葉で偽るような真似はしちゃいけない
contexts.english: I'd rather not tell her anything that's untrue.

findings.description: His unusual stubbornness becomes being red and flustered.
findings.sourceReading: いつもより意地っぱり is the extra stubbornness under his blush that Taiga finds cute and thinks embarrasses Sakura.
findings.explanation: His unusual stubbornness becomes being red and flustered.

contexts.japanese: いつもより意地っぱりで可愛い
contexts.english: kinda cute, getting all red and flustered.

findings.description: Blushing would disqualify him as her senior becomes simply not embarrassing himself.
findings.sourceReading: そういう後輩に照れてたら先輩失格 ties sexual self-consciousness to failure of his senior role; Taiga repeats 失格 and he then invokes responsibility for a friend’s sister.
findings.explanation: Blushing would disqualify him as her senior becomes simply not embarrassing himself.

contexts.japanese: 後輩に照れてたら先輩失格
contexts.english: I wouldn't embarrass myself in front of her like that!

contexts.japanese: 士郎は失格したくないんだ
contexts.english: you don't want to embarrass yourself

findings.description: Far beyond eye candy becomes not eye candy.
findings.sourceReading: 目の毒なんてもんじゃない intensifies a distracting/tempting sight beyond that inadequate expression, not denies visual temptation.
findings.explanation: Far beyond eye candy becomes not eye candy.

contexts.japanese: 目の毒なんてもんじゃない
contexts.english: This isn't eye candy.

findings.description: Shirou sitting on the floor and leaning against the bed becomes entering the bed and lying down.
findings.sourceReading: 床に腰を下ろす followed by 背中はベッドに預ける places him on the floor with his back resting against the bed, physically separated from her.
findings.explanation: Shirou sitting on the floor and leaning against the bed becomes entering the bed and lying down.

contexts.japanese: 床に腰を下ろす
contexts.english: I sit down on the bed.

contexts.japanese: 背中はベッドに預けてしまう
contexts.english: Then, I lie down on my back.

findings.description: If the temple Master caused the comas becomes stopping that Master from causing more comas.
findings.sourceReading: 昏睡事件を起こしているのなら is still conditional, following his explicit uncertainty over Rin’s account.
findings.explanation: If the temple Master caused the comas becomes stopping that Master from causing more comas.

contexts.japanese: 柳洞寺のマスターが昏睡事件を起こしているのなら
contexts.english: stop the Master from putting any more townspeople into comas

findings.description: A blindfold would stop him opening his eyes becomes a claim he never opened them.
findings.sourceReading: 目隠しなら誘惑に負けて目蓋を開けることもない describes a counterfactual benefit of the blindfold he lacked.
findings.explanation: A blindfold would stop him opening his eyes becomes a claim he never opened them.

contexts.japanese: 目隠しなら誘惑に負けて目蓋を開けることもない
contexts.english: Not once did I give into temptation and open them until my work was done.

findings.description: Shirou rejecting apparent appeasement becomes Saber not being in the mood.
findings.sourceReading: ご機嫌をうかがっているようで嫌 locates reluctance in his own dislike of seeming to curry favor while they are fighting.
findings.explanation: Shirou rejecting apparent appeasement becomes Saber not being in the mood.

contexts.japanese: ご機嫌をうかがっているようで嫌
contexts.english: she didn't look like she was in the mood

findings.description: He has only compromised a little becomes merely feeling like potato salad.
findings.sourceReading: 負けたワケではない ... 少し日和っただけ is a comic hairsplitting admission of accommodation after declaring he will not appease Saber.
findings.explanation: He has only compromised a little becomes merely feeling like potato salad.

contexts.japanese: 単に少し日和っただけ
contexts.english: I just felt like making potato salad.

findings.description: Pushing despite poor health becomes pushing because of poor health.
findings.sourceReading: 体調が悪いっていうのに無理しようとした marks the illness as the reason not to exert himself, overridden by Sakura.
findings.explanation: Pushing despite poor health becomes pushing because of poor health.

contexts.japanese: 体調が悪いっていうのに無理しようとした
contexts.english: pushing yourself because you haven't been feeling well.

findings.description: A girl busying herself solely with chores becomes making her do chores.
findings.sourceReading: 年頃の女の子が家事手伝いばかりに奔走 is the girl’s ongoing self-driven activity that Shirou considers unhealthy.
findings.explanation: A girl busying herself solely with chores becomes making her do chores.

contexts.japanese: 女の子が家事手伝いばかりに奔走
contexts.english: make a girl her age constantly do house chores.

contexts.japanese: 女の子が家事手伝いばかりに奔走
contexts.english: make a girl her age constantly do house chores.

findings.description: Loss of awareness becomes inability to remember anything.
findings.sourceReading: 前後不覚 describes losing awareness/composure; the next row expressly says he remembers Saber supporting him and putting him to bed.
findings.explanation: Loss of awareness becomes inability to remember anything.

contexts.japanese: 前後不覚になるなんて
contexts.english: if I can't remember anything that happened.

findings.description: Vaguely overhearing Sakura and Saber becomes remembering participating in their talk.
findings.sourceReading: Sakura and Saber were talking; Shirou thinks he heard them unclearly and asks what happened.
findings.explanation: Vaguely overhearing Sakura and Saber becomes remembering participating in their talk.

contexts.japanese: 桜とセイバーがなんか話してた気がする。……よく聞こえなかったんだけど、そん時なにかあったのか？
contexts.english: I remember talking with you and Saber about something.

findings.description: Shirou and Sakura caring for each other becomes both caring for Saber.
findings.sourceReading: 二人とも互いを気遣って means the two act out of consideration for one another.
findings.explanation: Shirou and Sakura caring for each other becomes both caring for Saber.

contexts.japanese: 二人とも互いを気遣って
contexts.english: your mutual way of being considerate to me.

findings.description: Normalizing longstanding hazards becomes claiming unprecedented current safety.
findings.sourceReading: He calls those incidents ordinary and argues that, if they mean danger, he has been in danger all along.
findings.explanation: Normalizing longstanding hazards becomes claiming unprecedented current safety.

contexts.japanese: そんなの全然普通じゃんか。それで危ないってんなら、今までずっと危なかったよ俺は
contexts.english: Well, I'm doing just fine. If anything, I'm safer now then I've ever been before.

findings.description: Rin beginning to amuse herself by teasing him becomes having come solely to tease him.
findings.sourceReading: からかって遊ぶようになってき identifies a developing pattern after their actual strategy discussion; Shirou himself brought her to the roof.
findings.explanation: Rin beginning to amuse herself by teasing him becomes having come solely to tease him.

contexts.japanese: 俺をからかって遊ぶようになってきやがった
contexts.english: She only came here to push my buttons.

findings.description: The indispensable disposition in which Shirou is unsurpassed becomes refusing to let himself lose.
findings.sourceReading: それだけは他の誰にも負けない identifies the one quality where he is unsurpassed; Rin subsequently defines it as other-directed striving and self-hatred.
findings.explanation: The indispensable disposition in which Shirou is unsurpassed becomes refusing to let himself lose.

contexts.japanese: それだけは他の誰にも負けない、彼が一番たり得るところよ
contexts.english: he won't let himself lose to anyone.

findings.description: Two possible reasons for watching Sakura collapse into unconscious watching.
findings.sourceReading: The narrator wonders whether he has nothing else to do or his eyes follow her unconsciously.
findings.explanation: Two possible reasons for watching Sakura collapse into unconscious watching.

contexts.japanese: 他にやる事がなかったからか、それとも、無意識に目が追ってしまうのか
contexts.english: I unconsciously find myself watching her.

findings.description: Knowing the war presupposed death before the contract becomes knowing from the contract onward.
findings.sourceReading: 契約する前から思い知らされていた places recognition before he takes her hand.
findings.explanation: Knowing the war presupposed death before the contract becomes knowing from the contract onward.

contexts.japanese: 彼女と契約する前から
contexts.english: from the moment we made our pact

findings.description: The necessity to carry duty through becomes merely still having something to do.
findings.sourceReading: やるべき事を、やり通さなければ insists on finishing what he must do despite loss of his means.
findings.explanation: The necessity to carry duty through becomes merely still having something to do.

contexts.japanese: やるべき事を、やり通さなければ
contexts.english: But I still have something to do.

findings.description: The last long touch loses its sustained duration.
findings.sourceReading: 最後に長く modifies the final movement of his finger over the blood before its release without bow or thanks.
findings.explanation: The last long touch loses its sustained duration.

contexts.japanese: 最後に長く、血の跡に指を這わせた
contexts.english: I touch the blood stain one last time.

findings.description: Having never said he would withdraw becomes having said nothing about fighting or forfeiting.
findings.sourceReading: まだ戦うつもりも何も dismisses the question of still fighting because he never said he was quitting.
findings.explanation: Having never said he would withdraw becomes having said nothing about fighting or forfeiting.

contexts.japanese: まだ戦うつもりも何も、降りるなんて言った覚えはないからだ
contexts.english: I still haven't said anything about fighting or forfeiting the war.

findings.description: Rider's earnest request to repeat the thanks becomes Shirou's thought that she will hear him. The change removes his observation of how seriously she receives the unexpected gratitude.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou remarks that Rider is earnestly asking what he just said, adding to his embarrassment about thanking her.
findings.explanation: Rider's earnest request to repeat the thanks becomes Shirou's thought that she will hear him. The change removes his observation of how seriously she receives the unexpected gratitude.

contexts.japanese: まじめに聞いてくるし
contexts.english: Because she'll hear me, after all.

findings.description: An abrupt departure story becomes an urgent event forcing her to leave.
findings.sourceReading: 急な話だけど comments on the sudden news before saying she went home and will not return.
findings.explanation: An abrupt departure story becomes an urgent event forcing her to leave.

contexts.japanese: 急な話だけど、あいつは帰った
contexts.english: Something urgent came up, so she had to leave.

findings.description: How he ought to respond now becomes how he repaid her before.
findings.sourceReading: 何をもって応えるべきなのか asks what he should offer in response to the six days she was his sword.
findings.explanation: How he ought to respond now becomes how he repaid her before.

contexts.japanese: 俺は何をもって応えるべきなのか
contexts.english: how did I repay her?

findings.description: More absence from tomorrow loses the increase.
findings.sourceReading: もっと家を留守にする forecasts greater absence while explicitly allowing Sakura to keep using the house.
findings.explanation: More absence from tomorrow loses the increase.

contexts.japanese: 明日からもっと家を留守にするだろう
contexts.english: I'm probably going to be out of the house from tomorrow

findings.description: English restates Shirou's resolve but omits his reminder that he had already declared this commitment.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou invokes his earlier declaration that he would become a hero of justice.
findings.explanation: English restates Shirou's resolve but omits his reminder that he had already declared this commitment.

contexts.japanese: 正義の味方になるって言ったんだ
contexts.english: I'm going to be a man who does what's right.

findings.description: Having reclaimed something becomes having taken something from Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: 奪い返した is taking back, with no expressed object or source-person in this sentence.
findings.explanation: Having reclaimed something becomes having taken something from Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 奪い返したという事実
contexts.english: What she took from him.

findings.description: Wanting pleasure even at the expense of protection becomes wanting to waste his protection.
findings.sourceReading: それを無駄にしてもよろこびを得たい makes pleasure the goal, even if his protective efforts are made futile.
findings.explanation: Wanting pleasure even at the expense of protection becomes wanting to waste his protection.

contexts.japanese: それを無駄にしてもよろこびを得たい
contexts.english: wanting to waste his efforts to protect her.

findings.description: If he gets injuries preventing walking becomes I will hurt you so you cannot walk.
findings.sourceReading: 歩けなくなるぐらいの怪我をしちゃえば imagines him being disabled as the solution but does not explicitly name who inflicts the injury.
findings.explanation: If he gets injuries preventing walking becomes I will hurt you so you cannot walk.

contexts.japanese: 歩けなくなるぐらいの怪我をしちゃえば
contexts.english: If I hurt you so you can't walk anymore

findings.description: A joke about urgent laundry protecting Shirou's household standing becomes a joke about purification and choosing silence. The feared social consequence changes.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou imagines urgently bleaching and spin-drying the evidence to avoid losing his standing to speak in the household.
findings.explanation: A joke about urgent laundry protecting Shirou's household standing becomes a joke about purification and choosing silence. The feared social consequence changes.

contexts.japanese: すみやかに漂白・脱水しなくては今後の発言権に支障をきたす
contexts.english: My first priority is to purify myself and then exercise my right to silence.

findings.description: This night’s lack of a strange event with Rin becomes never having done anything that crazy with her.
findings.sourceReading: 遠坂とおかしなコトになったワケでもない denies the recent dream’s events alongside not visiting school while asleep.
findings.explanation: This night’s lack of a strange event with Rin becomes never having done anything that crazy with her.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂とおかしなコトになったワケでもない
contexts.english: I've never done anything that crazy with Tohsaka.

findings.description: Doing something that could transmit the cold becomes deliberately trying to transfer it.
findings.sourceReading: 風邪が移るような真似しちゃったの teases about intimate conduct whose consequence could be catching the cold.
findings.explanation: Doing something that could transmit the cold becomes deliberately trying to transfer it.

contexts.japanese: 桜ちゃんの風邪が移るような真似しちゃったの
contexts.english: did you try to transfer Sakura's cold over?

findings.description: Lack of romantic initiative or gumption becomes lack of cleverness.
findings.sourceReading: そんな甲斐性ない mocks Shirou’s capacity to act on the intimate possibility, not his intelligence.
findings.explanation: Lack of romantic initiative or gumption becomes lack of cleverness.

contexts.japanese: 士郎にはそんな甲斐性ない
contexts.english: You aren't clever enough for that.

findings.description: The demand to recover by dinner loses the deadline.
findings.sourceReading: それまでに体を治して refers to the dinner she will bring; the next narrator calls this an impossible demand.
findings.explanation: The demand to recover by dinner loses the deadline.

contexts.japanese: それまでに体を治しておくこと
contexts.english: you need to let yourself rest and recover.

findings.description: Nursing even against her dislike becomes nursing despite awkward feelings.
findings.sourceReading: どんなに嫌がられても says he would persist even if she did not want the care.
findings.explanation: Nursing even against her dislike becomes nursing despite awkward feelings.

contexts.japanese: どんなに嫌がられても看病する
contexts.english: no matter how awkward it makes you feel.

findings.description: Finding unused rooms already tended becomes us tending them without thinking.
findings.sourceReading: 気がつけば手入れされていて gives Shirou’s discovery of the upkeep that the next paragraph attributes especially to Sakura.
findings.explanation: Finding unused rooms already tended becomes us tending them without thinking.

contexts.japanese: 使わない部屋も気がつけば手入れされていて
contexts.english: we've been tending to the unused rooms without even really thinking about it

findings.description: Trying to hold him with one hand while holding the thermometer in the other becomes a threatening thermometer approaching.
findings.sourceReading: 片手に体温計を持って、片手でこっちの体を押さえにかかる specifies the attempted bodily restraint.
findings.explanation: Trying to hold him with one hand while holding the thermometer in the other becomes a threatening thermometer approaching.

contexts.japanese: 片手に体温計を持って、片手でこっちの体を押さえにかかる
contexts.english: The thermometer inches threateningly towards me, its holder losing her composure.

findings.description: A feared possibility of contract termination becomes a certain result.
findings.sourceReading: 契約解除をしかねない says she might actually terminate it if he explains badly; this is Shirou’s apprehension.
findings.explanation: A feared possibility of contract termination becomes a certain result.

contexts.japanese: 本気で契約解除をしかねない
contexts.english: result in nothing less than Saber calling our contract null and void.

findings.description: The food trio’s mock sacred-treasures elevation becomes a plain fame claim.
findings.sourceReading: 三種の神器 playfully calls the three snacks the three sacred treasures.
findings.explanation: The food trio’s mock sacred-treasures elevation becomes a plain fame claim.

contexts.japanese: 三種の神器を扱うお店だ
contexts.english: They're famed for their taiyaki buns, dorayaki pancakes, and takoyaki octopus bites.

findings.description: Shirou's thought that Sakura is welcome to eat becomes a statement about her appetite, removing his reassurance that she need not hold back.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou thinks Sakura need not hold back: he has no objection to her eating the dorayaki.
findings.explanation: Shirou's thought that Sakura is welcome to eat becomes a statement about her appetite, removing his reassurance that she need not hold back.

contexts.japanese: どら焼きの一つや二つ、いくら食べても構わない
contexts.english: She's always ready for a dorayaki or two.

findings.description: Failure to fulfill a return promise becomes discovery of an already existing lie.
findings.sourceReading: そろそろ戻らないと嘘つきさんになってしまう says not returning soon would make him a liar about the note’s deadline.
findings.explanation: Failure to fulfill a return promise becomes discovery of an already existing lie.

contexts.japanese: そろそろ戻らないと嘘つきさんになってしまう
contexts.english: they'll know I was lying.

findings.description: The interrupted beginning of Illya’s name becomes a cry of pain.
findings.sourceReading: イ— follows her revealed prank and leads into17’s full イリヤ—！ after the intervening lecture.
findings.explanation: The interrupted beginning of Illya’s name becomes a cry of pain.

findings.description: Not listening to nonsense becomes failing to understand a joke.
findings.sourceReading: 戯言はもちろん耳に入ってこない dismisses her haughty lecture while he remains angry.
findings.explanation: Not listening to nonsense becomes failing to understand a joke.

contexts.japanese: そんな戯言はもちろん耳に入ってこない
contexts.english: the joke goes over my head.

findings.description: Shirou glaring at Illya while holding the bag becomes Illya looking at his shopping bag.
findings.sourceReading: スーパーのビニール袋を手に、キッとイリヤを睨みつける has Shirou holding groceries and glaring at her before her curious stare back.
findings.explanation: Shirou glaring at Illya while holding the bag becomes Illya looking at his shopping bag.

contexts.japanese: スーパーのビニール袋を手に、キッとイリヤを睨みつける
contexts.english: Illya shoots a glance at the shopping bag in my hand.

findings.description: His refusal to be defeated easily disappears and the dialogue is left unclosed.
findings.sourceReading: 俺だってマスターだ is followed by そう簡単にやられる訳には— within closed speech.
findings.explanation: His refusal to be defeated easily disappears and the dialogue is left unclosed.

contexts.japanese: そう簡単にやられる訳には—
contexts.english: but I'm a Master, too.

findings.description: Illya being a girl as an additional reason to soften becomes simply her being a kid.
findings.sourceReading: 俺は年上 and イリヤは女の子 supply separate age and gender rationales in Shirou’s thought.
findings.explanation: Illya being a girl as an additional reason to soften becomes simply her being a kid.

contexts.japanese: イリヤは女の子な訳だし
contexts.english: Illya's just a kid.

findings.description: Questioning his own lack of anger becomes knowing better than to say it.
findings.sourceReading: 自分でもどうかと思うけど doubts the appropriateness of his not being angry.
findings.explanation: Questioning his own lack of anger becomes knowing better than to say it.

contexts.japanese: 自分でもどうかと思うけど、怒ってない
contexts.english: I should know better than to say this, but I'm not mad.

findings.description: Having been caught by her becomes having her here.
findings.sourceReading: こうして捕まってしまった以上 makes Shirou the caught party conceding to the chat she wants.
findings.explanation: Having been caught by her becomes having her here.

contexts.japanese: こうして捕まってしまった以上
contexts.english: As long as I've got her here
