contexts.english: But do not be complacent. Magical energy runs through your body even when you aren't using magecraft. It may cause your left arm to react with pain or activation.

findings.description: Complaining as rejection of a life saved becomes disrespecting Archer's sacrifice.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou reasons that because the transplant was the means of keeping him alive, complaining would amount to abandoning the life he was given.
findings.explanation: Complaining as rejection of a life saved becomes disrespecting Archer's sacrifice.

contexts.japanese: それを生かす為の方法がアーチャーの腕の移植だったんだから、文句を言うって事は助かった命を放棄するって事になる。
contexts.english: Archer's arm transplant saved my life, so I would be making light of his sacrifice if I complained.

findings.description: Shirou asks the priest to pray for him; English has Shirou undertake the prayer himself. The wish survives, but the priest-directed banter loses its specific target.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou asks Father Kotomine to pray that there will be no fourth occasion, combining thanks with a pointed request suited to a priest.
findings.explanation: Shirou asks the priest to pray for him; English has Shirou undertake the prayer himself. The wish survives, but the priest-directed banter loses its specific target.

contexts.japanese: ……また世話になった、言峰神父。出来れば四度目がないよう祈っててくれ」
contexts.english: ...You helped me out again, Father Kotomine. I'll pray that it doesn't happen a fourth time."

findings.description: Having no reason to be glared at becomes never remembering Rin glaring like this before.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou cannot think of anything he did to deserve Rin's current glare, but is relieved she is safe.
findings.explanation: Having no reason to be glared at becomes never remembering Rin glaring like this before.

contexts.japanese: ……あんなふうに睨まれる覚えはないが、とりあえず遠坂も無事だったと判ってホッとする。
contexts.english: ...I don't remember her ever glaring at me like this before, but I'm relieved that she's safe.

findings.description: Remaining Masters uniformly lacking Servants and the outcome being decided becomes victory being close because few Servants remain.
findings.sourceReading: Kirei says the surviving Masters are gathered without Servants, so the result is effectively settled.
findings.explanation: Remaining Masters uniformly lacking Servants and the outcome being decided becomes victory being close because few Servants remain.

contexts.japanese: 残されたマスターがこうもそろってサーヴァントがいない状態では、もはや勝敗はついただろう」
contexts.english: Victory is close, with so few Servants remaining, despite this assembly of Masters."

findings.description: The second route to saving Sakura loses the requirement that someone obtain the Grail.
findings.sourceReading: Either Sakura must obtain the Grail, or a person who intends to save her must obtain it.
findings.explanation: The second route to saving Sakura loses the requirement that someone obtain the Grail.

contexts.japanese: 桜を救いたいのなら、それは桜が聖杯を手に入れるか、それとも—桜を助ける気がある人間が聖杯を手に入れるしかない。
contexts.english: If we want to save Sakura, then either Sakura has to win the Holy Grail, or someone willing to help her.

findings.description: A quotation-reporting connective becomes Shirou saying 'Huh.'
findings.sourceReading: The fragment と closes/reports Illya's odd reply before narration comments on it; it is not a spoken reaction.
findings.explanation: A quotation-reporting connective becomes Shirou saying 'Huh.'

contexts.japanese: と。
contexts.english: Huh.

findings.description: Rin's reminder that Illya once nearly killed Shirou disappears.
findings.sourceReading: Rin provocatively says Illya is returning to her castle without gratitude after being saved by Shirou, whom she once nearly killed.
findings.explanation: Rin's reminder that Illya once nearly killed Shirou disappears.

contexts.japanese: 「あーら、やっぱりそうなんだ。一度殺しかけた士郎に助けられたクセに、恩も感じずにお城に戻るワケね。
contexts.english: "Oh wow, really? Shirou saved your life, but you're just gonna run back to the castle without an ounce of gratitude.

findings.description: Shirou being unreliable becomes Illya not wanting to rely on him.
findings.sourceReading: Rin falsely paraphrases Illya as refusing the house because Emiya himself is not dependable, preferring her secure castle.
findings.explanation: Shirou being unreliable becomes Illya not wanting to rely on him.

contexts.japanese: 「言ってるじゃない。衛宮くんの家に行かないのは、衛宮くんが頼りにならないからでしょ？　だから安心できる自分の城に戻るって言ってるんじゃない」
contexts.english: "You're saying it right now. You don't want to go to Emiya's house because you don't want to rely on him, right? You'd feel better back at your own castle."

findings.description: Illya's offer to treat Sakura as human becomes unspecified special treatment. The English retains condescension but removes the precise insult that Sakura turns back on her.
findings.sourceReading: Illya grants Sakura the supposed exception of being treated as human because she knows Shirou.
findings.explanation: Illya's offer to treat Sakura as human becomes unspecified special treatment. The English retains condescension but removes the precise insult that Sakura turns back on her.

contexts.japanese: 「よろしくサクラ。マキリの娘だそうだけど、軽蔑はしないであげるわ。いちおうシロウの知り合いみたいだし、特別に人間扱いしてあげる」
contexts.english: "Hi, Sakura. I heard you're a daughter of the Makiris, but I won't hold that against you. You seem like you know Shirou, so I'll give you special treatment."

findings.description: Sakura silently continuing to eat after the shock becomes merely eating too.
findings.sourceReading: Crushed by Rin's superior cooking, Sakura says no more and wordlessly devotes herself to moving food into her mouth.
findings.explanation: Sakura silently continuing to eat after the shock becomes merely eating too.

contexts.japanese: ショックで打ちひしがれた桜は、それきりモクモクと料理を口に運ぶだけになった。
contexts.english: Sakura was stunned, but she still ended up eating the food too.

findings.description: Shirou wondering whether family rivalry explains Illya becomes asserting it must.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou speculates that the Einzbern and Makiri families may be on bad terms.
findings.explanation: Shirou wondering whether family rivalry explains Illya becomes asserting it must.

contexts.japanese: 「イリヤ、桜とは初対面のくせになんであんなにつっかかるんだろう。やっぱりアインツベルンとマキリって仲が悪いのかな」
contexts.english: "Why is Illya being so gruff with her when it's their first time meeting? The Einzberns and Makiris must not get along."

findings.description: Sakura's promise to strike back at Rin with Shirou-taught cooking becomes a promise to make his favorites. Her grin and the following mock battle talk remain, but their setup is missing.
findings.sourceReading: Sakura proposes playful retaliation against Rin through a breakfast made using what Shirou taught her. Her mischievous grin and their subsequent talk of striking back confirm the competitive framing.
findings.explanation: Sakura's promise to strike back at Rin with Shirou-taught cooking becomes a promise to make his favorites. Her grin and the following mock battle talk remain, but their setup is missing.

contexts.japanese: 今夜は遠坂先輩にご馳走してもらいましたから、明日の朝はわたしが受け持ちますね。先輩仕込みの朝食で仕返ししてあげちゃいます」
contexts.english: Since Tohsaka-senpai took care of us tonight, I'll make breakfast tomorrow morning. I'll cook the things you like for breakfast."

findings.description: Honoring Archer's words at the relevant choice becomes doing whatever Archer says.
findings.sourceReading: Illya tells Shirou to return immediately to the choice and properly keep Archer's words, specifically the protective instruction governing this escape.
findings.explanation: Honoring Archer's words at the relevant choice becomes doing whatever Archer says.

contexts.japanese: シロウはすぐに選択肢に戻って、ちゃあんとアーチャーの言葉を守るコト！
contexts.english: Shirou, go back to the last decision and do what Archer says!

findings.description: Shirou not believing appearance is his reason becomes not being influenced on purpose.
findings.sourceReading: He does not think he is simply fooled by Illya's looks, but admits that his hesitation itself proves her appearance affects him.
findings.explanation: Shirou not believing appearance is his reason becomes not being influenced on purpose.

contexts.japanese: 自分ではそんな気はしないが、躊躇っている時点であの子の外見に影響されているんだから。
contexts.english: It's not like I'm doing it on purpose, but maybe what she looks like is getting to me.

findings.description: Saber and Kiritsugu surviving to the end becomes winning the war.
findings.sourceReading: Saber says she cooperated with Kiritsugu and remained/won through to the final stage of the previous war.
findings.explanation: Saber and Kiritsugu surviving to the end becomes winning the war.

contexts.japanese: 前回の聖杯戦争のおり、衛宮切嗣はマスターの一人でした。私は彼と協力して聖杯戦争に挑み、最後まで勝ち残りました。
contexts.english: Kiritsugu Emiya was one of the Masters in the last Holy Grail War. I fought alongside him for the Grail, and we won.

findings.description: Shirou lacking the nerve to open the church door becomes opening it.
findings.sourceReading: Although he came at Saber's urging, Shirou cannot summon the spirit to push open the door and question Kirei about ten years ago.
findings.explanation: Shirou lacking the nerve to open the church door becomes opening it.

contexts.japanese: あの扉を押し開け、神父に十年前の出来事を尋ねる気概が生まれない。
contexts.english: As I push on the door, I don't feel particularly motivated to ask the priest about what happened ten years ago.

findings.description: Shirou's muscles locking when the man stands becomes admiration of firm, strong movement. Shirou still freezes later as the hand approaches his neck.
findings.sourceReading: The man's act of standing instantly makes Shirou's muscles lock. The following approach provokes an expectation of being killed.
findings.explanation: Shirou's muscles locking when the man stands becomes admiration of firm, strong movement. Shirou still freezes later as the hand approaches his neck.

contexts.japanese: その動作だけで、筋肉という筋肉が硬直した。
contexts.english: are firm and strong.

contexts.japanese: 瞬間。
contexts.english: Just from a glance, I can tell that his movements

findings.description: Shirou accepting he will be killed becomes feeling he must fight for his life.
findings.sourceReading: Despite the man's ordinary approach, Shirou inexplicably resigns himself to being killed there.
findings.explanation: Shirou accepting he will be killed becomes feeling he must fight for his life.

contexts.japanese: それだけだというのに、何故—俺はこの男に、ここで殺されると覚悟したのか。
contexts.english: But then...why do I feel like I'm about to fight for my life?

findings.description: Shirou recognizing the man's withdrawal as normal becomes agreeing that the man is not wrong.
findings.sourceReading: The man moves away; Shirou thinks that distancing is the natural outcome and that his own death panic was abnormal.
findings.explanation: Shirou recognizing the man's withdrawal as normal becomes agreeing that the man is not wrong.

contexts.japanese: そう、それが当然だ。
contexts.english: I can't say he's wrong.

findings.description: Shirou saying he would not visit Kirei even if asked becomes rejecting Kirei's stated reasons.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou says he came solely with a question and otherwise would not come to Kirei's place even if someone begged him.
findings.explanation: Shirou saying he would not visit Kirei even if asked becomes rejecting Kirei's stated reasons.

contexts.japanese: 「—そんな訳ないだろ。単に聞きたい事があるから来ただけだ。そうでもなけりゃ、頼まれたっておまえの所になんて来るもんか」
contexts.english: "I don't intend to. I'm just here to ask you a question. Like I'd come just for the reasons you gave."

findings.description: Kirei's ominous smile becomes repulsive.
findings.sourceReading: His curled mouth forms an ill-omened smile, as though secretly savoring pleasure.
findings.explanation: Kirei's ominous smile becomes repulsive.

contexts.japanese: 密かな愉しみに酔うような、それは、不吉な笑みだった。
contexts.english: It's a repulsive smile, as if he's savoring the moment.

findings.description: Refusing a separate killer persona becomes adopting one.
findings.sourceReading: Kirei says Kiritsugu could easily have prepared a separate 'cold-blooded' personality, but likely believed such a person could neither reach nor deserve the Grail.
findings.explanation: Refusing a separate killer persona becomes adopting one.

contexts.japanese: “冷徹である”という異なる人格さえ用意すれば容易いものを、そんな人間では聖杯に届かない、届く価値がないと信じたのだろう」
contexts.english: One so easily changed by magical suggestion or merely hardening their heart would not have been worthy of obtaining the grail. That must have been his belief. So he adopted the identity of a killer through and through.

findings.description: Shirou's certainty that none of the account was false disappears.
findings.sourceReading: What Shirou can tell is that nothing in Kirei's account was a lie, and that the otherwise indifferent man bears anger toward Kiritsugu.
findings.explanation: Shirou's certainty that none of the account was false disappears.

contexts.japanese: ……判るのは今の話に何一つ嘘がなかった事と—
contexts.english: But, the one thing that I do know for certain is...

findings.description: Shirou's two extremes and ordinary wounded human become avoidance versus embracing humanity.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou asks whether Kirei is different: neither one who suffers no wounds nor one who has nothing but wounds, but an ordinary human who is wounded when cut; is priesthood the difference from Kiritsugu?
findings.explanation: Shirou's two extremes and ordinary wounded human become avoidance versus embracing humanity.

contexts.japanese: 「……じゃあ、アンタは違うのか。傷を負わないのでもなく、傷しかないのでもない。斬られれば傷を負う、まっとうな人間だって。アンタは神父だから、そこが切嗣とは違うと……？」
contexts.english: "...And you're different? He was someone who avoided getting hurt. While you say you were hurt, as you took a path embracing humanity. Being a priest made you different from Kiritsugu...?"

findings.description: A childish wish becomes a wish held since childhood.
findings.sourceReading: Kirei calls Shirou and Kiritsugu people who retain an immature or childlike wish.
findings.explanation: A childish wish becomes a wish held since childhood.

contexts.japanese: 「幼いままの願望を持つもの。
contexts.english: "You've wished for something from an early age.

findings.description: Sacrifices to be ignored become excess and hypocrisy.
findings.sourceReading: In Kiritsugu's too-simple design, the surplus parts that do not fit its perfect shape are sacrifices; the text overlays disposing of them with ignoring them.
findings.explanation: Sacrifices to be ignored become excess and hypocrisy.

contexts.japanese: 「判らずともいい。ただ衛宮切嗣の願いは“平和”だった。実にシンプルだろう。シンプルすぎるが故に、複雑な世の中ではパーツが余ってしまう。その完璧な形に入りきれない余分は処分するしかない」
contexts.english: "You don't have to understand. Kiritsugu Emiya's wish was, in a word, 'peace.' Very simple, isn't it? So simple, in fact, that in a complex world it renders much unneeded. All he could do was dispose of or ignore all the excess and hypocrisy that didn't fit into his perfect ideal."

findings.description: A historically inherited tie becomes the sins of the father.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou and Einzbern stand under that inherited因縁: the charged connection produced by Kiritsugu's betrayal.
findings.explanation: A historically inherited tie becomes the sins of the father.

contexts.japanese: おまえとアインツベルンは、そういう因縁の下にある」
contexts.english: And the sins of the father underpin your relationship with them."

findings.description: Obsession no human can confront becomes obsession not just anyone can possess.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou has no words because an obsession lasting centuries is not something a human being can stand against or confront.
findings.explanation: Obsession no human can confront becomes obsession not just anyone can possess.

contexts.japanese: 何百年もの間続く執念なんて、それは人が対峙できるものではないからだ。
contexts.english: Not just anyone can obsess over a single goal for hundreds of years.

findings.description: Risking Shirou's own life each night becomes weighing lives in general.
findings.sourceReading: Kirei tells Shirou, like Kiritsugu, to put his own life on the scales night after night and lure out his target.
findings.explanation: Risking Shirou's own life each night becomes weighing lives in general.

contexts.japanese: 「十分だ。それがおまえの戦う意義ならば、死を賭して戦うがいい。長引けばそれだけ犠牲者は出る。切嗣と同じよう、夜毎己が命を秤にかけて標的を誘き寄せろ」
contexts.english: "That is sufficient. If that is what drives you, then fight like your life depends on it. The longer it lasts, the more victims there will be. Do as Kiritsugu did and weigh lives on a balance, all to lure out your objective."

findings.description: Shirou turning his back on Kirei becomes Kirei turning his back on Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou turns his back on the priest as he concludes he has nothing left to ask.
findings.explanation: Shirou turning his back on Kirei becomes Kirei turning his back on Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 神父に背を向ける。
contexts.english: The priest turns his back on me.

findings.description: Sakura seeming strange two days ago becomes looking strange throughout the last two days.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou recalls that Sakura also seemed odd two days earlier.
findings.explanation: Sakura seeming strange two days ago becomes looking strange throughout the last two days.

contexts.japanese: 思えば二日前の桜も様子が変だった。
contexts.english: Come to think of it, Sakura has looked off for the last two days.

findings.description: Descending a slope becomes starting down a nearby road.
findings.sourceReading: They begin descending the sloping road before choosing whether to patrol Miyama or Shinto.
findings.explanation: Descending a slope becomes starting down a nearby road.

contexts.japanese: 坂道を降り始める。
contexts.english: We start down a nearby road.

findings.description: Descending to the intersection becomes returning to it.
findings.sourceReading: After circling the residential area, they descend to the intersection.
findings.explanation: Descending to the intersection becomes returning to it.

contexts.japanese: 住宅地を一通り回って交差点に降りる。
contexts.english: After doing a circuit of the neighborhoods, we return to the intersection.

findings.description: Hesitation disappearing when Shirou nearly died becomes disappearing when he risked his life.
findings.sourceReading: In both patrol branches Shirou says his hesitation vanished when he was on the verge of death.
findings.explanation: Hesitation disappearing when Shirou nearly died becomes disappearing when he risked his life.

contexts.japanese: 躊躇いは死にかけた時に消えている。
contexts.english: Any hesitation disappeared the moment I risked my life.

contexts.japanese: 躊躇いは死にかけた時に消えている。
contexts.english: Any hesitation disappeared the moment I risked my life.

findings.description: A body that will not move and a mind that issues no command become a body disobeying its mind.
findings.sourceReading: His body will not move, and his head will not tell it what to do next: both thought and action are arrested.
findings.explanation: A body that will not move and a mind that issues no command become a body disobeying its mind.

contexts.japanese: なのに体は動かず、頭は次の行動を命じてくれない。
contexts.english: But now, my body won't listen to my brain.

contexts.japanese: なのに体は動かず、頭は次の行動を命じてくれない。
contexts.english: But now, my body won't listen to my brain.

findings.description: The victim not surviving if they remain still becomes doubt that the pair can help.
findings.sourceReading: Saber says that if things continue this way, the attacked person will not be saved, despite not knowing what happened.
findings.explanation: The victim not surviving if they remain still becomes doubt that the pair can help.

contexts.japanese: 「悲鳴が止みました。感じ取れる気配も消えかけています。何が起きたかは判りませんが、このままでは襲われた者は助からないでしょう」
contexts.english: "The scream stopped. The presence we sensed is fading. I don't know what just happened, but I doubt we'll be able to help whoever was attacked."

findings.description: Fear of letting someone die becomes fear of merely watching someone die.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou's fear of a death match is drowned out by fear that he will leave someone to die through inaction.
findings.explanation: Fear of letting someone die becomes fear of merely watching someone die.

contexts.japanese: 誰かを見殺しにするのだ、という恐れにかき消された。
contexts.english: the fear of an imminent battle of life and death.

contexts.japanese: 誰かを見殺しにするのだ、という恐れにかき消された。
contexts.english: the dread of an imminent battle of life and death.

findings.description: Shinto being easier for a hostile Master to operate in becomes easier for Shirou to deal with them there.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou chooses Shinto because a Master planning something dangerous would find it easier to act there than in Miyama.
findings.explanation: Shinto being easier for a hostile Master to operate in becomes easier for Shirou to deal with them there.

contexts.japanese: 「新都に行こう。物騒な事を企んでいるマスターがいるとしたら、深山より新都の方がやりやすいだろうからな」
contexts.english: "Let's go to Shinto. If any of the Masters is up to no good, then it'll be easier to deal with them there."

findings.description: Shirou's skill failing to match his plan becomes a shared failure to account for his skill.
findings.sourceReading: Saber says Shirou's action itself was right; if there was a shortcoming, only his ability failed to keep pace with his idea.
findings.explanation: Shirou's skill failing to match his plan becomes a shared failure to account for his skill.

contexts.japanese: 「いえ、マスターの行動自体は正しい。失点があるとしたら、シロウの技量が考えに付いてこなかっただけでしょう。
contexts.english: "No, Master, your actions were correct. If a mistake was made, it was that we failed to account for your skill level.

findings.description: Saber's decision not to pursue Shinji gains a for-my-sake motive.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou supposes she judged there was no need to pursue Shinji now that he was no longer a Master.
findings.explanation: Saber's decision not to pursue Shinji gains a for-my-sake motive.

contexts.japanese: マスターでなくなった慎二を追う必要はない、と考えてくれたのだろう。
contexts.english: She's probably decided—for my sake—that Shinji isn't worth pursuing now that he's no longer a Master.

findings.description: Zouken's account of learning about the Grail and arranging his grandson's contract becomes an account centered on Shinji's actions. The preceding admission that Zouken selected him survives, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of Zouken's agency.
findings.sourceReading: Zouken says he learned the Grail would appear and had his grandson contract in his place. He then addresses Shirou as someone belonging to a magical lineage.
findings.explanation: Zouken's account of learning about the Grail and arranging his grandson's contract becomes an account centered on Shinji's actions. The preceding admission that Zouken selected him survives, so the change is local rather than a complete removal of Zouken's agency.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯が現れると知り、ワシではなく孫にサーヴァントと契約させたのだ。おぬしとて魔道を究める血の末席。
contexts.english: When he learned of the Holy Grail, he—not I—made a contract with a Servant. Like you, he is the last of a line walking the ways of the wise.

findings.description: Shirou starting to run after handing over the woman becomes Saber starting to run.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou entrusts the woman to Saber and sets off running; she then announces she will lead and moves ahead.
findings.explanation: Shirou starting to run after handing over the woman becomes Saber starting to run.

contexts.japanese: 女性をセイバーに預けて走り出す。
contexts.english: Saber takes the woman and starts running.

findings.description: Kirei taking care of Shirou becomes Shirou owing him.
findings.sourceReading: Despite appearances, Shirou says Kirei ended up fussing over him or looking after him in one way or another.
findings.explanation: Kirei taking care of Shirou becomes Shirou owing him.

contexts.japanese: なんだかんだって世話やかれちまった」
contexts.english: I feel like I owe him now."

findings.description: A little carelessness causing a repeat becomes Shirou recklessly repeating the event.
findings.sourceReading: Saber warns that even slight carelessness could cause last night's near-fatal situation to recur.
findings.explanation: A little carelessness causing a repeat becomes Shirou recklessly repeating the event.

contexts.japanese: 「それで、何をされたのですかシロウ……！　貴方の傷はまだ完治してはいない。少しの油断で昨夜の繰り返しになるのだと、貴方自身も判っている筈です……！」
contexts.english: "What did he do to you, Shirou!? Your wounds aren't fully healed yet. You know what will happen if you're reckless enough to repeat what happened last night!"

findings.description: Shirou's cheeks loosening into a smile becomes his cheeks burning.
findings.sourceReading: Saber's indignant face is so fresh to Shirou that his expression involuntarily softens into another smile.
findings.explanation: Shirou's cheeks loosening into a smile becomes his cheeks burning.

contexts.japanese: そう抗議する顔すら新鮮で、つい頬が緩んでしまう。
contexts.english: Even her indignation is amusing, and my cheeks start burning.

findings.description: Saber jumping backward becomes flinching and taking one step.
findings.sourceReading: She springs backward with a sustained shuffling sound after Shirou calls her properly a girl.
findings.explanation: Saber jumping backward becomes flinching and taking one step.

contexts.japanese: ざざ、と後ろに跳び退くセイバー。
contexts.english: Saber flinches and takes a step back.

findings.description: Softhearted goodness becomes meddling.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou wonders whether Saber is an お人好し—a kind, overly good-natured person—or a perfectionist.
findings.explanation: Softhearted goodness becomes meddling.

contexts.japanese: 「—お人好しなんだか、完璧主義なんだかな」
contexts.english: "I can't tell if you're a busybody or a perfectionist."

findings.description: Fulfilling an overdue promise becomes doing a promise.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou thinks he must now properly fulfill the promise that should have been exchanged at the beginning.
findings.explanation: Fulfilling an overdue promise becomes doing a promise.

contexts.japanese: 交わすべきだった約束を、ここできちんと果たさないと。
contexts.english: I have to make her a promise that I should have done from the beginning.

findings.description: A patrol that amounts to relying on chance becomes an idea that happened to seem good to Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: Patrolling on foot is like hoping for coincidence, although Saber calls the method dangerous but reliable.
findings.explanation: A patrol that amounts to relying on chance becomes an idea that happened to seem good to Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 偶然に期待するようなものだが、セイバー曰く『危険ではあるが確実』な手なのだそうだ。
contexts.english: It just happened to seem like a good idea to me, but Saber said that it was a "risky but certain" choice.

findings.description: No mana supply becomes no extra mana.
findings.sourceReading: Saber receives no magical energy from Shirou and must spend her own reserves merely maintaining existence.
findings.explanation: No mana supply becomes no extra mana.

contexts.japanese: 俺からの魔力提供がないセイバーは、それこそ日々『ここにいる』だけで精一杯なのだ。
contexts.english: Without any extra magical energy from me, it takes all of Saber's power just to exist.

findings.description: Shirou's wish to make up for a leftovers lunch becomes an offer based on having leftovers available, changing why he insists on dinner.
findings.sourceReading: Because lunch was only leftovers, Shirou urges Saber to eat a proper evening meal before sleeping.
findings.explanation: Shirou's wish to make up for a leftovers lunch becomes an offer based on having leftovers available, changing why he insists on dinner.

contexts.japanese: 「魔力の温存は判ったよ。けど人間食事も大切だろ。昼は余りもので済ませちまったから、夕飯はちゃんと食べてくれ。寝るのはその後でいいじゃないか」
contexts.english: "I know you need to save energy, but meals are important, too. I still have some leftovers from lunch, so let me fix you dinner. You can go to bed after that."

findings.description: Shirou being unable to raise his cup becomes everyone refusing to drink.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou cannot bring himself to drink because even the sound of the teacup seems likely to echo; his hot green tea has gone cold.
findings.explanation: Shirou being unable to raise his cup becomes everyone refusing to drink.

contexts.japanese: お茶を飲もうにも湯飲みの音さえ響きそうで飲めず、熱い緑茶はとっくに冷めきっていた。
contexts.english: They don't even drink the tea to avoid making a sipping sound, leaving the hot tea to go cold.

findings.description: Shirou's remark that Saber is unsociable like her name disappears.
findings.sourceReading: He calls the name unusual, says she is as blunt or unsociable as the name suggests, but guarantees she is a good person and asks Sakura to teach her Japan.
findings.explanation: Shirou's remark that Saber is unsociable like her name disappears.

contexts.japanese: 「ん？　ああ、変わった名前だろ。名前通り無愛想だけど、いいヤツなのは保証する。あんまり日本になれてないんでおかしなところもあるけど、桜が教えてくれると助かる」
contexts.english: "Hm? Oh, yeah. Her name sounds kinda strange, but I guarantee that she's good people. She might act a little weird because she isn't used to Japan yet, but I'd appreciate it if you'd help her out."

findings.description: Inviting Rin inside because of a small connection becomes her stopping by the other day.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou's cover story says a minor connection led him to have Rin come into the house.
findings.explanation: Inviting Rin inside because of a small connection becomes her stopping by the other day.

contexts.japanese: 「ああ。ちょっとした縁で家にあがってもらったんだ。
contexts.english: "Yeah. She stopped by the other day.

findings.description: Shirou's admired model-student image becomes romantic fantasy and school-idol fixation.
findings.sourceReading: He jokes that the proud model student of their school died last night—in his own mind—and that 'model student Rin Tohsaka' has vanished from him.
findings.explanation: Shirou's admired model-student image becomes romantic fantasy and school-idol fixation.

contexts.japanese: 我が校の誇る優等生は昨夜死んだ。
contexts.english: Whatever fantasies I had of Tohsaka died last night.

contexts.japanese: まことに遺憾だが、優等生遠坂凛は俺の中から消え去ってしまったのだこんちくしょう。
contexts.english: To my deep regret, Rin Tohsaka, the star student and idol of my high school life, was wiped away yesterday. Damn it.

findings.description: Sakura's claim that Shirou and Rin are unrelated becomes Rin being unrelated to both Sakura and Shirou.
findings.sourceReading: Sakura insists that Senpai and that person have nothing to do with each other, while she is the one who is here, repeating why in distress.
findings.explanation: Sakura's claim that Shirou and Rin are unrelated becomes Rin being unrelated to both Sakura and Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 「どうして、遠坂先輩がここに来るんですか。そんなのおかしいです。だってぜんぜん関係ない。ここにいるのはわたしで、先輩とあの人はぜんぜん関係ないのに、どうして」
contexts.english: "Why was she here? It's a little strange. She has nothing to do with us. Not me, or you, so why?"

findings.description: People with no recourse but to cling to the Grail become people close to it.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou concludes that people who can only cling to something like the Grail are the ones who become Masters.
findings.explanation: People with no recourse but to cling to the Grail become people close to it.

contexts.japanese: いや、もとより“聖杯”なんてものに縋るしかない人間がマスターになる。
contexts.english: In fact, people close to the grail itself are bound to become Masters.

findings.description: An obsession Shirou cannot contend with becomes one he cannot imagine.
findings.sourceReading: Einzbern's thousand-year fixation is not something Shirou can do anything about or stand against.
findings.explanation: An obsession Shirou cannot contend with becomes one he cannot imagine.

contexts.japanese: その執念は俺がどうこうできるものじゃない。
contexts.english: I can't even begin to imagine that level of obsession.

findings.description: Kiritsugu making Grail-dependent people his enemies becomes merely defying the Grail.
findings.sourceReading: Kiritsugu turned those beings or people who could only be saved by the Grail against himself and destroyed it.
findings.explanation: Kiritsugu making Grail-dependent people his enemies becomes merely defying the Grail.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣はそれを敵に回して、聖杯を破壊した。
contexts.english: My old man defied the grail and chose to destroy it instead.

findings.description: Kirei's single spoken I see becomes a silent nod.
findings.sourceReading: He gives no extended answer, but does say one word, 'I see,' while nodding.
findings.explanation: Kirei's single spoken I see becomes a silent nod.

contexts.japanese: 神父は何も言わない。
contexts.english: The priest says nothing.

contexts.japanese: ただ一言、そうか、と頷いただけだ。
contexts.english: He merely nods in acknowledgement.

findings.description: Do not regret becomes no need to apologize.
findings.sourceReading: Kirei tells Shirou not to rue defeating the known Master because humans cannot change the past.
findings.explanation: Do not regret becomes no need to apologize.

contexts.japanese: 「ならば悔いるな。人間には過去を変える事はできん。
contexts.english: "Then there is no need to be sorry. People cannot change their pasts.

findings.description: Kirei already standing immediately before Shirou becomes Shirou taking position before Kirei.
findings.sourceReading: When Shirou reluctantly turns around, the priest is already standing right in front of him.
findings.explanation: Kirei already standing immediately before Shirou becomes Shirou taking position before Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 渋々と振り返ると、神父は俺のすぐ目の前に立っていた。
contexts.english: I reluctantly turn back and stand in front of the priest.

findings.description: Vile wishes become mundane wishes.
findings.sourceReading: Shirou hears Kirei equate lofty wishes with 下劣な, base or morally vile wishes.
findings.explanation: Vile wishes become mundane wishes.

contexts.japanese: 崇高な願いも下劣な願いも変わらない。
contexts.english: To him, there's no difference between noble and mundane wishes.

findings.description: Saber denying that Shirou's order was unreasonable becomes claiming she would never defy him.
findings.sourceReading: Saber begins to say she did not consider Shirou's instruction unreasonable.
findings.explanation: Saber denying that Shirou's order was unreasonable becomes claiming she would never defy him.

contexts.japanese: 「な、何を言うのです。私は別に、シロウの指示が無茶だとは思ってなど—」
contexts.english: "S-speak nothing of it! I would never defy your—"

findings.description: Saber looking nothing like her prior self becomes looking similar yet different.

counterexamples.sourceReading: If possible, they remove Master status through the marks; failure can force a fatal conflict.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou keeps a nonlethal objective before the worst-case death struggle.

contexts.japanese: 令呪を奪う事によりマスターでなくす
contexts.english: take away his Command Spells and he won't be a Master anymore.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s refusal to call Saber is his own choice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He does not want to seek help or worry her and suppresses groans.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s refusal to call Saber is his own choice.

contexts.japanese: セイバーに助けを求めるのはイヤだった
contexts.english: I don't want to call to Saber for help.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s ideal is accompanied by unresolved self-questioning.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He asks whether his thinking is right, where it originates and how to realize the dream.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s ideal is accompanied by unresolved self-questioning.

contexts.japanese: 自分の考えが正しいのか
contexts.english: If the way that I think is correct.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s lack of recognition is explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: 俺、あいつ知らない says he does not know her, beyond not being friends.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s lack of recognition is explicit.

contexts.japanese: 俺、あいつ知らないぞ
contexts.english: I don't even know her.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s brave surface excuse does not conceal his private ignorance from the reader.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He cites few remaining spells aloud but privately admits not knowing how to use them.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s brave surface excuse does not conceal his private ignorance from the reader.

contexts.japanese: 正直使い方が判らない
contexts.english: I don't really know how to use it either.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s Grail unease does not become knowledge of its nature.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He explicitly does not know what it is but vaguely feels it does not suit Saber.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s Grail unease does not become knowledge of its nature.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯が何なのかは知らない
contexts.english: I don't know what the Holy Grail is.

counterexamples.description: His fear of passive death concerns the pain imposed on Rin.
counterexamples.sourceReading: 無抵抗で殺される pushes painful responsibility onto her rather than only maximizing his pain.
counterexamples.explanation: His fear of passive death concerns the pain imposed on Rin.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂に辛い思いを押し付ける
contexts.english: more painful for Tohsaka

counterexamples.description: The work issue remains concealment rather than wanting money.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He anticipates lying about work to explain battle-related absence without worrying the household.
counterexamples.explanation: The work issue remains concealment rather than wanting money.

contexts.japanese: アルバイトと偽らなければならない
contexts.english: I'll have to lie and say I'm working

counterexamples.description: Taiga’s permissive Kiritsugu account remains her speech.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She remembers him accepting divergent views and letting life happen.
counterexamples.explanation: Taiga’s permissive Kiritsugu account remains her speech.

contexts.japanese: 人生なるようになるさ
contexts.english: whatever happens, happens.

counterexamples.description: The fleeing simile is explicitly corrected to actual flight.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He first says like fleeing, then admits he really fled.
counterexamples.explanation: The fleeing simile is explicitly corrected to actual flight.

contexts.japanese: 逃げるようにじゃなくて、逃げた
contexts.english: No, no ifs about it. I ran.

counterexamples.description: An existing answer remains distinguished from having none.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He corrects his initial claim of lacking an answer before describing a restriction on speaking.
counterexamples.explanation: An existing answer remains distinguished from having none.

contexts.japanese: いや、答えはある
contexts.english: No, I do have an answer.

counterexamples.description: Perceived futility coexists with the value of saving one person.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He continues doing possible cleanup if even one person can be helped.
counterexamples.explanation: Perceived futility coexists with the value of saving one person.

contexts.japanese: 一人でも助かるのなら
contexts.english: just saving one person.

counterexamples.description: Taking up the ideal remains an obligation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: ならないといけない binds him to succeeding Kiritsugu and guarding what he longed for.
counterexamples.explanation: Taking up the ideal remains an obligation.

contexts.japanese: 正義の味方にならないといけない
contexts.english: I have to become a hero of justice.

counterexamples.description: The secrecy undertaking does not stop aid to Rin.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He will not tell but excludes her independent discovery and promises continued cooperation.
counterexamples.explanation: The secrecy undertaking does not stop aid to Rin.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂に出来る限り協力する
contexts.english: I'm going to help Tohsaka as much as I can.

counterexamples.description: The quarrel deepens into not bearing being a hindrance.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Beyond resentment at being rescued, Shirou cannot endure slowing Archer’s escape.
counterexamples.explanation: The quarrel deepens into not bearing being a hindrance.

contexts.japanese: それより足手まといになる事が耐えられない
contexts.english: more than that, I can't bear being a hindrance to him.

counterexamples.description: Archer’s loyalty is Shirou’s belief before the unexplained pause.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou assumes Archer would not betray Rin, not a pledge by Archer himself.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer’s loyalty is Shirou’s belief before the unexplained pause.

contexts.japanese: アーチャーだって、遠坂を裏切るような真似はしない
contexts.english: Archer would also never betray Tohsaka.

counterexamples.description: Stopped pursuit is not acceptance or forgiveness.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou halts after the warning; his preceding fury remains unresolved as Caster vanishes.
counterexamples.explanation: Stopped pursuit is not acceptance or forgiveness.

contexts.japanese: 足を止める
contexts.english: I stop.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s defiance causes his own backward jump.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He jumps without considering consequences because he wants to resist Archer’s words.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s defiance causes his own backward jump.

contexts.japanese: 後先考えず後ろに跳んだ
contexts.english: I jump backwards without thinking of the consequences.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s unusual betrayal logic remains his own judgment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He thinks the attack is admissible because no promise was made.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s unusual betrayal logic remains his own judgment.

contexts.japanese: それはアリなんだと思う
contexts.english: I think that's fair.

counterexamples.description: Reaching Archer’s skill remains conditional on long training.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber gives natural aptitude plus a prolonged training condition.
counterexamples.explanation: Reaching Archer’s skill remains conditional on long training.

contexts.japanese: 長く鍛えれば
contexts.english: if you train long enough.

counterexamples.description: The training request changes from survival to fighting.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He rejects solely surviving as his future instructional goal.
counterexamples.explanation: The training request changes from survival to fighting.

contexts.japanese: 生き残る為の鍛錬じゃなくて、戦う方法
contexts.english: Not just how to survive, but I want to learn how to fight.

counterexamples.description: The question moves from desire to becoming.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The opening asks what was sought and why; this asks what he tried to become.
counterexamples.explanation: The question moves from desire to becoming.

contexts.japanese: 何に成ろうとしたのか
contexts.english: What did I want to become

counterexamples.description: The hero-justice quotation is recognized as someone else’s speech without naming them.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He realizes the speaker was not himself but wakes before explicitly identifying who.
counterexamples.explanation: The hero-justice quotation is recognized as someone else’s speech without naming them.

contexts.japanese: 俺ではなく、たしか
contexts.english: It's not me that said that, but...

counterexamples.description: He admits complete fault while asking for mitigating circumstances.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Full culpability and desire for some allowance coexist in the embarrassed monologue.
counterexamples.explanation: He admits complete fault while asking for mitigating circumstances.

contexts.japanese: 全面的に俺が悪い
contexts.english: I'm completely at fault.

counterexamples.description: Understanding the argument does not imply accepting its method.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou recognizes the rationale then refuses indiscriminate predation.
counterexamples.explanation: Understanding the argument does not imply accepting its method.

contexts.japanese: おまえの言い分は解った
contexts.english: I get your argument.

counterexamples.description: Taiga’s sisterlike role and the room remain personal stakes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He cannot lose the person who has long been his older sister in this living room.
counterexamples.explanation: Taiga’s sisterlike role and the room remain personal stakes.

contexts.japanese: 姉であってくれた人を、この居間で失う
contexts.english: like my older sister and stayed with me until now, in this very living room.

counterexamples.description: Escape acceptance is corrected to having no choice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Injured thought initially describes accepting escape, then revises to only being able to accept.
counterexamples.explanation: Escape acceptance is corrected to having no choice.

contexts.japanese: 受け入れるしか、なかった
contexts.english: I have no choice but to accept it.

counterexamples.description: The suppressed action against Rin stays suppressed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Extreme anger leaves a dash-hidden action should she endanger the hostage.
counterexamples.explanation: The suppressed action against Rin stays suppressed.

contexts.japanese: 俺が遠坂を—いる
contexts.english: I'll ----- Tohsaka

counterexamples.description: Refusing Caster does not mean refusing cooperation in general.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He says the Grail has nothing to do with it and he will not partner with her.
counterexamples.explanation: Refusing Caster does not mean refusing cooperation in general.

contexts.japanese: おまえとは組まないだけ
contexts.english: I just won't cooperate with you.

counterexamples.description: The equal-power comparison remains a self-opponent argument.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He contrasts defeat by others with refusing to submit to himself.
counterexamples.explanation: The equal-power comparison remains a self-opponent argument.

contexts.japanese: 自分には負けられない
contexts.english: I can't lose against myself.

counterexamples.description: His possible wrongness is separated from the path’s rightness.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He allows that he was wrong from the start but refuses to declare the pursued path wrong.
counterexamples.explanation: His possible wrongness is separated from the path’s rightness.

contexts.japanese: 自分が初めから間違いであったとしても
contexts.english: Even if I was wrong from the start

counterexamples.description: Shirou rejects her coerced control even without Master status.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He invokes Saber’s refusal and the ethical stake that outlives their contract.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou rejects her coerced control even without Master status.

contexts.japanese: セイバーは、嫌がっていた
contexts.english: Saber hated it.

counterexamples.description: The dinner example retains the reason for making.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou puts the origin/motive before materials and technique, using Rin’s Japanese-food request.
counterexamples.explanation: The dinner example retains the reason for making.

contexts.japanese: 何故それを作る気になったのか
contexts.english: why you decided to make that

counterexamples.description: Projection has never helped remains Shirou’s self-assessment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He dismisses his own ability while Rin’s strange reaction remains unarticulated.
counterexamples.explanation: Projection has never helped remains Shirou’s self-assessment.

contexts.japanese: 役に立ったコトなんてない
contexts.english: that's never helped me before

counterexamples.description: Rin explicitly excludes saving people to obtain love.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her diagnosis is distinguished from the usual selfish-attention explanation.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin explicitly excludes saving people to obtain love.

contexts.japanese: 他人を助けるのは自分が愛されたいからだ、なんて一般論を口にしてるんじゃない
contexts.english: I'm not talking about the common opinion that people save others so that they can be loved.

counterexamples.description: Admitted distortion does not become abandonment of the ideal.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou accepts something is wrong while refusing the advice because helping itself cannot be wrong.
counterexamples.explanation: Admitted distortion does not become abandonment of the ideal.

contexts.japanese: 確かに俺は何か間違えている。けどいいんだ
contexts.english: There is something wrong with me. But it's fine.

counterexamples.description: The confession exceeds repayment and remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The pendant debt is retrospective justification; long admiration and increased liking motivate the rescue.
counterexamples.explanation: The confession exceeds repayment and remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: ホントはただの後付け
contexts.english: that was just an afterthought.

counterexamples.description: Saber conditionally relinquishes her wish rather than being made categorically obedient.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If the Grail is what Gilgamesh described, Saber herself accepts that it must not exist and sacrifices her wish.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber conditionally relinquishes her wish rather than being made categorically obedient.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯がギルガメッシュの言う通りの物ならば
contexts.english: If the Holy Grail is exactly how Gilgamesh described

counterexamples.description: Shirou's reason for refusing passive sacrifice remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If going now will likely sacrifice someone, struggling until the last moment is not shameful by comparison.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's reason for refusing passive sacrifice remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: ギリギリまであがく事なんてみっともなくもなんともない
contexts.english: it's not a shame to try to do anything, to struggle until the very last moment.

counterexamples.description: Shirou explicitly includes the danger to Rin in his formation argument.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His objection is not simply preference for Saber: if she falls, Rin will be targeted next.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou explicitly includes the danger to Rin in his formation argument.

contexts.japanese: 足止め役のセイバーが倒されたら、次に狙われるのは遠坂なんだから
contexts.english: If Saber is defeated and no one is left to slow him down, Tohsaka would be next.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's tea invitation remains impromptu but emotionally honest.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Unable to confess that he wants time with her, he improvises a statement containing no false feeling.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's tea invitation remains impromptu but emotionally honest.

contexts.japanese: 思いつきで、嘘のない気持ちを口にした
contexts.english: I didn't really think too much and just told her how I felt.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's tactical explanation still includes Rin as the next target.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He rejects the claim that this is only about Saber and identifies the danger to Rin if Saber falls.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's tactical explanation still includes Rin as the next target.

contexts.japanese: 次に狙われるのは遠坂なんだから
contexts.english: Tohsaka would be next.

counterexamples.description: The short nap's clock time and duration are preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: It is still before one and Shirou slept only about thirty minutes.
counterexamples.explanation: The short nap's clock time and duration are preserved.

contexts.japanese: まだ一時前だ。三十分ぐらいしか寝てない
contexts.english: not even 1AM yet. I only slept for thirty minutes.

counterexamples.description: Shirou again identifies Rin as the next target if Saber falls.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His formation objection includes the danger to Rin rather than valuing Saber alone.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou again identifies Rin as the next target if Saber falls.

contexts.japanese: 次に狙われるのは遠坂なんだから
contexts.english: Tohsaka would be next.

counterexamples.description: Shirou explicitly limits this world's advantage to Gilgamesh.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He cannot match another Servant or an enemy with one ultimate weapon and lacks Gilgamesh's physical ability.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou explicitly limits this world's advantage to Gilgamesh.

contexts.japanese: 相手が他のサーヴァントなら、こんな世界を造ったところで太刀打ちできない
contexts.english: If my opponent was another Servant, I would not be able to match them even if I made a world like this.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's fall remains a voluntary act to prevent Gilgamesh's return.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He stops resisting and throws himself into the void after securing the chain.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's fall remains a voluntary act to prevent Gilgamesh's return.

contexts.japanese: 逆らわず、黒い孔へと身を投じた
contexts.english: Without resisting, I throw myself into the black hole.

counterexamples.description: Immobilized Shirou still chooses magecraft to continue his assigned role.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Unable to move, he refuses to give up before holding Kuzuki back and begins imagining another sword.
counterexamples.explanation: Immobilized Shirou still chooses magecraft to continue his assigned role.

contexts.japanese: 俺の役目は葛木の足止めだ。それを果たさないまま、おいそれと諦められるか
contexts.english: My role is to hold Kuzuki down. I can't give up without fulfilling my role

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s unnoticed smile and Saber’s dry rebuke survive.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber notices him smiling before he does and jokes that he may not need her shoulder after all.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s unnoticed smile and Saber’s dry rebuke survive.

contexts.japanese: 笑みがこぼれるほど元気があるのなら、この肩を貸すまでもなかったようですが
contexts.english: It seems as though I do not need to support you if you are well enough to laugh.

counterexamples.description: The crying-face reversal survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The boy who wished not to see anyone cry becomes able to see nothing but human tears forever.
counterexamples.explanation: The crying-face reversal survives.

contexts.japanese: 永遠に、人間の泣き顔しか、見ることができなくなった。
contexts.english: Could only see humans crying forever.

counterexamples.description: Rin preserves both criticism and love for Shirou’s naïveté.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She calls him naïve yet says that trait is lovable and necessary.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin preserves both criticism and love for Shirou’s naïveté.

contexts.japanese: あいつの甘いところが愛しいって思う。
contexts.english: I think that naïve part of him is lovable.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu’s limit is preserved as a problem of whom one sides with.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A hero of justice can save only the people whose side he takes.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu’s limit is preserved as a problem of whom one sides with.

contexts.japanese: 正義の味方に救えるのは、味方をした人間だけだ
contexts.english: A hero of justice can only save those he has sided with.

counterexamples.description: Shirou acknowledges the ideal’s distortion and impossibility.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He already knows there is no utopia where nobody is harmed and calls his attempted heroism hypocrisy.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou acknowledges the ideal’s distortion and impossibility.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮士郎が成ろうとする正義の味方なんてものは、それだけで偽善なんだ。
contexts.english: The hero of justice that I am trying to become is just hypocrisy.

counterexamples.description: The literal and figurative killing sequence is preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Archer says he killed people, killed hopes, saved only visible objects, and killed still more wishes.
counterexamples.explanation: The literal and figurative killing sequence is preserved.

contexts.japanese: 何十という人間の救いを殺して、目に見えるモノだけの救いを生かして、より多くの願いを殺してきた。
contexts.english: I killed the hopes of dozens of people, saved those whom I could see, and killed the wishes of even more.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's final question about regret is direct and intact.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Before crossing the point of no return, Shirou asks whether Archer regrets his path.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's final question about regret is direct and intact.

contexts.japanese: アーチャー。おまえ、後悔してるのか
contexts.english: Archer. Do you regret it?

counterexamples.description: The repeated refusal of pity and impending self-recognition are preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou repeats that he does not pity Archer, yet imagining his own feet walking that path nearly breaks him.
counterexamples.explanation: The repeated refusal of pity and impending self-recognition are preserved.

contexts.japanese: 同情なんてしない、けれど。
contexts.english: Don't feel sorry for him...but...

counterexamples.description: Archer's rejection of simple survivor guilt is preserved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He says Shirou did not adopt the ideal from guilt at being the sole rescue, but from admiration of Kiritsugu's happiness.
counterexamples.explanation: Archer's rejection of simple survivor guilt is preserved.

contexts.japanese: 助けられなかった人々に後ろめたさを感じていた訳じゃない。
contexts.english: You didn't have survivor's guilt for being the only person to be rescued.

counterexamples.description: Shirou openly admits the ideal is borrowed and driven by a curse-like compulsion.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He accepts both the borrowed origin and the obsession that his body must serve someone else before defending the beauty he saw.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou openly admits the ideal is borrowed and driven by a curse-like compulsion.

contexts.japanese: この身は誰かの為にならなければならないと、呪いのような強迫観念に、ずっとつき動かされてきた。
contexts.english: I was always driven by this curse-like obsession that my body needed to be for someone else.

counterexamples.description: The distinction between a false origin and genuine beauty remains the pivot of Shirou's answer.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He asks whether something must be false and forbidden merely because the feeling did not originate in him.
counterexamples.explanation: The distinction between a false origin and genuine beauty remains the pivot of Shirou's answer.

contexts.japanese: 自分の気持ちではないから、それは偽物なのか。
contexts.english: Is it fake because it's not my own feelings?

counterexamples.description: Shirou acknowledges sacrifice as reality while continuing to seek happiness without harm.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His ideal does not deny the real tradeoff; it refuses to call the painful best available outcome the end of moral aspiration.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou acknowledges sacrifice as reality while continuing to seek happiness without harm.

contexts.japanese: 多くを救う為に傷つけて、それが最善であっても、それでも—誰も傷つかない幸福を求め続ける。
contexts.english: Even if the best outcome is for someone to get hurt in order to save many, I'm still going to seek a version of happiness where nobody gets hurt.

counterexamples.description: Shirou limits his rescue horizon to the world visible to him before recognizing that small world as his magic.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He resolves to fight if he can save even the world he can see, then identifies the small world he alone can produce.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou limits his rescue horizon to the world visible to him before recognizing that small world as his magic.

contexts.japanese: 自分に見える世界だけでも救えるのなら、その為に戦おうと。
contexts.english: If I could save just the world that I can see, I'll fight for it.

counterexamples.description: Unlimited Blade Works remains the creation of a world containing infinite swords.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou does not merely manufacture individual blades; his only permitted magecraft gives form to the inner world that contains them without limit.
counterexamples.explanation: Unlimited Blade Works remains the creation of a world containing infinite swords.

contexts.japanese: 俺は、無限に剣を内包した世界を作る。
contexts.english: I create a world that contains infinite swords.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's opening claim that a fake can surpass the real thing remains intact.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He accepts the counterfeit label and turns it into the tactical and thematic premise for defeating the original owner.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's opening claim that a fake can surpass the real thing remains intact.

contexts.japanese: 偽物が本物に敵わない、なんて道理はない。
contexts.english: There's no rule or reason a fake can't best the real thing.

counterexamples.description: Shirou still rejects the sensible thought of resting until his arm recovers.
counterexamples.sourceReading: However phrased, the dangerous pivot is that he immediately shakes off stopping.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou still rejects the sensible thought of resting until his arm recovers.

contexts.japanese: 即座に振り払った。
contexts.english: I quickly shake that thought off.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s misunderstanding of “inner world” remains visible.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He reduces Rin’s claim about material origin to the ordinary fact that circuits generate magical energy within the body.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s misunderstanding of “inner world” remains visible.

contexts.japanese: そんなの当たり前じゃないか。
contexts.english: But isn't that obvious?

counterexamples.description: Shirou admits he simply wants to know Saber better.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The menu rationale contains a conscious personal desire for closeness.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou admits he simply wants to know Saber better.

contexts.japanese: ホントはセイバーのコトが知りたいだけ
contexts.english: Really, I just want to get to know her.

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s excessive denial of caring whether Rin likes him remains.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His stammering overreaction exposes what he tries to deny.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s excessive denial of caring whether Rin likes him remains.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂に嫌われようが好かれようが俺の知ったコトじゃない
contexts.english: I don't care whether Tohsaka likes me or not

counterexamples.description: Shirou’s assent remains an unguarded automatic response.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Taiga’s comparison catches him physically and mentally relaxed, eliciting “yeah” before reflection.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou’s assent remains an unguarded automatic response.

contexts.japanese: 間の抜けた条件反射

counterexamples.description: Past seven clock anchor retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Clock is past seven after the sun has set.
counterexamples.explanation: Past seven clock anchor retained.

contexts.japanese: 時計は七時を過ぎている。
contexts.english: The clock reads past 7:00 PM.

counterexamples.description: Impossible subjective sunset-to-night jump retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The sudden shift seems impossible to him.
counterexamples.explanation: Impossible subjective sunset-to-night jump retained.

contexts.japanese: 玄関に入るまでは夕方だったのに、居間にあがった途端夜になっているなんて、有り得ない。
contexts.english: It was barely sunset when I got into the house, but the moment I enter the living room, night has fallen. That's impossible.

counterexamples.description: Illya absent from expected side retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He addresses her beside him but finds she is no longer there.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya absent from expected side retained.

contexts.japanese: だが隣にイリヤの姿はない。
contexts.english: But Illya isn't next to me.

counterexamples.description: Dinner actually cooked despite missing recollection.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Physical meal remains and fullness support his conclusion.
counterexamples.explanation: Dinner actually cooked despite missing recollection.

contexts.japanese: どうやら夕食を作ったのは本当らしい。
contexts.english: It seems like I really did cook dinner.

counterexamples.description: Failure to retrieve shopping memory retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: After prolonged searching he can only allow it may have happened.
counterexamples.explanation: Failure to retrieve shopping memory retained.

contexts.japanese: そういう事も、あったのかもしれない。
contexts.english: Maybe that did happen.

counterexamples.description: Illya’s rest suggestion retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She treats dinner as complete and tells him he only needs rest.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya’s rest suggestion retained.

contexts.japanese: 「ええ。あとはゆっくり休むだけだね、シロウ」
contexts.english: "Yeah. You just need to rest now, Shirou."

counterexamples.description: Immediate-return plan retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He plans a short clothing change and a talk upon returning.
counterexamples.explanation: Immediate-return plan retained.

contexts.japanese: 「ん—そうだな、休まないとな。ちょっと部屋で着替えてくる。話があるから、イリヤはもうちょっと起きててくれ。すぐ戻る」
contexts.english: "Mm. Yeah, I should get some rest. I'm going to go change in my room. I want to talk to you about something, so wait here a little longer. I'll be right back."

counterexamples.description: Life force loss framed as sensation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Pain and heat feel like life force flowing out instead of blood.
counterexamples.explanation: Life force loss framed as sensation.

contexts.japanese: そうとしか思えないほど胸は熱く、痺れ、ドクドクと血液のかわりに、生気が流出していっているように思えた。
contexts.english: That's the only way I can describe it. My chest is hot, and numb. It feels like my life force is gushing out instead of blood.

counterexamples.description: Stabbing corrected to hallucination.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Narration explicitly denies a literal sword wound.
counterexamples.explanation: Stabbing corrected to hallucination.

contexts.japanese: そんなものは幻覚だ。
contexts.english: That's just a hallucination.

counterexamples.description: Past memory versus new records distinction retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He is not losing his past but failing to record current experiences.
counterexamples.explanation: Past memory versus new records distinction retained.

contexts.japanese: 過去の記憶がないのではなく、出来事の記録ができていない。
contexts.english: I'm not missing memories of my past, but I'm not making new records of my experiences.

counterexamples.description: Self and memory ruby relation retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: 自分 with きおく ruby binds personal continuity to memory sustained by pain or equivalent focus.
counterexamples.explanation: Self and memory ruby relation retained.

contexts.japanese: 胸を貫かれるほどの痛みか、それと同等の集中をしていないと、自分が保てない。
contexts.english: My memories and my self won't hold together unless I keep my focus as keen as the pain stabbing me in the chest.

counterexamples.description: Unsustainable and uncertain remedy retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He cannot keep concentration up and does not know how long it could work.
counterexamples.explanation: Unsustainable and uncertain remedy retained.

contexts.japanese: そんなものは続けられないし、続けたところで、その方法でいつまで保ってくれるか判らない。
contexts.english: I can't keep that up, and even if I could, I don't know how long it will keep working.

counterexamples.description: Sleep risks irreversible self-loss in his reasoning.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He fears he will not return to being Shirou if he sleeps.
counterexamples.explanation: Sleep risks irreversible self-loss in his reasoning.

contexts.japanese: 眠ってしまったら、もう『衛宮士郎』という自分は戻ってこれない。
contexts.english: If I fall asleep, I won't go back to being Shirou Emiya.

counterexamples.description: Residual pendant power below one Strengthening retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Ruby specifies Strengthening and remaining energy is less than one use.
counterexamples.explanation: Residual pendant power below one Strengthening retained.

contexts.japanese: 元はどれだけの魔力が篭められていたかは知らないが、残っている魔力は俺の魔術一回分にも満たない。
contexts.english: I don't know how much magical energy it used to contain, but it doesn't have enough left to use my Strengthening even once.

counterexamples.description: Happy thoughts threaten continuity retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Pleasure relaxes concentration and threatens collapse.
counterexamples.explanation: Happy thoughts threaten continuity retained.

contexts.japanese: 嬉しいコトとか楽しいコトを考えると、気が抜けて倒れそうになる。
contexts.english: If I think of fun or happy things, I'll relax and pass out.

counterexamples.description: Three-use estimate remains probable.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Remaining Blade Works limit is his estimate.
counterexamples.explanation: Three-use estimate remains probable.

contexts.japanese: 投影……アーチャーの腕を使っての“剣製”のリミットは、おそらく三回。
contexts.english: As for Projection... I can probably use Archer's "Blade Works" no more than three times.

counterexamples.description: Third use may destroy body while mind remains.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He fears bodily self-destruction independent of residual mind.
counterexamples.explanation: Third use may destroy body while mind remains.

contexts.japanese: 最後の三回目は決定的になる。精神が残っていようが、体の方が自滅する気がする。
contexts.english: And the third Projection will be decisive. My mind might remain, but I have a feeling my body will self-destruct.

counterexamples.description: Internal thousand-sword danger retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The feared consequence is stabbing from inside his own body.
counterexamples.explanation: Internal thousand-sword danger retained.

contexts.japanese: 俺は内側から、千の剣で串刺しにされて死ぬのだ。
contexts.english: I'm going to get stabbed from the inside by a thousand swords and die.

counterexamples.description: Promise to protect Sakura grounds refusal to die.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His survival insistence follows his unconditional protection promise.
counterexamples.explanation: Promise to protect Sakura grounds refusal to die.

contexts.japanese: 何があろうと桜を守ると言った。
contexts.english: I said that I'd protect Sakura, no matter what.

counterexamples.description: Kotomine’s safety and cooperation remain unsettled.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He wonders whether Kotomine is safe and expects his usual stance after Illya’s rescue.
counterexamples.explanation: Kotomine’s safety and cooperation remain unsettled.

contexts.japanese: 言峰の無事も気になるが、イリヤを助け出した今、あいつは元のスタンスに戻るだろう。
contexts.english: I wonder if Kotomine's safe, but now that I've rescued Illya, he'll probably go back to his usual stance.

counterexamples.description: Two-hour lapse retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He intended immediate return but two hours passed.
counterexamples.explanation: Two-hour lapse retained.

contexts.japanese: すぐに戻ってきたつもりだったが、あれから二時間も経っていた。
contexts.english: I meant to be right back, but it's been two hours.

counterexamples.description: Rin’s earlier arrival and briefing retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She arrived an hour earlier and heard the forest events from Illya.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin’s earlier arrival and briefing retained.

contexts.japanese: 「ほんの一時間前よ。森で何が起きたのかはイリヤから聞いたわ」
contexts.english: "Just an hour ago. Illya told me what happened in the forest."

counterexamples.description: Rin’s anger at being left behind retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The narrator infers the reason for her clear anger.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin’s anger at being left behind retained.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂を置いて森に行った事が気に食わないらしい。
contexts.english: She must be upset that we went to the forest without her.

counterexamples.description: Friendly banter triggers renewed lapse.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Relaxation from the exchange threatens concentration.
counterexamples.explanation: Friendly banter triggers renewed lapse.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂とイリヤの掛け合いで、緊張感が薄れてしまったようだ。
contexts.english: Tohsaka and Illya's banter threatened to relax my tension.

counterexamples.description: Resignation remains narrator’s uncertain reading.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He tentatively interprets her closing eyes as resignation.
counterexamples.explanation: Resignation remains narrator’s uncertain reading.

contexts.japanese: ……あれは諦め、だろうか。
contexts.english: ...In resignation, I think.

counterexamples.description: Illya’s altered hollow calm retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Narration marks a current unusual calm and emptiness like another person.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya’s altered hollow calm retained.

contexts.japanese: 今のイリヤは、どこか別人のような静けさと空虚さを持っていた。
contexts.english: Right now, Illya's displaying a hollow calm that makes her seem like a different person.

counterexamples.description: Absorbed souls prompt the objection.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Defeated Heroic Spirits are collected rather than disappearing.
counterexamples.explanation: Absorbed souls prompt the objection.

contexts.japanese: だが倒された英霊は消え去らず聖杯に取り込まれるのだ、と知った時、違和感は生まれてきた。
contexts.english: But when I learned that defeated Heroic Spirits are absorbed into the Holy Grail instead of disappearing, I started to have questions.

counterexamples.description: Masters as tools versus needed spirits retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Only Heroic Spirits are needed; Masters enable summoning.
counterexamples.explanation: Masters as tools versus needed spirits retained.

contexts.japanese: 「……つまり、聖杯戦争にとって必要なのは英霊だけで、マスターはただ、英霊を呼び寄せる為だけの道具だって事か……？」
contexts.english: "...You're saying that the Holy Grail War only needs the Heroic Spirits, and that the Masters are tools to summon them...?"

counterexamples.description: Magic versus magecraft and current attainability retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Current humans cannot realize it through any means, and magecraft cannot achieve it.
counterexamples.explanation: Magic versus magecraft and current attainability retained.

contexts.japanese: 魔術では到達できない神秘、あらゆる手段を以ってしても、現在の人間では届かない実現不可能の現象。
contexts.english: Mystics that magecraft can't achieve. Phenomena that current humans can't realize through any means.

counterexamples.description: Five recognized Magics retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Association recognition count is five.
counterexamples.explanation: Five recognized Magics retained.

contexts.japanese: 現在、魔術協会において認定されている魔法は五つ。
contexts.english: Currently, the Mage's Association recognizes five Magics.

counterexamples.description: Obtain Grail versus use Grail to go outside retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The ritual’s final purpose reverses the apparent prize contest.
counterexamples.explanation: Obtain Grail versus use Grail to go outside retained.

contexts.japanese: ……要するに、聖杯戦争とは聖杯を手に入れる為の戦いではなく、聖杯を用いて外に出る為の儀式だった。
contexts.english: ...In other words, the Holy Grail War ritual wasn't meant to obtain the Holy Grail, but to use it to go outside of the world.

counterexamples.description: Cosmological account retains report qualifiers.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Arcane studies say a pinnacle power exists outside the world.
counterexamples.explanation: Cosmological account retains report qualifiers.

contexts.japanese: 神秘学によると、この世界の外側には次元論の頂点に在るという“力”がある。
contexts.english: According to studies of the arcane, a power said to be the pinnacle of dimensional theory is located outside of this world.

counterexamples.description: Shirou deprioritizes ritual purpose for Sakura.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He explicitly declines the true-goal discussion as irrelevant to their immediate concern.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou deprioritizes ritual purpose for Sakura.

contexts.japanese: 「イリヤ。聖杯戦争の本当の目的とかはいい。イリヤの言ったとおり、それは俺たちには関係のない話だ。
contexts.english: "Illya. I don't care about the true goal of the Holy Grail War. You said yourself that it isn't relevant to us.

counterexamples.description: Sakura’s condition challenges the claimed path.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou asks whether her suffering would also count as Magic.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura’s condition challenges the claimed path.

contexts.japanese: ……だいたいな、そうでなかったら桜の事をどう説明するんだ。聖杯が魔法に至る道だっていうなら、桜があんな風になるのも魔法なのかよ」
contexts.english: ...Besides, how else would you explain Sakura? If the Holy Grail is a path to Magic, are you saying that what's happening to Sakura is Magic, too?"

counterexamples.description: Greater location versus human Lesser vessels retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He distinguishes the circle from Illya and Sakura while asking where the unknown entity is.
counterexamples.explanation: Greater location versus human Lesser vessels retained.

contexts.japanese: その何かっていうのが復讐者ってヤツなのか。そいつは聖杯……イリヤや桜の中じゃなく、大聖杯とかいう魔法陣の中にいると……？」
contexts.english: It's gotta be that Avenger thing you mentioned. Is it inside the Holy Grail? Not inside you or Sakura, but the Greater Grail?"

counterexamples.description: Source’s Persian devil account and nine-thousand-year span retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Narrator reports the source’s light-versus-evil conflict.
counterexamples.explanation: Source’s Persian devil account and nine-thousand-year span retained.

contexts.japanese: 拝火教における最大の悪魔であり、人間の善性を守護する光明神と九千年間戦い続けるという、悪性の容認者。
contexts.english: It's the greatest devil of Zoroastrianism—an advocate of evil that has been battling for nine thousand years against the light god safeguarding humanity's goodness.

counterexamples.description: If Illya is truthful limits inference.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou’s continued evil-bearing conclusion depends on her account being true.
counterexamples.explanation: If Illya is truthful limits inference.

contexts.japanese: イリヤの話が本当なら、アンリマユという英霊になったそいつは、今も人間の悪を背負い続けている事になる。
contexts.english: If what Illya is saying is true, the guy who became Aŋra Mainiiu would still bear the evil of humanity.

counterexamples.description: Revenge corrected to fulfilling imposed role.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He revises revenge into the duty wished by others and asks if Sakura is being used for it.
counterexamples.explanation: Revenge corrected to fulfilling imposed role.

contexts.japanese: 悪魔の名を冠したそいつは、自らを魔にしたてあげた人間への復讐……いや、人々が願った通りの役割をこなす為に、桜を利用しているというのか……？
contexts.english: Someone crowned with the name of a devil taking revenge on the people who turned him evil... No, is he using Sakura to carry out the duty that people wanted from him...?

counterexamples.description: Shirou derives Servant contract as rescue opening.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He asks if Sakura is contracted with the established entity.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou derives Servant contract as rescue opening.

contexts.japanese: つまり桜は、アヴェンジャーというサーヴァントと契約している、という事になるのか……？
contexts.english: Does that mean Sakura is contracted with Aŋra Mainiiu...?

counterexamples.description: Emergence threatens repeat of prior disaster.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If the entity comes out, the ten-years-earlier tragedy would recur.
counterexamples.explanation: Emergence threatens repeat of prior disaster.

contexts.japanese: そいつをこのまま外に出せば、十年前と同じ惨劇が起きてしまう。
contexts.english: If it comes out, it'll cause the same tragedy as ten years ago.

counterexamples.description: Preventing further burden on Sakura motivates action.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He refuses to let her bear more lives regardless of cost.
counterexamples.explanation: Preventing further burden on Sakura motivates action.

contexts.japanese: 何を犠牲にしても、これ以上桜に命を背負わせるコトは出来ない。
contexts.english: No matter the cost, I won't let Sakura shoulder the burden of any more lives.

counterexamples.description: Separation proposal preserves rescue distinction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He agrees to fight Sakura while proposing separation from Avenger.
counterexamples.explanation: Separation proposal preserves rescue distinction.

contexts.japanese: 「そうだな。桜と戦って、アンリマユを引き離す。それが一番の近道だし、方針として判り易い」
contexts.english: "Yeah. We'll fight Sakura and separate her from Aŋra Mainiiu. That's the fastest and simplest way."

counterexamples.description: Illya’s account conditions impossibility claim.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If Avenger is as she says, humans cannot oppose it after emergence.
counterexamples.explanation: Illya’s account conditions impossibility claim.

contexts.japanese: 「……今はそれしかないだろう。アンリマユとやらがイリヤが言う通りのモノなら、人間に太刀打ちできるものじゃない。そいつを外に出した時点で俺たちの負けだ。
contexts.english: "...We don't have a choice right now. If Aŋra Mainiiu is what Illya says it is, then there's nothing humans can do about it. Once it gets out, we've lost.

counterexamples.description: Right-hand pendant helps collect thoughts.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Cold touch stabilizes his planning after prolonged focus.
counterexamples.explanation: Right-hand pendant helps collect thoughts.

contexts.japanese: 右手に持ったペンダントの冷たい感触が、さっきの考えをより明確に纏めてくれる。
contexts.english: The cold touch of the pendant in my right hand helps me collect my thoughts.

counterexamples.description: Shirou intends survival despite agreeing to fight.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He means to finish the war with Sakura alive; Rin probably intends killing.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou intends survival despite agreeing to fight.

contexts.japanese: だが俺は、桜を生かす方法で戦いを終わらせて—
contexts.english: But I'm going to find a way to end this war and let her live—

counterexamples.description: Shadow pressure arrives before yard run.
