counterexamples.sourceReading: The separation is physical and temporary.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou enters while Saber remains under winter sky.

contexts.japanese: 冬の寒空の下、セイバーを一人残して教会へ踏み入った。
contexts.english: Saber remains alone under the cold winter sky as I enter the church.

counterexamples.description: A lone blond figure sits in the chapel.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei is absent.
counterexamples.explanation: A lone blond figure sits in the chapel.

contexts.japanese: その代わりといってはなんだが、椅子には一つだけ人影があった。
contexts.english: Instead, there's someone sitting in the pews.

counterexamples.description: Shirou politely asks the stranger for Father Kotomine.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No recognition occurs.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou politely asks the stranger for Father Kotomine.

contexts.japanese: 「すみません。言峰神父はいらっしゃいますか」
contexts.english: "Excuse me. Is Father Kotomine here?"

counterexamples.description: The man's ordinary approach is inexplicably threatening.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No overt attack has begun.
counterexamples.explanation: The man's ordinary approach is inexplicably threatening.

contexts.japanese: 何の変哲もないその動作は、あまりにも不可解だった。
contexts.english: There's nothing strange about how he moves, yet there's something I can't put my finger on.

counterexamples.description: The hand reaches toward Shirou's neck and stops midair.
counterexamples.sourceReading: No contact or killing occurs.
counterexamples.explanation: The hand reaches toward Shirou's neck and stops midair.

contexts.japanese: それは、ぼんやりと立ち尽くす俺の首に伸び—
contexts.english: As I freeze stiff, he slowly reaches for my neck...

counterexamples.description: The stranger says something unsavory is drawn to Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The target remains unnamed.
counterexamples.explanation: The stranger says something unsavory is drawn to Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 「—ほう。よくないモノに魅入られているな、おまえ」
contexts.english: "...Oh? Something rather unsavory has developed an attraction to you."

counterexamples.description: The stranger tells Shirou to wait for Kirei.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He disappears behind altar.
counterexamples.explanation: The stranger tells Shirou to wait for Kirei.

contexts.japanese: 「そこで待っていろ。言峰に用があるのだろう」
contexts.english: "Wait there. You seek Kotomine, yes?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei mockingly asks whether Shirou retires after half a day.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The greeting frames their antagonistic banter.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei mockingly asks whether Shirou retires after half a day.

contexts.japanese: 「驚いたな。まさか半日たらずでリタイヤかね、衛宮士郎」
contexts.english: "I'm surprised. To think you'd retire after only half a day, Shirou Emiya."

counterexamples.description: Kirei replies that he does not want Shirou becoming attached/dependent.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He mirrors the hostility.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei replies that he does not want Shirou becoming attached/dependent.

contexts.japanese: 「それは結構。私も暇ではないのでね、簡単に懐かれても困る」
contexts.english: "That is fine with me. I'm a busy man as well, so I wouldn't want you becoming dependent."

counterexamples.description: Kirei's presence forces awareness of Shirou's weakness.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The severe atmosphere is both priestly asset and defect.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's presence forces awareness of Shirou's weakness.

contexts.japanese: この男は、ただ立っているだけで己の弱さを意識させるような、厳格な雰囲気を持っている。
contexts.english: He gives off a severe air that makes me feel conscious of my flaws just by standing near him.

counterexamples.description: Kirei demands the question without pleasantries.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They are not friends.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei demands the question without pleasantries.

contexts.japanese: 「どうした？　質問があるのなら口にしろ。挨拶などする仲でもあるまい」
contexts.english: "And? State your question. We're hardly acquainted such that I feel a need to exchange pleasantries."

counterexamples.description: Shirou asks why Kirei concealed Kiritsugu's Master history.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The grievance is direct.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou asks why Kirei concealed Kiritsugu's Master history.

contexts.japanese: 「—切嗣の事だ。衛宮切嗣がマスターで、前回の聖杯戦争で戦ってたって事を、どうして黙っていた」
contexts.english: "About my old man. Why didn't you say that Kiritsugu Emiya was a Master in the last Holy Grail War?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei enjoys hearing Kiritsugu's name from Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He shows no shame.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei enjoys hearing Kiritsugu's name from Shirou.

contexts.japanese: ヤツに悪びれた様子はない。……この男は純粋に、俺の口から切嗣の名が出た事を楽しんでいる。
contexts.english: The priest doesn't show a hint of shame. In fact, he looks like he's enjoying hearing me say Kiritsugu's name.

counterexamples.description: Kirei argues Kiritsugu's deeds give Shirou no benefit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The claim separates inherited fame from present ability.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei argues Kiritsugu's deeds give Shirou no benefit.

contexts.japanese: 「何故も何もなかろう。おまえの父が前回のマスターであった事が、おまえにとってなんの益になる。衛宮切嗣の功績は衛宮士郎には無関係だ」
contexts.english: "There was hardly any reason to. How would knowing that your father was a Master benefit you? Kiritsugu Emiya's deeds are irrelevant to Shirou Emiya."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu raised Shirou as son and trained him as apprentice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Adoption and instruction coexist.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu raised Shirou as son and trained him as apprentice.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣の息子として育って、弟子として魔術を鍛えてきた。
contexts.english: Kiritsugu raised me as his son and trained me in magecraft as his apprentice.

counterexamples.description: Shirou argues Kiritsugu's history would have induced him to fight.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He treats omission as strategically surprising.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou argues Kiritsugu's history would have induced him to fight.

contexts.japanese: そんな説明より切嗣の事を言えば、俺はアンタの思い通り戦うと決めた筈だ。それを、どうして口にしなかった」
contexts.english: But if you had told me about Kiritsugu, then I would willingly fight in the war, just like you want. Why didn't you mention it?"

counterexamples.description: Kirei rejects known genetic succession because Shirou is not biological son.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He does not deny adoptive relation.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei rejects known genetic succession because Shirou is not biological son.

contexts.japanese: 遺伝によるマスターの継承など知らぬし、そもそもおまえは切嗣の息子ではあるまい。
contexts.english: I know of no genetic succession of Masterhood, and to begin with, you aren't Kiritsugu's blood-related son.

counterexamples.description: Shirou is exceptional because he lacked Grail knowledge and preparation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says he does not know why he was chosen.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou is exceptional because he lacked Grail knowledge and preparation.

contexts.japanese: 「本来、いかに魔術師であろうと聖杯を知らぬ者に令呪は宿らん。その例外であるおまえが選ばれた理由など、私の知るところではない」
contexts.english: "Normally, the Command Spells would not be bestowed upon someone who is ignorant of the Holy Grail, even if he is a mage. I don't know why an exception like you would occur."

counterexamples.description: Shirou seeks confirmation that rescue was pure goodwill.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The clause remains his formulation.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou seeks confirmation that rescue was pure goodwill.

contexts.japanese: ただ、純粋な善意で、死のうとしていた子供を助けただけだった、と。
contexts.english: ...sheer goodwill, because he wanted to save a dying child?

counterexamples.description: Kirei qualifies his answer as only what he knows.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He proposes Grail causation without certainty.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei qualifies his answer as only what he knows.

contexts.japanese: 「私が知る限りではな。だが聖杯の思惑となると、私には計り知れん。衛宮士郎がマスターに選ばれた事は偶然と切り捨てたいところだが、少なからず因果を感じる。
contexts.english: "As far as I know. But I cannot divine the will of the Holy Grail. As much as I'd like to dismiss your selection as random chance, I feel some karmic connection at work.

counterexamples.description: Kirei says Kiritsugu destroyed the Grail to end the war.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Betrayal is Kirei's personified framing.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei says Kiritsugu destroyed the Grail to end the war.

contexts.japanese: ヤツは最後の最後で聖杯を破壊した。聖杯戦争そのものを終わらせる為に、ヤツに期待を寄せた聖杯と、その宿願を裏切ったのだ」
contexts.english: In the last possible moment, he destroyed it. He turned on his own wish, on the grail's expectations, in order to end the Holy Grail War."

counterexamples.description: Shirou rejects betrayal and sees destruction as ending conflict.
counterexamples.sourceReading: This is his idealized judgment.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou rejects betrayal and sees destruction as ending conflict.

contexts.japanese: それを破壊した切嗣は、裏切ってなんかいない。
contexts.english: The old man didn't betray anything by destroying it.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu remains Shirou's champion of justice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The conclusion is filial admiration.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu remains Shirou's champion of justice.

contexts.japanese: 切嗣は切嗣のまま、俺が憧れ続けた正義の味方として聖杯戦争を終わらせたんだ。
contexts.english: Kiritsugu ended the war by staying true to himself and doing the right thing, by being the champion of justice I've always looked up to.

counterexamples.description: Kirei offers the earlier Kiritsugu as correction.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He marks the story wasteful but pleasurable.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei offers the earlier Kiritsugu as correction.

contexts.japanese: —いいだろう。無駄な話だが、衛宮切嗣の正体を教えてやる」
contexts.english: ...Very well. Perhaps this is a waste of time, but I will tell you who that man truly was."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu sought a miracle beyond his own power.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The ideal is beyond human realization.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu sought a miracle beyond his own power.

contexts.japanese: 自身の力では叶わない奇跡。
contexts.english: He sought a miracle his own powers could not achieve.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's weakness betraying everything is retained.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says the weakness ultimately made him betray all invested hopes and his own wish.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's weakness betraying everything is retained.

contexts.japanese: 「だが、そこまでして結局—その弱さが、ヤツに全てを裏切らせた。
contexts.english: "But in going to such extremes, his weakness betrayed everything he had:

counterexamples.description: The one-for-ten sacrifice rule remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kiritsugu personally and promptly sacrifices one when required to save ten.
counterexamples.explanation: The one-for-ten sacrifice rule remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 人死にを許さぬくせに、人を助ける為に自らの手で人を殺す。十の命を生かす為に一の犠牲が必要とされるなら、速やかに自らの手で事を成した」
contexts.english: He could not abide death, yet he would kill others to save people. If a single life had to be sacrificed to save ten, then he would make that sacrifice without hesitation."

counterexamples.description: Kirei's deliberately provocative Anti-Hero gloss survives.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He first gives the literal opposite-of-hero framing and calls it an incorrigible killer.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's deliberately provocative Anti-Hero gloss survives.

contexts.japanese: 「字の如しだが？　英雄の反対、度し難い殺人者という意味だ」
contexts.english: "Does the word not explain itself? It is the opposite of a hero: an incorrigible killer."

counterexamples.description: Kirei's mixed reaction to reliance by his enemy's son remains comic and unsettled.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He welcomes Shirou yet cannot settle whether to rejoice or grieve at being relied upon by Kiritsugu's son.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's mixed reaction to reliance by his enemy's son remains comic and unsettled.

contexts.japanese: 「なんと。誤解があるようだが、私はおまえを歓迎しているぞ？　なにしろ切嗣の息子だ。仇敵の息子に頼りにされてみろ。喜ぶべきか悲しむべきか、複雑すぎて心が定まらん」
contexts.english: "Perish the thought. Lest you misunderstand, I welcome you. You are his son, after all. The child of my nemesis is coming to me for help. Should I rejoice or lament? My feelings are so mixed I can hardly bear it."

counterexamples.description: Shirou rejects heroism as a wish-granted office.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A hero is what one has become after events are over, not something one sets out to become; the Grail supplies disproportionate power.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou rejects heroism as a wish-granted office.

contexts.japanese: 「そ、そんなの知るかっ！　とにかく違うものは違うんだ。それにな、英雄なんてのはなるものじゃなくて、終わった後になってるもんだろ。聖杯が用意できるものなんて、結局分不相応の力だけじゃないのか」
contexts.english: "I-I don't know! But I know they're different. Plus, a hero isn't something you try to be, but someone you become after everything's over. All the Holy Grail can do is give you power beyond your means, right?"

counterexamples.description: Shirou notices that Kirei has never belittled Kiritsugu.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Despite saying many hostile things, Kirei has not once spoken slightingly of him.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou notices that Kirei has never belittled Kiritsugu.

contexts.japanese: 色々言ってるけど、切嗣を一度もけなしていない。
contexts.english: He's said a lot of stuff about Kiritsugu, but none of it belittled him.

counterexamples.description: The conflict-free world remains impossible on earth.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says such a world does not exist here and Kiritsugu sought the Grail to reject that fact.
counterexamples.explanation: The conflict-free world remains impossible on earth.

contexts.japanese: “争いのない世界”は地上には存在しない。ヤツはそれを否定する為に聖杯を求めた」
contexts.english: A world without conflict does not exist on this earth. He sought out the Holy Grail because he could not abide that fact."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's dream remains impossible even through the impossible Grail.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His dream is magic that cannot come true except through the impossible thing called the Grail, and still ought not be realizable.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's dream remains impossible even through the impossible Grail.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮切嗣という男の夢は、聖杯という“あり得ないもの”でしか叶わない、叶う筈のない魔法だった」
contexts.english: The dream of Kiritsugu Emiya was an impossible, magical idea that only an impossible device like the Holy Grail could make come true."

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's betrayal follows admission into the guarded lineage.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The family endures lost ownership and breaks blood unity to invite an outsider, who betrays the Grail.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's betrayal follows admission into the guarded lineage.

contexts.japanese: その結果が聖杯の所有権を奪われ、一参加者として競争しあうという体たらくだ。その屈辱に耐え、守り通した血の結束を破ってまで外来の魔術師を招き入れたというのに、その男は聖杯を前にして、あろうことか聖杯を裏切った」
contexts.english: As a result: they lost claim of ownership over the Holy Grail and were reduced to fighting their rivals for it. They bore that humiliation and even invited an outsider to contaminate their lineage. Then, when that man was within arm's reach of the prize, he betrayed his benefactors."

counterexamples.description: Shirou connects Illya's attack to Kiritsugu's betrayal.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He concludes it is natural that the girl targeted him first.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou connects Illya's attack to Kiritsugu's betrayal.

contexts.japanese: あの子が真っ先に俺を狙いに来たのは当然だ。
contexts.english: No wonder she went straight for me.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's fighting purpose remains prevention of another fire.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Whatever Masters think, he fights so the event ten years ago will not recur.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's fighting purpose remains prevention of another fire.

contexts.japanese: 「—削がれてなんかない。理由はどうあれ、俺は戦うと決めたんだ。他のマスターが何を考えようが、十年前のような事は起こさせない」
contexts.english: "Yeah, right. No matter the story behind this war, I've made up my mind. Whatever the other Masters are planning, I won't let them repeat what happened ten years ago."

counterexamples.description: Sakura's fever remains a simile.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She spaces out as though suffering a fever.
counterexamples.explanation: Sakura's fever remains a simile.

contexts.japanese: 元気がなくなって、熱病にかかったようにぼんやりとしていた。
contexts.english: She didn't have much energy, and was spacing out like she had a fever.

counterexamples.description: Shirou distinguishes stopping Masters from defeating them.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber sees Rin as an enemy to defeat; Shirou wants Masters stopped.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou distinguishes stopping Masters from defeating them.

contexts.japanese: だが俺にとって、マスターは止めるものであって倒すものじゃない。
contexts.english: To me, though, the others need to be stopped, but not defeated.

counterexamples.description: Surrender and Command Spell exhaustion remain Shirou's policy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If Master and Servant surrender, fighting stops; he intends to exhaust Command Spells.
counterexamples.explanation: Surrender and Command Spell exhaustion remain Shirou's policy.

contexts.japanese: 「セイバー。確認するが、マスターとサーヴァントが降伏した時は戦いを止める。俺の方針は令呪を使い切らせてマスターでなくす事だ。　……本当に、それでいいな？」
contexts.english: "Just to be sure we're on the same page... Saber, if a Master and their Servant surrender, stop. I want to force the other Masters to use up their Command Spells. Are you all right with that?"

counterexamples.description: The patrol choice remains unresolved at the branch point.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou considers Miyama versus Shinto.
counterexamples.explanation: The patrol choice remains unresolved at the branch point.

contexts.japanese: —深山町を巡回するか、新都を巡回するか。
contexts.english: Should we patrol nearby Miyama, or Shinto across the bridge?

counterexamples.description: The sensed event remains both a scream and magical aftereffect.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou identifies a scream and wake of strong mana.
counterexamples.explanation: The sensed event remains both a scream and magical aftereffect.

contexts.japanese: だが、今のは間違いなく誰かの悲鳴であり、強い魔力の余波だった。
contexts.english: But it was unmistakably a scream accompanied by a strong wave of magical energy.

counterexamples.description: Being attacked and initiating attack remain opposed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou may be used to attack but not attacking first.
counterexamples.explanation: Being attacked and initiating attack remain opposed.

contexts.japanese: だから動けない。襲われる事には慣れても、自分から襲う事に慣れていない。
contexts.english: So I can't move. I may be used to being attacked, but I'm not used to going on the attack.

counterexamples.description: Running does not complete Shirou's resolve.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He is unprepared and his legs shake as he runs.
counterexamples.explanation: Running does not complete Shirou's resolve.

contexts.japanese: 覚悟は出来ていない。
contexts.english: I'm not ready.

counterexamples.description: The mental lock remains a simile tied to circuit activation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou locks his heart as he would put a circuit pseudo-nerve into his back.
counterexamples.explanation: The mental lock remains a simile tied to circuit activation.

contexts.japanese: 背中に魔術回路を入れるように、心に鍵をかけて新都へ歩き出した。
contexts.english: I steel myself as we walk, just like I do when I insert the pseudo-nerve of a Magic Circuit into my back.

counterexamples.description: The Shinto patrol lasts about one hour.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They spend roughly an hour patrolling without visible anomaly.
counterexamples.explanation: The Shinto patrol lasts about one hour.

contexts.japanese: 一時間ほど新都を巡回した。
contexts.english: We spend about an hour patrolling Shinto.

counterexamples.description: Saber asks for orders and presents rescue as possible.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She does not know what happened but says Shirou's order may permit rescue.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber asks for orders and presents rescue as possible.

contexts.japanese: 「マスター、指示を。何が起きたかは判りませんが、敵はすぐ近くにいる。貴方の指示次第では、悲鳴をあげた人間を助ける事も出来る筈です」
contexts.english: "Your orders, Master. I don't know what just happened, but the enemy is nearby. If you command it, we can help whoever was just attacked."

counterexamples.description: The contaminated-mana simile remains a clear stream fouled by oil.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou compares the ominous dense energy to heavy oil in clear water.
counterexamples.explanation: The contaminated-mana simile remains a clear stream fouled by oil.

contexts.japanese: 清流の中に重油が流れているようなもの。
contexts.english: It's like an oil spill in the middle of a clear stream.

counterexamples.description: Vampire remains an analogy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The sight is like seeing a legendary vampire.
counterexamples.explanation: Vampire remains an analogy.

contexts.japanese: ……伝説に言う吸血鬼を見るようだった。
contexts.english: ...It was like seeing a vampire out of folktales.

counterexamples.description: Rider drains mind and memory rather than flesh.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou perceives the victim's inner human contents being sucked up.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider drains mind and memory rather than flesh.

contexts.japanese: あの黒い装束の女は、人間の中身—精神とか記憶とか、そういったモノを吸い上げている。
contexts.english: The woman in black was sucking on a person's entire being: her victim's mind and memories.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's lack of threat response is framed as failing reason.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A Servant he should flee does not feel threatening because his reason is nearly gone.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's lack of threat response is framed as failing reason.

contexts.japanese: 俺よりずっと強い存在、全力で逃げなくてはいけないサーヴァントが目の前にいるっていうのに、まったく脅威を感じない。
contexts.english: Something far stronger than me—a Servant I should do everything in my power to flee from—is right in front of me, and it doesn't feel threatening at all.

counterexamples.description: The victim may still be saved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou thinks haste may save the woman.
counterexamples.explanation: The victim may still be saved.

contexts.japanese: 急げばあの女性は助かるかもしれない。
contexts.english: If I hurry, I might be able to save this woman.

counterexamples.description: Rider's response to Shinji's hostility remains tentative.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou wonders whether she took the look as an order.
counterexamples.explanation: Rider's response to Shinji's hostility remains tentative.

contexts.japanese: それを命令と取ったのか、黒いサーヴァントの体が沈み—
contexts.english: As if taking that as a signal, the black-clad Servant sinks to the ground, and—

counterexamples.description: Saber initially appears unable to match Rider's speed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She plants and guards while Rider moves rapidly.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber initially appears unable to match Rider's speed.

contexts.japanese: セイバーは敵のスピードについていけず、ただ足を止めて守りを固めている。
contexts.english: She can't keep up with her opponent's speed, so she plants her feet and solidifies her guard.

counterexamples.description: The bat and sandbag metaphor survives in full.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber is batter and Rider the sandbag sent flying.
counterexamples.explanation: The bat and sandbag metaphor survives in full.

contexts.japanese: バットでサンドバッグをかっ飛ばすかのような豪快さ。
contexts.english: It's as magnificent as sending a sandbag flying with a bat.

contexts.japanese: 無論バッターはセイバーで、吹っ飛ばされたサンドバッグがライダーである。
contexts.english: The batter in this case is Saber, while the sandbag is Rider.

counterexamples.description: Shinji and Shirou look at different subjects after the reversal.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shinji stares at wounded Rider while Shirou watches bored Saber sheathe or lower her sword.
counterexamples.explanation: Shinji and Shirou look at different subjects after the reversal.

contexts.japanese: 慎二は呆然と傷ついたライダーを見つめ、
contexts.english: Shinji stares at the wounded Rider in shock.

contexts.japanese: 俺は愕然と、つまらなそうに剣を納めたセイバーを見つめてしまった。
contexts.english: Astonished, I watch as Saber lowers her sword with a bored expression.

counterexamples.description: Saber offers surrender under Shirou's policy.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Though unwilling to ask, she follows her Master's word and asks for discarded Command Spells and admitted defeat.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber offers surrender under Shirou's policy.

contexts.japanese: 我が主の言葉に従い、訊きたくはないが降伏の意思を訊ねる。令呪を破棄し、敗北を認めるか」
contexts.english: As much as it pains me to say it, my Master offers you a chance to surrender. Will you forfeit your Command Spells and admit defeat?"

counterexamples.description: Saber grants conversation without yielding the route.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She moves slightly but keeps blocking passage.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber grants conversation without yielding the route.

contexts.japanese: 道は譲らないが、老人と向き合うだけの機会をくれた、という事だろう。
contexts.english: She's giving me a chance to speak to him, but she isn't going to let me pass.

counterexamples.description: Shirou directly asks whether Sakura is also a Master.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His concern shifts from the name lecture to Sakura.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou directly asks whether Sakura is also a Master.

contexts.japanese: 「—じゃあ。桜は—桜も、慎二と同じようにマスターなのか」
contexts.english: "Then, Sakura... Is Sakura a Master like Shinji?"

counterexamples.description: Shirou's relief rests on what he has just been told.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He feels Sakura need not enter the killing contest.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's relief rests on what he has just been told.

contexts.japanese: それでも、桜がこんな殺し合いに関わらなくていいのだ、と今は素直に安堵できる。
contexts.english: Still, I can rest easy knowing that Sakura won't be involved in any deathmatches.

counterexamples.description: Apparent bodily shrinking is immediately corrected.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Silent backward motion created the illusion.
counterexamples.explanation: Apparent bodily shrinking is immediately corrected.

contexts.japanese: 老人の体が縮む。
contexts.english: The old man's body shrinks.

contexts.japanese: いや、足音もたてずに後ろに引いたため、そう錯覚させられただけだ。
contexts.english: No, it just seems that way, because he backed up without making a sound.

counterexamples.description: Church treatment remains an expectation, not a shown cure.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou thinks Kirei should be able to do something if they hurry.
counterexamples.explanation: Church treatment remains an expectation, not a shown cure.

contexts.japanese: 「教会に行くぞセイバー。まだ間に合う。あいつならなんとか出来るはずだ」
contexts.english: "Let's go to the church, Saber. We can still make it. He'll know what to do."

counterexamples.description: Saber leads and Shirou runs at full speed behind her.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She tells him to stay close; he tries not to be left.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber leads and Shirou runs at full speed behind her.

contexts.japanese: 「先行します。離れずに付いて来てください」
contexts.english: "I'll lead the way. Follow me, and stay close."

contexts.japanese: その速さに引き離されぬよう、こっちも全力で走り出した。
contexts.english: I run as fast as I can, trying not to get left behind.

counterexamples.description: Saber's debt and severe self-appraisal remain explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She will not let Shirou die before repaying responsibility and says she has not helped once.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's debt and severe self-appraisal remain explicit.

contexts.japanese: 「傷を見せてくださいシロウっ。昨夜の傷は私にも責任がある。その責を返さないまま貴方を死なせる訳にはいかない。私はまだサーヴァントとして一度も貴方の助けになっていないのです、こんな事で契約を破棄する事など許容できない……！」
contexts.english: "Show me your injuries, Shirou. It's partly my fault you were hurt. I cannot let you die without repaying that debt. I still haven't helped you even once as a Servant. I refuse to let our contract end this way!"

counterexamples.description: Shirou counts two prior rescues against Saber's self-judgment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He recalls Lancer and her attempt to let him escape Berserker.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou counts two prior rescues against Saber's self-judgment.

contexts.japanese: ランサーから俺を助けてくれた事、バーサーカーを前にして俺を逃がそうとしてくれた事。
contexts.english: I recall how she saved me from Lancer, and how she tried to buy me time to get away from Berserker.

contexts.japanese: 二度も命を救っておいて、彼女はそれを助けと考えない。
contexts.english: She's saved my life twice over, and she still thinks she hasn't helped me.

counterexamples.description: Shirou regrets only the accidental beginning.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He wishes he had intentionally taken Saber's hand from the start.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou regrets only the accidental beginning.

contexts.japanese: 「ただの偶然だけどな。……うん。だからまあ、今はそれが悔しい。初めから、ちゃんと自分の意志でセイバーの手を取りたかった」
contexts.english: "Only by coincidence. It's too bad. I wish I could've reached out to you like I meant it."

counterexamples.description: The renewed alliance is reciprocal.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou asks for help; Saber says she also needs his aid.
counterexamples.explanation: The renewed alliance is reciprocal.

contexts.japanese: 「これから一緒に戦ってくれるか。俺にはセイバーの助けが必要だ」
contexts.english: "Will you fight with me? I need your help, Saber."

contexts.japanese: 「—それに助けが必要なのはお互い様です。
contexts.english: "...And I will require your aid, as well.

counterexamples.description: Saber retains her own Grail objective.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She borrows Shirou's power to obtain the Grail and promises power matching trust.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber retains her own Grail objective.

contexts.japanese: 聖杯を手に入れる為に、私は貴方の力を借りる。貴方が信頼してくれるのなら、私はその心に見合う力を振いましょう」
contexts.english: I will borrow your power to obtain the Holy Grail. If you trust me, then I will show you power worthy of that faith."

counterexamples.description: Half a day since the opening night remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The alliance realization occurs half a day after the beginning night.
counterexamples.explanation: Half a day since the opening night remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 始まりの夜から半日過ぎた今。
contexts.english: It's been half a day since the night when this all started.

counterexamples.description: Night patrol is a plan awaiting nightfall.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They decide to wait for night and then go into town.
counterexamples.explanation: Night patrol is a plan awaiting nightfall.

contexts.japanese: —夜を待って街に出る。
contexts.english: We wait for nightfall, then head out into town.

counterexamples.description: Mana residue remains an indirect clue.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Patrolling for traces may yield clues to other Masters.
counterexamples.explanation: Mana residue remains an indirect clue.

contexts.japanese: それを頼りに街を巡回していれば、他のマスターの手がかりぐらいは得られるだろう。
contexts.english: If I canvass the city looking for those traces, then I might find clues leading to the other Masters.

counterexamples.description: Saber's permission is conditional on joint movement.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She demands a promise never to go out alone at night.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's permission is conditional on joint movement.

contexts.japanese: 『……判りました。では、必ず私と共に行動すると約束してください。夜中、一人では決して外に出る事はしないと誓えますか？』
contexts.english: "...Very well. But promise me that you will act with me at all times. Will you swear not to venture outside alone at night?"

counterexamples.description: The energy scale retains its key values.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Recovery eight, maintenance six, reserve two, Lancer fifty and Berserker two hundred.
counterexamples.explanation: The energy scale retains its key values.

contexts.japanese: セイバーの一日の魔力回復量が８だとすると、肉体維持に必要な魔力は６。んで、余剰の２が貯められる貯金になる。
contexts.english: You recover eight points of magical energy a day, and it takes six to maintain your body. That leaves two in reserve.

contexts.japanese: シロウ風に言うのなら、ランサーとの戦いに五十、バーサーカーとの戦いにいたっては二百ほど魔力を消費しました」
contexts.english: To use your terms, I spent fifty points in my skirmish with Lancer, and two hundred fighting Berserker."

counterexamples.description: Current reserve is about one thousand, not a maximum.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber gives an approximate present quantity in Shirou's scale.
counterexamples.explanation: Current reserve is about one thousand, not a maximum.

contexts.japanese: 「シロウ風に言うのなら、一千ほどですが」
contexts.english: "In your terms, about a thousand points."

counterexamples.description: Shirou cannot tell why Saber is angry.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Possible reasons are burdening her or delaying her sleep.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou cannot tell why Saber is angry.

contexts.japanese: それがマスターとしてセイバーに負担をかけていることになのか、
contexts.english: I'm not sure if it's because her incompetent Master is a burden to her,

contexts.japanese: それとも睡眠をとるというセイバーを押し止めていることに対してなのか、判別がつかない。
contexts.english: or if it's because I'm not letting her get a good night's rest.

counterexamples.description: The mana problem remains unsolved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: They can only understand the current situation, not fix supply.
counterexamples.explanation: The mana problem remains unsolved.

contexts.japanese: もとより俺たちではどうしようもない問題だし、解決策は現状を把握するぐらいしかない。
contexts.english: It isn't something we have a solution for, so the next step is to get a firm grasp on our situation.

counterexamples.description: Saber is included in the surprised silence.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou wonders why even Saber looks surprised.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber is included in the surprised silence.

contexts.japanese: 藤ねえと桜が黙り込むのは判るのだが、なんでおまえまでそんな意外そうな顔してるんだ、セイバー。
contexts.english: I can understand Fuji-nee and Sakura's reaction, but why does Saber look so surprised?

counterexamples.description: Archery does not prove brute strength.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou reassures himself then immediately notes a bow is not drawn by strength alone.
counterexamples.explanation: Archery does not prove brute strength.

contexts.japanese: よしよし、弓を引いてるんだから気にするまでもなかったか。
contexts.english: She can pull a bowstring, after all, so I shouldn't have worried.

contexts.japanese: 「ま、弓だって力だけで引くわけじゃないけどな」
contexts.english: "Though there's more to archery than pulling a bowstring..."

counterexamples.description: Rin's nursing remains Shirou's recollection.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He remembers she cared for him after Berserker.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's nursing remains Shirou's recollection.

contexts.japanese: バーサーカーとの一件のあと、倒れた俺を看病してくれたのは遠坂だ。
contexts.english: Tohsaka took care of me after I collapsed during the Berserker fight.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's account remains a cover story.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He calls the injury a foolish accident and Rin a passerby who treated him.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's account remains a cover story.

contexts.japanese: その、つまんないドジでケガしちまってさ。偶然通りがかった遠坂が親切にも手当てしてくれたんだよ。さすが我が校の誇る優等生。慈愛に満ちてるってもんだ」
contexts.english: Um, I was stupid and got myself hurt. Tohsaka was passing by and was kind enough to give me first aid. She really is the gracious star student of our school, huh."

counterexamples.description: Shirou has no immediate response to Sakura's outburst.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The sudden change leaves him unable to find words.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou has no immediate response to Sakura's outburst.

contexts.japanese: 突然の事に、かける言葉が見当たらない。
contexts.english: It's so sudden, I don't know what to say.

counterexamples.description: Only Shirou enters with the patient.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber hands the woman over outside and Kirei carries her into his back room.
counterexamples.explanation: Only Shirou enters with the patient.

contexts.japanese: 教会前でセイバーから女性を預かり、一人で礼拝堂に入る。
contexts.english: Saber hands the unconscious victim over to me in front of the church, and I take her inside.

contexts.japanese: 大声で言峰を呼ぶと、あいつは衰弱した女性の姿を見るなり、女性を抱きかかえて奥に引っ込んでしまった。
contexts.english: I call loudly for Kotomine, who comes out, takes one look at the victim, and carries her into a back room.

counterexamples.description: Outcome remains dependent on Kirei while Shirou waits.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou trusts him and cannot do more.
counterexamples.explanation: Outcome remains dependent on Kirei while Shirou waits.

contexts.japanese: あの女の人が助かるかどうかは言峰次第だ。
contexts.english: It's up to Kotomine whether she'll pull through.

contexts.japanese: 今は言峰を信じて、こうして結果を待ち続けるしかない。
contexts.english: I just have to trust him and wait for the outcome.

counterexamples.description: Shirou questions his right to oppose ancient claimants.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He compares himself with families pursuing the Grail for centuries.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou questions his right to oppose ancient claimants.

contexts.japanese: アインツベルンやマキリのように、
contexts.english: Do I really have the right to fight in the same war as the Einzberns and Makiris,

contexts.japanese: 何百年も前から求め続けた連中と、肩を並べて争う権利があるのかどうか—
contexts.english: who have been chasing their goal for hundreds of years...?

counterexamples.description: Successful treatment is initially only Shirou's inference.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He reads Kirei's non-grim face and wonders if it went well.
counterexamples.explanation: Successful treatment is initially only Shirou's inference.

contexts.japanese: なら、治療は上手くいったという事だろうか。
contexts.english: That must mean the treatment went well.

counterexamples.description: The prognosis remains partly unresolved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei says she stabilized but the rest depends on her.
counterexamples.explanation: The prognosis remains partly unresolved.

contexts.japanese: 「持ち直しはした。後は本人次第だ。ここに連れてくるのが半時ほど遅ければ、今ごろは本職に戻らねばならなかったが」
contexts.english: "I've done what I can. The rest depends on her. If you'd brought her even a half hour later, I would have had to perform the rites of my actual occupation."

counterexamples.description: Kirei's regret remains uncertain.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He closes his mouth as if rueful, and Shirou cannot judge sincerity.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's regret remains uncertain.

contexts.japanese: どこまで本気なのか、神父は悔いるように口を閉ざす。
contexts.english: The priest seems rueful, but I can't tell how sincere he is.

counterexamples.description: Shirou admits the known Master because he cannot bear it alone.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He calls the disclosure a weak complaint.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou admits the known Master because he cannot bear it alone.

contexts.japanese: 自分ひとりでは耐え切れず、そう、泣き言を呟いていた。
contexts.english: I murmur pitifully, unable to keep it to myself.

counterexamples.description: Defeated does not become killed.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei asks whether Shirou defeated the known Master.
counterexamples.explanation: Defeated does not become killed.

contexts.japanese: 「当然倒したのだろうな、衛宮士郎」
contexts.english: "And you defeated him, of course."

counterexamples.description: Future action remains the place to test carried guilt.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei tells him to question what he does next and interpret past tragedy himself.
counterexamples.explanation: Future action remains the place to test carried guilt.

contexts.japanese: それでも罪を背負いたいのならば、これからの自身の行いに問うがいい。既に起きた惨事をどう捉えるかはおまえ次第だ」
contexts.english: If you must shoulder your sins, then question your next actions. Only you can decide how to face the tragedies of the past."

counterexamples.description: Shirou centers his next choice.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Bloodlines and obsessions recede behind what he will decide.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou centers his next choice.

contexts.japanese: 大事なのは、これから自分がどうするのか、という決断だけ。
contexts.english: What matters are the choices I make next.

counterexamples.description: The treatment fee is listening, not money.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kirei demands attention to brief advice as payment.
counterexamples.explanation: The treatment fee is listening, not money.

contexts.japanese: 「なに、すぐに済む。こんな夜更けに治療をしてやったのだ。治療代として話に付き合え」
contexts.english: "It won't take long. I've already gone through the trouble of healing your charge in the middle of the night, so consider this your fee and listen."

counterexamples.description: Kirei identifies an unspoken hesitation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou dislikes how accurately the priest names it.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei identifies an unspoken hesitation.

contexts.japanese: 何も言ってないってのに、こっちの迷いを的確に言い当てやがる。
contexts.english: I haven't even said anything yet, but he hits me right where I'm most uncertain.

counterexamples.description: Shirou cannot tell whether Kirei is sarcastic.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The priest speaks pleasantly while offering brutal advice.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou cannot tell whether Kirei is sarcastic.

contexts.japanese: それが皮肉なのかどうかは分からない。
contexts.english: I can't tell if he's being sarcastic or not.

counterexamples.description: Rin's condemnation remains imagined.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou predicts what she would say if she heard Kirei.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's condemnation remains imagined.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂が聞いたら、アンタなんか初めっから神父失格よ、なんて言うに決まってる。
contexts.english: If Tohsaka heard that, she'd say he's always been a failure.

counterexamples.description: Shirou leaves with audible irritation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He snorts and makes rough loud footsteps.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou leaves with audible irritation.

contexts.japanese: ふん、と鼻を鳴らして出口に向かう。
contexts.english: I snort, turn on my heel, and march out of the church.

contexts.japanese: カンカンと乱暴に足音をたてて、今度こそ礼拝堂を後にした。
contexts.english: This time, I really do leave, announcing it with loud and forceful footsteps.

counterexamples.description: Credit for rescue passes between partners.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou credits Saber; she credits his choice and her compliance.
counterexamples.explanation: Credit for rescue passes between partners.

contexts.japanese: 「—あの人、助かったよ。セイバーのおかげだ」
contexts.english: "She's going to be all right. It's all thanks to you, Saber."

contexts.japanese: 「礼には及びません。あの女性を助けようとしたのはシロウです。私は貴方の方針に従っただけですから」
contexts.english: "I require no thanks. You're the one who saved that woman, Shirou. I merely accepted your decision."

counterexamples.description: The fight-and-death counterfactual remains Shirou's reasoning.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He thinks stopping Zouken would cause battle and kill the patient.
counterexamples.explanation: The fight-and-death counterfactual remains Shirou's reasoning.

contexts.japanese: あそこであの老人を止めていたら、間違いなく戦いになった。そうなればあの女性は確実に衰弱死していた。
contexts.english: If we'd stopped the old man from leaving, there would have been another fight. The woman was in critical condition, and wouldn't have made it.

contexts.japanese: セイバーはそれを考慮して、間桐臓硯を見逃したんだ。
contexts.english: Saber must have had that in mind when she let Zouken go.

counterexamples.description: Saber reserves judgment when Shirou is endangered.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She says she only promised to prioritize her own decision then.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber reserves judgment when Shirou is endangered.

contexts.japanese: 「そ、そんな顔はしていませんっ！　マスターの身に危険が迫った時は私の判断を優先する、と言っただけではないですかっ。それをそうかぁ？　などとよく言えたものですね、シロウは」
contexts.english: "N-no I wasn't! I simply said that I would prioritize my own decisions if you were in danger! Don't give me that tone, Shirou!"

counterexamples.description: Shirou's earlier halfheartedness remains lack of a personal Grail wish.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He intended Saber to receive the Grail if they remained.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's earlier halfheartedness remains lack of a personal Grail wish.

contexts.japanese: 「俺はセイバーみたいに聖杯が必要って訳じゃなかった。
contexts.english: "Unlike you, I don't need the Holy Grail.

contexts.japanese: 戦いを終わらせて、最後まで残れたら聖杯はセイバーに貰ってほしい、なんて思ってた。そんな半端な自分で、セイバーは本当にいいのかって迷いがあった」
contexts.english: I was thinking that we'd end the war and give the Grail to you if we survive. I wasn't confident that my half-hearted conviction made me good enough to be your partner, Saber."

counterexamples.description: The night's fight does not make Shirou accept the war.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He still rejects it but commits to fight through.
counterexamples.explanation: The night's fight does not make Shirou accept the war.

contexts.japanese: 「いや、これが全然。まだ聖杯戦争には納得できてない。
contexts.english: "Not at all. I still don't accept this Holy Grail War.

contexts.japanese: —けど、必ず最後まで戦う。
contexts.english: ...But, I'll fight until the end.

counterexamples.description: Saber's oath retains worthiness as a condition.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She is his sword only while he is a fitting Master.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's oath retains worthiness as a condition.

contexts.japanese: 貴方が私の主として相応しい限り、この身は貴方の剣となる。シロウがシロウである限り—その期待を、決して裏切る事はありません」
contexts.english: As long you are worthy of my service, I swear to be your sword. Remain true to yourself, Shirou...and I will never betray you."

counterexamples.description: Shirou resolves to live up to Saber's trust.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He will hold fast to the self she believes in.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou resolves to live up to Saber's trust.

contexts.japanese: ならこっちも精一杯胸を張ろう。
contexts.english: I need to do everything I can to live up to that trust.

contexts.japanese: 彼女が信じてくれた自分を最後まで張り通せるよう。
contexts.english: To stay true to the person that she thinks I am.

counterexamples.description: The recap preserves the school battle as last night's starting point.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou lacked time to think after witnessing Lancer and Archer.
counterexamples.explanation: The recap preserves the school battle as last night's starting point.

contexts.japanese: 昨夜の事件—夜の学校でランサーとアーチャーの戦いを目撃してからこっち、まともに考える時間がなかった為だ。
contexts.english: Ever since last night, when I witnessed Lancer and Archer fighting at the school, I haven't had time to collect my thoughts.

counterexamples.description: The unknown first rescue remains unknown.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Something or someone saved Shirou after Lancer pierced his chest.
counterexamples.explanation: The unknown first rescue remains unknown.

contexts.japanese: その後、俺はランサーに胸を貫かれ、なんでか助かって家に戻り、再びランサーに襲われ—
contexts.english: After that, Lancer stabbed me through the chest, something or someone saved me and I went home, only to get attacked by Lancer again...

counterexamples.description: Shirou retains his count of three attacks.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The war feels unreal despite three enemy assaults.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou retains his count of three attacks.

contexts.japanese: そんな大事まったく実感が持てないが、俺はもう三度も敵に襲われている。
contexts.english: It all sounds fantastical and still not quite real, but I've already been attacked three times.

counterexamples.description: Helping someone like Kiritsugu remains the positive opportunity.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou sees a chance to be of use to others.
counterexamples.explanation: Helping someone like Kiritsugu remains the positive opportunity.

contexts.japanese: ずっと目指していたもの、衛宮切嗣のように『誰かの為』になれる機会。
contexts.english: It's a chance for me to fight for someone else's sake, just like I've always wanted. Just like Kiritsugu Emiya did.

counterexamples.description: Kirei's intrusive phrasing remains separated across the internal sequence.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Rejoice and the forbidden inverted wish interrupt Shirou's opportunity thought.
counterexamples.explanation: Kirei's intrusive phrasing remains separated across the internal sequence.

contexts.japanese: —喜べ衛宮士郎。
contexts.english: Rejoice, Shirou Emiya.

contexts.japanese: その、願ってはならないサカシマな願望が、
contexts.english: Your absurd, forbidden desire

contexts.japanese: —君の望みは、ようやく叶う。
contexts.english: will finally be granted.

counterexamples.description: Shirou denies wishing for the war.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He uses the denial to press down but not erase his doubt.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou denies wishing for the war.

contexts.japanese: 「—そんな事はない。聖杯戦争なんて、俺が望んだものじゃない」
contexts.english: "That can't be true. I never wanted this Holy Grail War to happen."

counterexamples.description: Saber's dojo stillness retains the clear-water image.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her upright seiza and silence appear beautiful and pure.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber's dojo stillness retains the clear-water image.

contexts.japanese: 凛と背筋を伸ばし、目を閉じて正座をするセイバーは、綺麗だった。
contexts.english: Saber looks beautiful. She strikes a refined, dignified figure as she sits there, eyes closed.

contexts.japanese: 静寂に溶け込む彼女の有り様は、清らかな水を思わせる。
contexts.english: Matching the stillness of the dojo, she reminds me of clear, pure water.

counterexamples.description: Saber as sacred moral reassurance remains Shirou's perception.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He thinks her presence means he will not take a wrong path.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber as sacred moral reassurance remains Shirou's perception.

contexts.japanese: サーヴァントだろうとなんだろうと、彼女は聖なるものだと思う。
contexts.english: Servant or whatever it is, she seems sacrosanct.

contexts.japanese: なら—この先、自分が間違った道を進む事はないだろう。
contexts.english: So... From now on, I'm sure I won't go down the wrong path.

counterexamples.description: Saber rests because she cannot heal Shirou.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She prepares her own body instead.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber rests because she cannot heal Shirou.

contexts.japanese: 「体を休めていました。私にはシロウの手当ては出来ませんから、今はせめて自身を万全にしておこうと思いまして」
contexts.english: "I was resting. Since I cannot treat you, I figured that I would at least ensure that my body is in as perfect a condition as I can make it."

counterexamples.description: Saber calmly prioritizes Master's survival over herself.
counterexamples.sourceReading: If she alone dies, Shirou need not have been hurt; he has no need to shield her.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber calmly prioritizes Master's survival over herself.

contexts.japanese: 「その時は私が死ぬだけでしょう。シロウが傷つく事ではなかった。
contexts.english: "Perhaps I would have died. But you would not have been hurt.

contexts.japanese: マスターである貴方が私を庇う必要はありませんし、そんな理由もないでしょう」
contexts.english: My Master need not defend me, nor is there any reason to do so."

counterexamples.description: Shirou's reflexive gendered rescue principle remains explicit.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He says no reason is needed to protect a girl.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's reflexive gendered rescue principle remains explicit.

contexts.japanese: 「な—バカ言ってんな、女の子を助けるのに理由なんているもんか……！」
contexts.english: "Wha... Don't be stupid! I don't need a reason to protect a girl!"

counterexamples.description: Shirou recognizes his remark as out of place.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber's dignity makes him retreat and feel embarrassed.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou recognizes his remark as out of place.

contexts.japanese: なんか、自分がすごく場違いな台詞を言ったな、と思い知らされて恥ずかしくなってしまった。
contexts.english: Now I just feel embarrassed, like I've said something incredibly tone-deaf.

counterexamples.description: Saber values thanks despite protection being duty.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She calls Shirou courteous; he denies it.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber values thanks despite protection being duty.

contexts.japanese: 「それはどうも。サーヴァントがマスターを守護するのは当たり前ですが、感謝をされるのは嬉しい。シロウは礼儀正しいのですね」
contexts.english: "You are most welcome. It is a Servant's duty to protect their Master, but it is still nice to be acknowledged. You are very courteous, Shirou."

contexts.japanese: 「いや。別に礼儀正しくなんかないぞ、俺」
contexts.english: "I don't think I'm particularly polite, actually."

counterexamples.description: Accidental summoning and chosen participation remain distinct.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou did not intentionally summon her but has intentionally decided to fight.
counterexamples.explanation: Accidental summoning and chosen participation remain distinct.

contexts.japanese: 「違う。俺がおまえを呼び出したのはただの偶然だ。
contexts.english: "No, actually. It was just a coincidence.

contexts.japanese: けど、戦うと決めたからには戦う。未熟なマスターだけど、セイバーはそれでいいのか」
contexts.english: But, now that I've decided to, I'll fight. I'm inexperienced as a Master, but are you okay with that?"

counterexamples.description: Saber cannot voluntarily betray her own code.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Harming the unarmed violates her knightly oath.
counterexamples.explanation: Saber cannot voluntarily betray her own code.

contexts.japanese: 私は私が許す行為しか出来ない。自分を裏切る事は、私には不可能です。剣を持たぬ人間に傷を負わせる事など、騎士の誓いに反します」
contexts.english: I can only do things I allow myself to. It is impossible for me to betray my own beliefs. Harming unarmed innocents goes against a knight's oath."

counterexamples.description: Both acknowledge the misunderstanding.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber admits jumping to conclusions and asks Shirou to raise his head.
counterexamples.explanation: Both acknowledge the misunderstanding.

contexts.japanese: 「ぁ……いえ、私もマスターの意図が掴めずに早合点してしまいました。シロウは悪くないのですから、顔をあげてくれませんか……？」
contexts.english: "Ah... No, I also failed to grasp your intentions and jumped to conclusions. You are not at fault, so may you please raise your head...?"

counterexamples.description: Close-combat superiority remains hypothetical.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Saber asks what Shirou would do against a better melee opponent.
counterexamples.explanation: Close-combat superiority remains hypothetical.

contexts.japanese: 例えばの話ですが、敵が自身より白兵戦で優れている場合、貴方ならどうしますか？」
contexts.english: This is hypothetical, but if your enemy is better at close combat than you, then what would you do?"

counterexamples.description: A Noble Phantasm trades identity exposure for a decisive blow.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Failure exposes weakness.
counterexamples.explanation: A Noble Phantasm trades identity exposure for a decisive blow.

contexts.japanese: 正体を明かすかわりに、避けきれぬ必殺の一撃を炸裂させる。
contexts.english: In exchange for revealing the identity, it would launch an unavoidable fatal blow.

contexts.japanese: だがそれが不発に終わった時—そのサーヴァントは、自らの欠点をもさらけ出す事になる。
contexts.english: And if that attack misses or fails, the Servant has revealed their weaknesses.

counterexamples.description: Mind-reading remains a hypothetical risk.
counterexamples.sourceReading: A superior mage might read inexperienced Shirou's thoughts.
counterexamples.explanation: Mind-reading remains a hypothetical risk.

contexts.japanese: 優れた魔術師ならば、シロウの思考を読む事も可能でしょう。ですから—」
contexts.english: If you encounter a superior mage, they should be able to read your mind. Therefore..."

counterexamples.description: Shirou delegates Noble Phantasm timing after considering the reason.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He denies the choice was thoughtless.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou delegates Noble Phantasm timing after considering the reason.

contexts.japanese: —よし、そうしよう。セイバーの“宝具”の使いどころは、セイバー自身の判断に任せる」
contexts.english: Okay then. I'll leave it up to you to decide when to use your Noble Phantasm."

contexts.japanese: 「あっさりじゃないぞ。ちゃんと考えて納得したんだ。
contexts.english: "It's not rash. I thought it over, and I'm satisfied by the conclusion I reached.

counterexamples.description: Rin remains the only known opponent and unwilling target.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou does not want to fight her though she appears ready.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin remains the only known opponent and unwilling target.

contexts.japanese: 戦うと決めたものの、判っている相手は遠坂だけで、俺はあいつとドンパチやる気はまったくない。
contexts.english: I decided to fight, yet the only opponent that I know of is Tohsaka, and I have no intention of fighting her at all.

contexts.japanese: ……ああいや、向こうはやる気満々だから、そうも言ってはいられないだろうが。
contexts.english: ...Well actually, she's ready to fight me, so I guess I'm not the one in a position to say that.

counterexamples.description: Two years near Rin demonstrate Shirou's poor mage detection.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He repeatedly saw her without recognizing her identity.
counterexamples.explanation: Two years near Rin demonstrate Shirou's poor mage detection.

contexts.japanese: そもそも同じ学校にいた遠坂の正体にも気づかなかったんだぞ、俺は。
contexts.english: I mean, I didn't even realize Tohsaka's identity, and we go to the same school.

contexts.japanese: 二年間も同じ建物にいて、あまつさえ何度も見かけているっていうのにだ。
contexts.english: We were in the same building for two years, and on top of that, I saw her many times.

counterexamples.description: The forehead point is Saber's fingertip, not a blade.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She instructs him to focus on it and sense mana.
counterexamples.explanation: The forehead point is Saber's fingertip, not a blade.

contexts.japanese: 「……。マスター、黙って私の指先に意識を集中してください。貴方も魔術師なら、それでこちらの魔力を感じ取れるでしょう」
contexts.english: "...Master, please be quiet and concentrate on my fingertip. If you are a mage, you should be able to feel my magical energy from that."

contexts.japanese: そうか、触れてるのはセイバーの指か。
contexts.english: Oh, so it's Saber's finger touching me.

counterexamples.description: The death memory remains placed five winters earlier under a beautiful moon.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The scene opens as a dated memory on a beautiful moonlit night.
counterexamples.explanation: The death memory remains placed five winters earlier under a beautiful moon.

contexts.japanese: それは、五年前の冬の話。
contexts.english: Winter, five years ago.

contexts.japanese: 月の綺麗な夜だった。
contexts.english: It was a beautiful, moonlit night.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's abandoned justice ideal remains surprising because Shirou sees him as its embodiment.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kiritsugu nostalgically says he once wanted to be a champion of justice.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's abandoned justice ideal remains surprising because Shirou sees him as its embodiment.

contexts.japanese: 「子供の頃、僕は正義の味方に憧れてた」
contexts.english: "When I was a boy, I wanted to be a champion of justice."

contexts.japanese: 自分から見たら正義の味方そのものの父は、懐かしむように、そんな事を呟いた。
contexts.english: My father, who already seemed like a champion of justice in my eyes, said that as if he were reflecting on a memory.

counterexamples.description: Heroism's adult time limit remains Kiritsugu's rueful explanation.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Kiritsugu says becoming an adult made the title difficult and wishes he had noticed sooner; the child trusts him.
counterexamples.explanation: Heroism's adult time limit remains Kiritsugu's rueful explanation.

contexts.japanese: 「うん、残念ながらね。ヒーローは期間限定で、オトナになると名乗るのが難しくなるんだ。そんなコト、もっと早くに気が付けば良かった」
contexts.english: "Unfortunately, yes. You can only be a hero for so long. It gets harder to call yourself one as you grow up. I wish I'd found that out earlier."

contexts.japanese: なんでそうなのかは分からなかったが、切嗣の言うことだから間違いないと思ったのだ。
contexts.english: I wasn't sure why, but if Kiritsugu said it, then it had to be true.

counterexamples.description: Young Shirou explicitly volunteers to realize Kiritsugu's dream.
counterexamples.sourceReading: The child says he will take over and make the dream real.
counterexamples.explanation: Young Shirou explicitly volunteers to realize Kiritsugu's dream.

contexts.japanese: 「うん、しょうがないから俺が代わりになってやるよ。
contexts.english: "Okay. If you can't do it, then I'll do it for you.

contexts.japanese: “—俺が、ちゃんと形にしてやるから”
contexts.english: Because I'll make it a reality.

counterexamples.description: Absence of felt sadness coexists with unstoppable tears.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou neither cries out nor thinks himself sad, yet tears continue until moonset.
counterexamples.explanation: Absence of felt sadness coexists with unstoppable tears.

contexts.japanese: 泣き声もあげず、悲しいと思う事もない。
contexts.english: I didn't cry out loud, nor did I feel sad.

contexts.japanese: 月が落ちるまで、ただ、涙だけが止まらなかった。
contexts.english: But tears flowed down my cheek until the moon sank past the horizon.

counterexamples.description: Kiritsugu's fire rescue keeps the joy of saving one dying child.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He lifts and carries the burned child out while weeping with joy.
counterexamples.explanation: Kiritsugu's fire rescue keeps the joy of saving one dying child.

contexts.japanese: 十年前、火事場に残されていた自分を救い出してくれた男の姿を。
contexts.english: Ten years ago, a man saved me from a fire.

contexts.japanese: 意識もなく、全身に火傷を負って死にかけていた子供を抱き上げて、目に涙をためるぐらい喜んで、外に連れ出してくれた。
contexts.english: He picked up a burned, dying child and carried him out of hell, weeping with joy.

counterexamples.description: The saved child and failed would-be savior remain grammatically distinct.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Nobody saved Shirou, Shirou could save nobody, then Kiritsugu alone saves him.
counterexamples.explanation: The saved child and failed would-be savior remain grammatically distinct.

contexts.japanese: 誰も助けてくれなかった。
contexts.english: Nobody else saved me.

contexts.japanese: 誰も助けてやれなかった。
contexts.english: I couldn't save anyone.

contexts.japanese: その中でただ一人助けられた自分と、ただ一人助けてくれた人がいた。
contexts.english: In the ruins of the fire, there was only a boy who was saved, and the man who saved him.

counterexamples.description: Shirou's childhood vow remains an obligation to save someone as he was saved.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He swears to become a hero of justice and fulfill the dream of the man he admired most.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's childhood vow remains an obligation to save someone as he was saved.

contexts.japanese: 衛宮士郎は正義の味方になって、かつての自分のような誰かを助けなくてはいけない。
contexts.english: Shirou Emiya must become a hero of justice and save someone the same way that he was once saved.

contexts.japanese: 幼い頃にそう誓った。
contexts.english: I swore to myself I would do it.

contexts.japanese: 誰よりも憧れたあの男の代わりに、彼の夢を果たすのだと。
contexts.english: I vowed to fulfill the dream of the man I most admired.

counterexamples.description: The unexplained bandage is noticed and deferred rather than rationalized.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou finds abdominal bandages and, having no explanation, puts the question aside.
counterexamples.explanation: The unexplained bandage is noticed and deferred rather than rationalized.

contexts.japanese: なぜか腹には包帯が巻かれていた。
contexts.english: For some reason, my abdomen is wrapped in bandages.

contexts.japanese: 思い当たる節がないので、とりあえず保留にしておく。
contexts.english: I have no idea why, but I'll deal with it later.

counterexamples.description: The quiet room is only compared with an ordinary Sunday, then immediately contradicted.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou momentarily frames the scene as Sunday-like before Rin's presence breaks it.
counterexamples.explanation: The quiet room is only compared with an ordinary Sunday, then immediately contradicted.

contexts.japanese: 静かな居間は、いつもの日曜日といった風景—
contexts.english: The living room's quiet, like a typical Sunday—

contexts.japanese: —なんかじゃねえ。
contexts.english: ...or not.

counterexamples.description: Rin correctly connects shielding a Servant with the Master's death ending the contract.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She scolds Shirou for protecting a Servant despite the Master's survival being necessary.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin correctly connects shielding a Servant with the Master's death ending the contract.

contexts.japanese: 「マスターが死んだらサーヴァントは消えるって言ったでしょう？　だっていうのにサーヴァントを庇うなんてどうかしてるわ」
contexts.english: "If the Master dies, the Servant disappears too, remember? I can't believe you actually tried to shield your own Servant."

counterexamples.description: Shirou distinguishes intent from his awareness that approaching Berserker could kill him.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He denies deliberately shielding Saber while admitting he expected lethal danger.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou distinguishes intent from his awareness that approaching Berserker could kill him.

contexts.japanese: 「庇った訳じゃない。助けようとしたらああなっちまっただけだ。俺だってあんな目にあうなんて思わなかった」
contexts.english: "I wasn't shielding her. I was just trying to get her out of there. I didn't think that would happen to me."

contexts.japanese: あんな怪物に近寄れば死ぬだろうな、ぐらいは考えてはいたが、それはそれだ。
contexts.english: I knew I might die if I got near a monster like that, but that's beside the point.

counterexamples.description: Rin's church intervention remains a survival measure rather than help toward victory.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She wanted an ignorant Shirou to have a chance to survive alone.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's church intervention remains a survival measure rather than help toward victory.

contexts.japanese: 「あのね衛宮くん。きっちりと言っておくけど、教会まで連れて行ったのは貴方に勝たせる為じゃないわ。
contexts.english: "I'll be straight with you, Emiya. I didn't take you to the church so that you could win.

contexts.japanese: あれはね、何も知らない貴方が一人でも生き残れるようにって考えた結果なの。どうも、そのあたりを解ってなかったみたいね」
contexts.english: I was just trying to give you a chance to survive because you literally don't know anything. It sounds like you still don't get it."

counterexamples.description: Rin explicitly admits a full night of worry.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her anger follows from Shirou making her worry all night.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin explicitly admits a full night of worry.

contexts.japanese: 「関係あるわよ、このわたしを一晩も心配させたんだから！」
contexts.english: "It has everything to do with me, because you made me worry all night long!"

counterexamples.description: Shirou's thanks also carry an apology.
counterexamples.sourceReading: He bows to Rin with gratitude and apology after learning what she did.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's thanks also carry an apology.

contexts.japanese: 「そうか。遠坂には世話になったんだな。ありがとう」
contexts.english: "Is that so? Guess I owe you one, Tohsaka. Thanks."

contexts.japanese: 感謝と謝罪をこめて頭をさげる。
contexts.english: I bow my head in appreciation and apology.

counterexamples.description: Rin explicitly credits Shirou's own power with completing the healing.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Her help did not replace the self-repair that actually closed the wound.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin explicitly credits Shirou's own power with completing the healing.

contexts.japanese: 「ここで重要なのは、貴方は貴方一人で生ききったっていう事実よ。確かにわたしは手助けしたけど、あの傷を完治させたのは貴方自身の力だった。そこ、勘違いしないでよね」
contexts.english: "What's important here is that you managed to survive on your own. I might have helped a bit, but it was your power that healed your wound. So, don't get that twisted, okay?"

contexts.japanese: 「話を聞くとそうみたいだけど。なんだ、遠坂が治してくれたんじゃないのか？」
contexts.english: "That's what it sounds like from the way you told it. So you aren't the one who healed me?"

counterexamples.description: The upstream-river analogy and Saber's exceptional power remain intact.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou supplies the image and Rin accepts it as normally impossible.
counterexamples.explanation: The upstream-river analogy and Saber's exceptional power remain intact.

contexts.japanese: 「……む。簡単に言って、川の水が下から上に流れているようなもんか？」
contexts.english: "Hm. So it's like a river flowing upstream?"

contexts.japanese: 「上手い喩えね。本来ならあり得ないだろうけど、セイバーの魔力ってのは川の流れを変えるほど膨大なんでしょう。そうでなければあの体格でバーサーカーとまともに打ち合うなんて考えられない」
contexts.english: "That's a good way of putting it. Normally, that wouldn't be possible, but Saber's magical energy must be powerful enough to change the flow of a river. Otherwise there's no chance she'd be able to go up against Berserker with that tiny frame of hers."

counterexamples.description: The bank-balance tangent remains a joke about magecraft consuming money.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou questions the example and Rin turns it into a personal grievance.
counterexamples.explanation: The bank-balance tangent remains a joke about magecraft consuming money.

contexts.japanese: 「遠坂。預金残高は関係ないのでは」
contexts.english: "Tohsaka. I don't think my bank account has anything to do with it."

contexts.japanese: 「関係あるわよ！　魔術ってのは金食い虫なんだから、使ってればどんどんどんどんお金は減っていくものなの！
contexts.english: "Of course it does! Using magecraft means you're pretty much throwing your money away. The more you use it, the more it drains your money!

contexts.japanese: そうでなければ許さないんだから、とくにわたしが！」
contexts.english: Otherwise none of this would be acceptable! Especially to me!"

counterexamples.description: Shirou distinguishes Rin's private self from her school persona.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Talking with her confirms that the present Rin feels genuine and school Rin formal.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou distinguishes Rin's private self from her school persona.

contexts.japanese: 話せば話すほど、こっちの遠坂が地で、学校での遠坂がよそ行きだと判ってしまう。
contexts.english: The more I talk to her, the more this Tohsaka feels like the real one, while the girl at school feels like an act.

contexts.japanese: ……ああ、いやまあ、そんなのは昨日の段階で判りきっていた事だったか。
contexts.english: ...Though, I guess I already noticed that yesterday.

counterexamples.description: Rin's direct planning question remains the one Shirou least wants.
counterexamples.sourceReading: She frankly asks his next move and he recognizes the pressure point.
counterexamples.explanation: Rin's direct planning question remains the one Shirou least wants.

contexts.japanese: 「じゃあ率直に訊くけど。衛宮くん、貴方これからどうするつもり？」
contexts.english: "Then I'll be frank. What do you plan to do next?"

counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's lack of Grail interest remains separate from his reluctance to risk his life for it.

contexts.english: I don't really know if I can risk my life for something I don't want."

counterexamples.description: Master reconciliation does not remove Servants' competing wishes.
counterexamples.sourceReading: Shirou realizes Saber too may fight, kill and be killed for the Grail.
counterexamples.explanation: Master reconciliation does not remove Servants' competing wishes.

contexts.english: That means that Servants must fight and kill each other.

contexts.japanese: マスター同士で和解して、お互いに聖杯を諦めれば話は済むと思っていたけれど、サーヴァントが聖杯を求めて召喚に応じて現れたモノで、けして聖杯を諦めないのならば、それじゃあ結局、サーヴァント同士の戦いは避けられない。
contexts.english: I thought it would've been enough as long as the Masters made peace with each other and gave up the Holy Grail. But if Servants answer the summons because they also seek the Holy Grail and will never give up until they have it, then battle between Servants really is inevitable.

contexts.japanese: 自分を守るために戦い抜いてくれたあの少女も、聖杯を巡って争い、殺し、殺される立場だというのか。
contexts.english: ...is the girl who fought so hard to protect me also here to fight, kill for, and maybe die...all for the Holy Grail?

counterexamples.description: Return after Servant death does not erase Shirou's objection to a human-shaped death.

counterexamples.explanation: Return after Servant death does not erase Shirou's objection to a human-shaped death.

contexts.english: "Oh, don't worry about that. Servants aren't mortal, so if they die, they'll just go back to where they came from. Heroic Spirits are phenomena that can't die. Only Masters can actually get killed when they lose a fight."

contexts.japanese: たとえ仮初めの死だとしても。
contexts.english: Even if their deaths are figurative...

contexts.japanese: この世界で、人の姿をしたモノが息絶えるという事に変わりはない。
contexts.english: It doesn't change the fact that something which takes the form of a human dies in this world.

counterexamples.description: Shirou accepts death's proximity to magecraft but rejects judging human life and death.
counterexamples.sourceReading: His limitation is moral and personal, not ignorance of lethal risk.
counterexamples.explanation: Shirou accepts death's proximity to magecraft but rejects judging human life and death.

contexts.japanese: 遠坂の言うことはもっともだ。
contexts.english: Tohsaka's right.

contexts.japanese: 魔術師である以上、死は身近に存在する。
contexts.english: As a mage, death is never far.

contexts.japanese: そんな事はとっくに覚悟しているし、理解している。

contexts.japanese: それでも俺は—人の生き死にに善悪を計れるほど強くはない。
contexts.english: But I'm not strong enough to be the judge of when and where other people should live or die.

counterexamples.description: Shirou distinguishes initiating killing from ruthless self-defense.

counterexamples.explanation: Shirou distinguishes initiating killing from ruthless self-defense.

contexts.english: "That's not my point. All I have to do is to stay alive until the end, right? I don't intend to kill anyone, but I'm also not going to hold back if I need to defend myself.

contexts.japanese: ……人を殺しに来る相手なら、逆に殺されても文句は言えないだろ」
contexts.english: ...Someone who shows up ready to kill others can't complain about getting killed."

counterexamples.description: Rin tests Shirou with a hypothetical city massacre rather than reporting one.

counterexamples.explanation: Rin tests Shirou with a hypothetical city massacre rather than reporting one.

contexts.english: "Hm. So you're going to play defense. You're just going to watch and see what the other Masters do? Even if that thing from yesterday goes around killing everyone in town, you'll just ignore it?"

counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's mass-killing question and Rin's qualified response remain hypothetical.

contexts.japanese: 「そうね。けど頭のいいヤツならそんな無駄な事はしないんじゃないかな」
contexts.english: "Maybe. But I can't see a smart Master doing something like that."

counterexamples.explanation: Rin exposes the contradiction in Shirou's reactive justice policy.

contexts.english: "We're getting off topic. So, what's next for you?

contexts.japanese: 「そうなったら止めるだけだ。サーヴァントさえ倒せば、マスターだって大人しくなるんだろう」

contexts.japanese: 衛宮くん、自分が矛盾してるって解ってる？」

contexts.japanese: 忘れるもんか。帰り道、問答無用で襲いかかってきた相手なんだから。
contexts.english: How can I forget? She attacked us on our way home without any warning.

counterexamples.explanation: Shirou independently accepts he probably will not survive another Berserker attack.

contexts.english: "...That goes for me, too. I'm pretty sure I won't survive the next round with that thing."

counterexamples.explanation: Rin's offer is explicitly an alliance, not a surrender or settled agreement.

contexts.japanese: もう、ここまで言ってるのに分からない？　ようするに、わたしと手を組まないかって言ってるの」

counterexamples.explanation: Shirou's desire to avoid fighting Rin remains one reason the offer appeals.
